title: [Bug] Non cacheline aligned arena allocations
author: jlombera

comments.body:
Hello 👋
Ah yes you're absolutely right, AFAIK `malloc` and friends will return 8 byte aligned on modern systems so at least that case is covered, but it makes sense for us to consider a misaligned initial provided `memory` pointer as part of both the min memory size and setting the initial `nextAllocation` offset, rather than leaving it as zero.
Should be a quick and easy fix, I will put it in tomorrow 👍

> AFAIK `malloc` and friends will return 8 byte aligned on modern systems so at least that case is covered, but it makes sense for us to consider a misaligned initial provided `memory` pointer [...]

The code tries to align to cacheline, i.e. 64 bytes instead of 8.  So even when memory comes from `malloc(3)` it's not guarantee it'll be cacheline aligned.


> [...] and setting the initial nextAllocation offset, rather than leaving it as zero.

Just setting `nextAllocation` initially won't help.  Next time the offset is computed solely based on the value of `nextAllocation` (as in `(1)` above), it'll result in a misaligned address (because `memory` is still misaligned).

You have to either:
a) Adjust `memory` so that it's aligned.  Afterwards it will be safe to compute the offset based only on the value of `nextAllocation`.  Or

b) Take into account both `nextAllocation` and `memory` alignment when an offset is computed.  E.g. (I haven't double checked the correctness of the computation):
```c
offset = nextAllocation + (64 - ((memory + nextAllocation) % 64));

return (memory + offset);
```

Yes you're right! I've aligned the base `memory` pointer to 64 here:
https://github.com/nicbarker/clay/commit/b9e27178c0aee15ff77351335b2643eca2423502
Let me know what you think!
It looks good.  I would have done that `memory` adjustment when the arena is created, though (e.g. in `Clay_CreateArenaWithCapacityAndMemory()`), but that's me 😃

@jlombera while that would normally be very sensible, I've seen people constructing the arena struct by hand and passing it in rather than calling `CreateArenaWithCapacityAndMemory`, so I thought I might try to catch those cases as well 🙂

I see, that makes sense.  Personally, I would be less lenient: "It's the user's problem if they don't use the API as intended" 😉.

But looking into the examples, it seems the only use the user has of `Clay_Arena` is to pass it to `Clay_Initialize()`.  So I was wondering, why not make the arena an internal definition instead?  `Clay_Initialize()` might instead receive just the pointer to the memory and length.  The proper arena creation and initialization (e.g. address alignment) would be done internally.  I see some benefits doing this:
- Makes the API a little simpler, with one less concept the user has to think about.
- You ensure the arena is properly initialized internally, without user intervention.
- You don't expose the arena, removing the chances of user messing with it (even if by mistake).
- The API feels less "verbose".  To me, as a user, having to construct an API object, just to pass it to another API function and never touch it again always evokes the reaction: "why don't you construct it yourself internally? why do I have to litter my code with these repetitive definitions that have no use from my side?" (The exception to this is when memory allocation is required.  I want to have control of memory allocation.  I rather the API ask me to construct the object myself than it allocating memory from the heap (`malloc(3)`) internally.  I _do_ like that Clay asks for the memory to be used internally)

I'd say I agree with most of the points there, the API grew organically and it feels like a little bit of ceremony now (4 functions or something just to get things "initialized") so it could definitely be time for a cleanup 🙂

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that ensures all arena allocations are properly aligned to cacheline boundaries (64 bytes) regardless of the initial memory pointer alignment
The alignment correction must account for the relationship between the base memory pointer and allocation offsets, not just one or the other
The solution must handle cases where users provide their own memory pointer to the arena, including potentially misaligned pointers

author: brutaldev

comments.body: OK I think I see what the issue is. I was trying to map the internal port (9401) to 6382 instead of using `-p 6382` so that it binds to that port internally instead. This works but only if combined with `--net=host` and not when using it with another network such as in a compose file. To use that you also need to explicitly enable this in Docker Desktop which was disabled by default: So I can get it working, but it's not ideal because other containers cannot access it within their own network because it doesn't seem to work without `--net=host` internally in the container environment or from the host machine. Any idea how I can get this work from a compose file like this? ``` networks: test-internal: name: test-network services: dragonfly: container_name: dragonfly image: docker.dragonflydb.io/dragonflydb/dragonfly:latest restart: unless-stopped command: ["--cache_mode=true", "--proactor_threads=1"] ulimits: memlock: -1 ports: - 6380:6379 networks: - test-internal garnet: container_name: garnet image: ghcr.io/microsoft/garnet:latest restart: unless-stopped ulimits: memlock: -1 ports: - 6381:6379 networks: - test-internal pogocache: container_name: pogocache image: pogocache/pogocache:latest command: ["-p", "6382"] restart: unless-stopped #network_mode: host - cannot use this "service pogocache declares mutually exclusive `network_mode` and `networks`: invalid compose project" networks: - test-internal ``` I've used working Dragonfly and Garnet here as well which just use port mapping and as accessible by the host and other containers in the `test-internal` network.

For security, Pogocache bind to loopback (127.0.0.1:9401) by default. 
I may be wrong, but `--net=host` is required when connecting to 127.0.0.1.

I think the workaround is to bind Pogocache to `-h 0.0.0.0`.

```
sudo docker run -p 6382:9401 pogocache/pogocache -h 0.0.0.0
```

This should open up the 9401 to the full IP range.

Perfect!
In my scenario that's not a problem since it would run within a private virtual network (like as a pod in Kubernetes) and never exposed to the internet, only internal services that require a cache facility.

For anyone else trying this, here's the docker compose for that command.
```
  pogocache:
    container_name: pogocache
    image: pogocache/pogocache:latest
    command: ["-h", "0.0.0.0"]
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - 6382:9401
    networks:
      - test-internal
```

Thanks @tidwall, this allows us to evaluate Pogocache as an alternative to Redis (of which we've gone with Garnet in the past and settled on Dragonfly because has better command support). Always on the lookout for faster alternatives and Pogocache looks amazing in that respect!

title: CAS is not working (or I'm doing something wrong)
body:
I'm trying to figure out how to avoid race conditions when working with the same key in multiple threads (the end goal is to implement query on top of pogocache). I've read about CAS in Memcached, so I'm trying to use it. Simplest example that I came up with: 1) two threads 2) each thread reads value with **gets**; 3) each tries to update value with **cas**; 4) if update fails - wait some time and try to read and update again.

```python
import memcache 
import threading
import time

SERVER_URL = 'pogocache:9401'
#SERVER_URL = 'memcached:11211'

def worker(worker_id):
    mc = memcache.Client([SERVER_URL], debug=1, cache_cas=True)

    def increment():
        value = mc.gets('counter')
        print(f"Worker {worker_id} gets: {value=}")
        value = int(value) + 1
        cas_result = mc.cas('counter', str(value))
        print(f"Worker {worker_id} cas: {cas_result=}")
        return cas_result
    
    if increment() is False:
        time.sleep(0.1)
        increment()


if __name__ =="__main__":
    mc = memcache.Client([SERVER_URL], debug=1, cache_cas=True)
    mc.delete('counter')
    mc.add('counter', '0')

    t1 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(1,))
    t2 = threading.Thread(target=worker, args=(2,))

    t1.start()
    t2.start()

    t1.join()
    t2.join()

    print(mc.get('counter'))
```

**What I expect**:
In the end counter is equal to 2 every time
**What actually happens**
Half of the time counter is equal to 1 (race condition)

title: PSRAM not detected on ESP32-S3-N16R8
body:
PSRAM is not detected on ESP32-S3-N16R8 and returned as 0.

On this ESP32-S3 module, PSRAM is Octal SPI not Quad SPI interface maybe this is why it isn't detected.
Don't know if this as any impact on ESP32-Bus-Pirate behaviour.
One thing to note, GPIO35, 36, 37 are not available as they are connected to the PSRAM
author: fdufnews

comments.body:
It's normal that you don't see the PSRAM, the core doesn't support it. 
Even if you have some on your board, it won't be recognized and isn't used for the firmware.

I've added PSRAM log in the memory infos with the others just in case for future versions.
OK, understand it.

title: Bug at SUBGHZ bruteforce
body: I discovered a potential issue with the bruteforce command in SUBGHZ mode. After running bruteforce and stopping it with the Enter key, the transmitter remains active across the entire band, as shown in the attached screenshot. The only way to stop the transmission is to power-cycle the board. Neither a system reboot nor pressing the onboard RST button resolves the problem. Upon reviewing Bruce firmware (from which SUBGHZ mode was adapted), I noticed a call to the deinitRfModule() function after stopping bruteforce. This function sets the CS pin to HIGH and the GDO0 pin to LOW. It seems this step might be missing in the ESP32-Bus-Pirate implementation of SUBGHZ bruteforce, which could explain the persistent transmission.
author: pecaxxl

Anyway, thank you for this great tool !

I also checked the behavior of the jam command on a single frequency, and it behaves the same way. I may have found another bug in the jam command. This should be handled by the new fix I already added, the frequency is set beforehand, and setTX no longer takes an argument so it just sets the CC1101 state without reapplying the frequency

author: nico0481

comments.body:
When using Dev Kit board rev1, the LED GPIO is 48, but that has changed to 38 for rev 1.1.
This can be changed recompiling from source code modifing the corresponding line in your board definition


` ; --- LED ---
  -DLED_DATA_PIN=48
  -DLED_CLOCK_PIN=39
`

@geo-tp can we add a separate definition for the 2 board revisions?

It's normal not to be able to change pins in LED mode, FastLED (the lib used for the 50 LED protocols) needs the pins at compile time, the usecase here is rather to operate external LEDs connected to the defined GPIO rather than the builtin LED of the esp32s3 devkit.


However I can adjust the pins, 38/39 for example but it cannot be modified on the fly in the firmware

I got it.

Using pin to control external RGB is indeed the best option.
I was just wondering how I couldn't manage to change the pin.

title: Remove float in sprite logic
body:
In `sprite_object_update()` there is a variable `epsilon` that is the result of `float2fx` which uses the **_dreaded_** software floating point: 

```c
INLINE FIXED float2fx(float f)
{	return (FIXED)(f*FIX_SCALEF);	}
```

The declaration of the `epsilon` variable _seems_ to be re-made every update loop call, as it is not a `static` variable:

```c
const FIXED epsilon = float2fx(0.01f);
```

There are also uses of `float2fx` in some code below, and that definitely gets calculated per frame:

```c
    sprite_object->vscale = float2fx(0.3f);
    sprite_object->vrotation = float2fx(8.0f); // Rotate the card when it's scored
```

The easiest solution to this would be to calculate the result of `float2fx(foo)` and save it as a macro.
author: ricfehr3

comments.body: I thought the compiler optimizes this because these are constants but I could be wrong? I think it's worth double checking the compiled assembly.

> I thought the compiler optimizes this because these are constants but I could be wrong? I think it's worth double checking the compiled assembly.

You're totally right.

This code in c:

```c
void sprite_object_shake(SpriteObject* sprite_object, mm_word sound_id)
{
    sprite_object->vscale = float2fx(0.3f);
    sprite_object->vrotation = float2fx(8.0f); // Rotate the card when it's scored

    if (sound_id == UNDEFINED)
        return; // If no sound ID is provided, do nothing

    play_sfx(sound_id, MM_BASE_PITCH_RATE, SFX_DEFAULT_VOLUME);
}

```

Looks like this (`arm-none-eabi-objdump -d build/sprite.o`):
 
```asm
000004dc <sprite_object_shake>:
 4dc:   224c            movs    r2, #76 @ 0x4c
 4de:   2380            movs    r3, #128        @ 0x80
 4e0:   b510            push    {r4, lr}
 4e2:   6242            str     r2, [r0, #36]   @ 0x24
 4e4:   011a            lsls    r2, r3, #4
 4e6:   6302            str     r2, [r0, #48]   @ 0x30
 4e8:   1c4a            adds    r2, r1, #1
 4ea:   d005            beq.n   4f8 <sprite_object_shake+0x1c>
 4ec:   0008            movs    r0, r1
 4ee:   2180            movs    r1, #128        @ 0x80
 4f0:   22ff            movs    r2, #255        @ 0xff
 4f2:   00c9            lsls    r1, r1, #3
 4f4:   f7ff fffe       bl      0 <play_sfx>
 4f8:   bc10            pop     {r4}
 4fa:   bc01            pop     {r0}
 4fc:   4700            bx      r0
 4fe:   46c0            nop                     @ (mov r8, r8)
```

I tested and found:
```
float2fx(0.3) = 76
float2fx(8.0) = 2048
```

And you can see the constants moving:
```asm
...
 4dc:   224c            movs    r2, #76  @ 0x4c <---- #76 is float2fx(0.3)
 4de:   2380            movs    r3, #128 @ 0x80 <---- first 128 is loaded into register 3
...
 4e4:   011a            lsls    r2, r3, #4      <---- r3(128) is shifted left by 4 and saved in r2 (making 2048)
...
```

Closing this, thanks for pointing that out.

satisfaction_conditions: Verification that the compiler already optimizes constant floating-point conversions
Evidence from compiled assembly code showing the actual runtime behavior

title: Add a C standard to the makefile
body:
I never noticed we don't have a standard in the makefile, I think it makes sense to add one so the project is explicit about which one it conforms to make sure the compiler doesn't default to a standard we don't support. 
My gut feeling tells me to have the latest so we support all the latest features and conform to the latest practices.
However, we need to also make sure the libraries we're using (namely tonc) conforms to the standard and that the standard is supported by the arm GCC compiler we're using.

#define __STDC_VERSION__ 202311L
```

Thanks!

Adding the flag `-std=c23` generates the following errors.

```
C:/devkitPro/libtonc/include/tonc_tte.h:472:20: error: implicit declaration of function 'iprintf'; did you mean 'sprintf'? [-Wimplicit-function-declaration]
  472 | #define tte_printf iprintf

      |                               ^~~~~~
      |                               rand
```

I did wonder about the usage of `random()` instead of `rand()`, however the `iprintf()` error is from tonc and we can't (or at least shouldn't) override it.

From https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/Standards.html:

_By default, GCC provides some extensions to the C language that, on rare occasions conflict with the C standard. See [Extensions to the C Language Family](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/C-Extensions.html). Some features that are part of the C99 standard are accepted as extensions in C90 mode, and some features that are part of the C11 standard are accepted as extensions in C90 and C99 modes. Use of the -std options listed above disables these extensions where they conflict with the C standard version selected. You may also select an extended version of the C language explicitly with -std=gnu90 (for C90 with GNU extensions), -std=gnu99 (for C99 with GNU extensions), -std=gnu11 (for C11 with GNU extensions), -std=gnu17 (for C17 with GNU extensions) or -std=gnu23 (for C23 with GNU extensions)._

**_The default, if no C language dialect options are given, is -std=gnu23_**.

title: Discover Contacts - only works while connected to App
body:
I disabled „auto add contacts“ - i want to add them manually.

The list „discover contacts“ is only collecting new contacts while i am connected via the App.

If i leave the companion alone (disconnected) - new adverted contacts will not be added to the „discover contacts“ list.

Is this behaviour wanted? Or is it a bug?

I thought if i get home from work, i can connect to my companion and see in the „discover contacts“ list, if there were new contacts adverted. But the list is only growing while my mobile is connected.
author: dreimal8

comments.body:
Howdy, this is correct behavior.

The "discover contacts" list in the app is a database maintained entirely by the app. The firmware doesn't know anything about it.
It can only be updated if the app is listening to incoming adverts. If the app is disconnected, it can't receive these adverts.

The firmware only stores the auto or manual added contacts in flash, and the app syncs this over when it connects.
Since these devices have limited resources, storing the discover list on them isn't feasible.

The app is able to store thousands of discovered contacts, since it's in the app only.
But the firmware only stores about 350 added contacts.

I'll close this one out, since it's expected behavior, and we can't do too much about this :)
Thank you very much for the explanation!

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of whether the observed behavior is intentional design or a defect
Technical explanation of the architectural constraints that determine the system's behavior
Information about the data persistence model and synchronization behavior between the companion device and mobile app

таблицы имеются:

--- table(localnets), set(0) ---
10.12.0.0/24 0

проверяю curl на этом же хосте:
`curl -4 -A Mozilla -m 5 -k --interface 192.168.12.109 --tls-max 1.2 --tlsv1.2 -v https://www.ledger.com/`

Стратегия одна из найденных блокчеком.
Теперь к сути. 
Если запускать dvtws2 без листов, или с ipset листом
```
### No hostlist-exclude:
/usr/local/sbin/dvtws2 --debug=1 --port=1999 --lua-init=@/usr/local/etc/zapret2/lua/zapret-lib.lua --lua-init=@/usr/local/etc/zapret2/lua/zapret-antidpi.lua --comment=General_HTTPS --filter-l3=ipv4 --filter-tcp=443 --ipset=/usr/local/etc/zapret2/ipset-cloudflare.txt --payload=tls_client_hello --lua-desync=fake:blob=fake_default_tls:tcp_md5:repeats=1 --payload=empty --out-range="<s1" --lua-desync=send:tcp_md5
```
то все работает. курл проламывается, получает полный ответ. (вообще без дурения - обрезанный, как водится ~16kb)

Если запускать с --hostlist-exclude
```
### With hostlist-exclude:
/usr/local/sbin/dvtws2 --debug=1 --port=1999 --lua-init=@/usr/local/etc/zapret2/lua/zapret-lib.lua --lua-init=@/usr/local/etc/zapret2/lua/zapret-antidpi.lua --comment=General_HTTPS --filter-l3=ipv4 --filter-tcp=443 --hostlist-exclude=/usr/local/etc/zapret2/list-exclude.txt --ipset=/usr/local/etc/zapret2/ipset-cloudflare.txt --payload=tls_client_hello --lua-desync=fake:blob=fake_default_tls:tcp_md5:repeats=1 --payload=empty --out-range="<s1" --lua-desync=send:tcp_md5
```
то не работает. Курл отваливается через 5 секунд (-m 5). При этом в логе dvtws2 еще минут 10 продолжают капать пакеты, по 1 в минуту примерно. Возможно ретрансмитит сама операционка, потому что можно и dvtws2 убить, запустить заново, а пакеты продолжаю капать.
Такой-же эффект дает подключение --hostlist.
И что еще страннее, такой-же эффект если даже без всяких листов просто добавить --filter-l7=tls.

логи dvtws2.

[dvtws2_ipset_only.log](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24536088/dvtws2_ipset_only.log)

Как только туда попадает  домен - поведение становится как и при остальных хостлистах, курл получает таймаут не получив данных.

решил покопать различия реализации **lua_newstate** в классике и в jit'е
вот что интересное нашел:

А вот в jit'е сначала инициализируется псевдорандом, и потом уже основная туша.  
Ну то есть дергает seed из системы, чтобы не работать с фиксированным значением. Переключение на фиксированное значение идет через флаг **LUAJIT_SECURITY_PRNG** (если проблема в этом)

2. В классике аллокация по умолчанию через realloc происходит. 
В жите - нет. Там сразу mmap дергается по умолчанию (это поведение отключается флагом **LUAJIT_USE_SYSMALLOC**, чтоб realloc использовать)
https://github.com/LuaJIT/LuaJIT/blob/7152e15489d2077cd299ee23e3d51a4c599ab14f/src/lj_state.c#L259

title: Potential Timing Oracle in Basic Auth
body:
Very cool project! I love the structure of the source and the whole vibe of it.

I noticed a potential security bug, likely low risk [2]:

https://github.com/ashtonjamesd/lavandula/blob/3333c76da6fdc14e81e1c6cd830bb079550ff5bf/src/auth.c#L61

Depending on the implementation [1], `strcmp()` might (not not!) compare one byte at a time, creating a very small but statistically detectable difference in request handling time between having ex. zero correct password bytes, and one first correct password byte. Over many requests, one can then use this timing difference to guess the password one/a few bytes at a time.

Still, I've seen papers demonstrate timing attacks on nanosecond delays, and "implementation dependent security risk" makes me uneasy. What I would suggest is just hashing both sides of the strcmp() beforehand, with some kind of cryptographic hash function. 

Hope this is helpful! And very cool project!!

[1] https://www.sjoerdlangkemper.nl/2024/05/29/string-comparison-timing-attacks/

[2] I looked for a security / disclosure policy, but couldn't find any. I decided the transparency about memory issues was a sufficient "don't actually use this yet" marker to just make a bug report for this kind of low risk thing. Please let me know if you disagree.
author: so-rose

comments.body:
Thanks!

I have replaced it with a constant-time string comparison function to remove the potential vulnerability.

And thank you again for catching this :)

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that eliminates timing-based information leakage in password comparison

title: Arabic glyph advances are sometimes incorrect
body:
Using the [attached sample program](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21024400/kb-shape.txt) (adapted from the README file, produces output similar to `hb-shape` for easy comparison) and [`Amiri-Regular.ttf`](https://github.com/aliftype/amiri/blob/main/fonts/Amiri-Regular.ttf):

```
$ ./kb-shape Amiri-Regular.ttf ىرى
[89+764|2037+364|2016+176]
$ hb-shape --no-clusters --no-glyph-names Amiri-Regular.ttf ىرى
[89+764|2037+299|2016+176]
```

The middle glyph (GID 2037) has an advance of 299 font units in HarfBuzz, while `kb_text_shape.h` gives 364 font units.

If I remove the last character from the string, both give the same glyph advances:
```
$ ./kb-shape Amiri-Regular.ttf ىر
[2037+299|2016+176]
$ hb-shape --no-clusters --no-glyph-names Amiri-Regular.ttf ىر
[2037+299|2016+176]
```
author: khaledhosny

comments.body:
Even adding replacing the third character with space triggers the issue:
```
$ cc ./kb-shape Amiri-Regular.ttf 'ىر '
[1+292|2037+364|2016+176]
$ hb-shape --no-clusters --no-glyph-names Amiri-Regular.ttf 'ىر '
[1+292|2037+299|2016+176]
```

We are applying a GPOS pair adjustment when we shouldn't.
Microsoft says:

> PairPosFormat2 requires that each glyph in all pairs be assigned to a class, which is identified by an integer called a class value.

It seems this is just incorrect? As far as I can see, if the second glyph in the pair is not defined in the class definition table, then the lookup is indeed canceled, but if the first glyph in the pair is not defined, then it's fine and we just give it class 0?

---

Fixed in https://github.com/JimmyLefevre/kb/commit/bf6071cf7ac4d80881b77b2bb3550d4cb4767784 , although I am open to readjusting the current behavior if my interpretation is incorrect.

Here is another issue, I’m not sure if it is related or not:
```
$ hb-shape --no-clusters --no-glyph-names Amiri-Regular.ttf "ـىريـ"
[5477+185|1604+190|2859@122,0+413|2838+258|5477+185]
$ ./kb-shape Amiri-Regular.ttf "ـىريـ"
[5477+185|1604+190|2859@105,0+332|2838+258|5477+185]
```

Both the x offset and advance of the middle glyph seem off. 

---

> We are applying a GPOS pair adjustment when we shouldn't. Microsoft says:
> 
> > PairPosFormat2 requires that each glyph in all pairs be assigned to a class, which is identified by an integer called a class value.
> 
> It seems this is just incorrect? As far as I can see, if the second glyph in the pair is not defined in the class definition table, then the lookup is indeed canceled, but if the first glyph in the pair is not defined, then it's fine and we just give it class 0?

My reading of HarfBuzz code is that it skips the pair of either glyph is not in the respective class definition table.

> Here is another issue, I’m not sure if it is related or not:
> 
> ```
> $ hb-shape --no-clusters --no-glyph-names Amiri-Regular.ttf "ـىريـ"
> [5477+185|1604+190|2859@122,0+413|2838+258|5477+185]
> $ ./kb-shape Amiri-Regular.ttf "ـىريـ"
> [5477+185|1604+190|2859@105,0+332|2838+258|5477+185]
> ```
> 
> Both the x offset and advance of the middle glyph seem off.

You are right.
Turns out it wasn't related, but the issue still happened in pair positioning, which is one of the lookup types I have the fewest tests for.
This is very helpful, thank you =)

https://github.com/JimmyLefevre/kb/commit/7e0f0f678ae2ec63f1acd878622a6c8ffa9f934b

BTW, while testing this I tried to disable kern feature to rule-out kerning issue, but it seems that it is not possible to disable GPOS features at all.

title: docs: Some suggestions to "On-Disk Storage"
body:
In https://lite3.io/design_and_limitations.html#autotoc_md41 some parts may benefit from some detai:

> This is dangerous, because if the system crashes while syncing data to disk, the structure can end up in a corrupt intermediate state. The most reliable atomic pattern is to write your new data to a temporary file, flush and sync it to disk, then use the `rename()` syscall to replace the target file. On Linux, `rename()` is atomic at the filesystem level.

If you want durability (which you do seem to want given that you talk about "sync it to disk"), you need to both `fsync` file and `fsync` the parent directory, otherwise your `fsync`ed inode will be somewhere on the disk but your `rename()` may not have been durably persisted.

> ### `mmap()`
>
> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling `fsync()`

Should that be `msync()`?

> Even when calling `fsync()` manually, you rely on the OS to sync changes to disk.

Not sure I understand. You rely on the OS implementing your `*sync()` operation of course, and it makes sense to rely on it (just as much as `fsync` for files).

Maybe the sentence should be

> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling `msync()`, a crash during it could leave your data ..."
author: nh2

comments.body:
Atomically changing the contents of a file on Linux indeed turns out to require more steps than I naively assumed. I now changed the text to the following:
> > direct file I/O
> 
> This is dangerous, because if the system crashes while syncing data to disk, the structure can end up in a corrupt intermediate state. To atomically update the contents of a file on Linux, a very specific sequence of steps is required. If not followed exactly, data could be at risk during a crash or power-out event.
> 
> The steps are as follows:
> 1. create a new temporary file (on the same file system!)
> 2. write data to the temporary file
> 3. fsync() the temporary file
> 4. rename the temporary file to the appropriate name (using the `rename()` syscall)
> 5. fsync() the containing directory
> 
> For more information, see: [https://lwn.net/Articles/457667](https://lwn.net/Articles/457667)

Then to address your other comment:

> Maybe the sentence should be
>> Write-maps do not have built-in atomicity. Even when calling msync(), a crash during it could leave your data ..."

Yes, thank you for pointing that out. This has now also been updated in the docs page.

satisfaction_conditions: Documentation must accurately describe the complete sequence of operations required for atomic file updates on Linux, including both file and directory synchronization
Documentation must use the correct system call terminology when discussing memory-mapped file synchronization
Documentation must clarify the relationship between synchronization operations and crash safety for memory-mapped files
Documentation must provide authoritative external references for complex durability guarantees

title: VGA Connection
body:
Hello,

I want to solder half of a VGA cable to the Pico and I found this website for the VGA connector pins:

[VGA Connector Pins](https://pc-anwender.de/Blog/Blog-2010/04-07-vga-anschluss-pinbelegung.htm)

It is in german but I hope it is understandable (Masse in german means Ground). In my case I have pins 1-3 for RGB, 4 and 5 not connected, 6-8 GND (soldered together in the connector I assume), 9 not connected but should be for 5V according to the above website, 10 ground for vertical synchronisation, 11 not connected, 12 for SDA, 13 for HSYNC, 14 for VSYNC, 15 for SCL. Is this correct? 

Is there no 5V connection between the Pico and the VGA device? VGA 5 should be the ground for the horizontal synchronisation but it is not connected to a wire in my case. I have only eight coloured wires plus one non-isolated ground wire.

If I understood your description right, I should just connect GND to VGA 6 (7 or 8), HSYNC with 68 ohms (I don’t have 66, but should be ok - or it is better to take a lower value? - I have 47 ohms) to VGA 13, VSYNC with 68 ohms to VGA 14 and Video Out to VGA 1-3 (connect all of them together). I also assume that I have to connect VGA 5 and VGA 10 with ground too, right?

Thanks 
Martin
author: Martius108

comments.body:
Hello!
Just connect as many grounds as you have available (as many of 5-8,10 as are wired) all together to the nearest Pico Gnd. Maybe they’ve cheaped out and made the shield connect to all the ground pins? Anyway likely not critical as long as “some” are connected. :)
Then RGB 1-3 together, HS 13, VS 14, to the corresponding resistors. And then, don’t worry about any of the other pins (no I2C, no 5V). Your resistor values sound just fine, 68 will do. (If it doesn’t, try lower, but am pretty sure it’ll be fine.)
Viel Glück!
Works great! Thank you.

Hello, I also encountered a similar VGA problem
I set up and tested it at the beginning, I can work normally
Then I found the Universal Board to welded the components. I confirmed that my VGA 1-3 link was connected to the PICO 18 pins of PICO with 100Ω.
VGA 13 pin connect a 66Ω resistor (I get an approximate resistance value through two resistors) connected to the 21 pin of Pico
VGA 14 pin connect 66Ω resistance to the 19 pin of Pico
VGA's 5,6,7,8,10 pin I connect to the GND of Pico (the pin between 19 and 21)
Then he was strange that he didn't work!

title: Virtual Monitor Seems to Replace First Monitor
body:
I have three screens, the laptop (eDP-1-1) on the left and two external monitors (DP-1-2-2 and DP-1-3-2) to the right.  I'm using xmonad as my window manager with 9 workspaces.

If I put the clipscreen monitor on screen 2 or 3, screen 1 can no longer display workspaces.  Otherwise, clipscreen seems to work as designed:  I can drag windows on top of it.

If I put the clipscreen monitor on screen 1, as soon as a drag a window over the clipscreen monitor, it starts acting like screen 1, displaying a workspace, and I can switch which workspace is displayed within the clipscreen screen.

If I disable the external monitors and start clipscreen on the laptop screen, no workspace is displayed.  If I start an application, e.g. xeyes, and drag it into the clipscreen window, a workspace is displayed.  If I change the workspace, nothing is displayed until I drag a window over the clipscreen monitor, which causes the workspace to be displayed.
author: cwarden

comments.body: sorry. no idea. I only ever tested this on my single monitor setup. happy about pull requests addressing the issue.
I think fixing this would require some way of telling xmonad to not try to manage the virtual monitor.

same thing on awesome window manager. It replaces the first screen and seems to assign the windows from the first screen to the second screen. It is even OK for the windowmanager to manage that screen, fullscreen works nicely in that rectangle! Just clipscreen should create an additional screen instead of replacing screen 1.

I googled a bit, but I couldn't find a way to add the new monitor to the end of the list. Even when using xrandr --setmonitor on the command line it will create the new monitor as monitor 0. There is probably a way to reorder the monitors afterwards but I have no idea how.

I did notice that --listmonitors complained about an unknown output for the clipscreen monitor. I fixed that, but I don't know if that changes anything for this particular problem.

If I remove line https://github.com/splitbrain/clipscreen/blob/788c1458886b7484d72e1cd512ec5b3a01c90190/clipscreen.cpp#L71  then it does not replace the first monitor, can you check @cwarden ? 
Only remove the one we added in the end, not before.

Commenting out `remove_monitor(d, root);`, I still see the first monitor being replaced.

Before starting clipscreen:
```
$ xrandr --listmonitors
Monitors: 3
 0: +*eDP-1-1 1920/344x1080/194+0+0  eDP-1-1
 1: +DP-1-3-2 2560/597x1440/336+1920+0  DP-1-3-2
 2: +DP-1-2-2 2560/597x1440/336+4480+0  DP-1-2-2
```

After starting clipscreen:

```
Monitors: 3
 0: clipscreen 943/943x551/551+549+354  eDP-1-1
 1: +DP-1-3-2 2560/597x1440/336+1920+0  DP-1-3-2
 2: +DP-1-2-2 2560/597x1440/336+4480+0  DP-1-2-2
```
Yes, right, that wasn't it. Yesterday's commit fixed it for me.

Yes, 788c1458886b7484d72e1cd512ec5b3a01c90190 pretty much fixes the issue by creating a new monitor:
```
$ xrandr --listmonitors
Monitors: 4
 0: +*eDP-1-1 1920/344x1080/194+0+0  eDP-1-1
 1: clipscreen 1291/1291x737/737+5047+376
 2: +DP-1-3-2 2560/597x1440/336+1920+0  DP-1-3-2
 3: +DP-1-2-2 2560/597x1440/336+4480+0  DP-1-2-2
```

It's a little wonky because the workspace displayed on the first monitor moves to the monitor with the new virtual monitor, but it then works as expected, allowing me to drag windows over it, and xmonad no longer displays workspaces in the virtual monitor.

Thanks, @splitbrain.
Good to hear that the major issue is fixed. Im closing this now. If anyone can figure out how to add the monitor at the end of the list, I'd be happy about a PR.

satisfaction_conditions: The virtual monitor must be created as an additional display rather than replacing an existing monitor
The window manager must be able to continue managing workspaces on the original physical monitors

body:

If you run vortex from the command line, it will report its detected rpm and you can check that it corresponds to the rate you're waving your hand.

I will continue with the build. My next unknown is if my motor will work with it. I noticed only yesterday that my total screen size is a lot bigger than yours. I have 4 64x64 matrixes, but they are 192x192mm each and your Vortex is only 235mm wide. So I might have an underpowered motor and maybe more heavy fibration issues.

---

What would be the target rpm of the core?

The lowest you can really get away with is a 10fps refresh, which is 600 rpm. That's OK for eyes in a dark room, but tricky to film. My target was 30fps, which I can do with the smaller double sided layout of Vortex - 900 rpm. For the single sided Rotovox layout that would be 1800 rpm, which is well above what I've attempted with this design.

That makes a lot of sense. With to screens back to back you double the frame rate. I did not think of it like that.

For your Vortex build only one of the screens has pixels going through the center of rotation. Does this make it less bright in the center? I do not notice that in your video's. On the other hand the LED's in the center travel less distance per rotation, making the center brighter in theory?

I'm still working on mechanical parts of my build, but it is going well.

The code compensates for the distance the LEDs travel, to maintain uniform brightness / density. The bigger problem is that when the panel is edge on to the viewer, the brightness drops off. This is an inescapable consequence of using panels with the LEDs all in one plane - each pixel is a nice bright circle when face on, but becomes thinner and thinner at glancing angles until it's just an infinitessimal line. This manifests itself as a dark wedge going through the centre of the volume.

Putting the two panels at different offsets from the axis helps reduce this effect. One panel goes right through the axis, which enables it to addres columns right in the centre, at the cost of extremely glancing angles along the line to the viewer. The other panel is further out where it can't address the centre or the region behind the axis, but has better viewing angles in the front and centre region where it matters most.

Further from the axis, the two panels are largely the same and just give a doubling of the frame rate. In the middle, they complement each other and cover up some of each other's drawbacks.

You can make it out in the water in this video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ILNbnWneTIg - there's a dark triangular region that extends out from the centre to the back of the display. If it only had a single panel on the axis, that same feature would extend all the way to the front as well. The second, offset, panel is what fills it in. You can see that the dark triangle in front of the axis cuts off against a well lit circle, which is as close in as the second panel comes. You can also see that the radial lines overlap each other in a cross hatch pattern at the front - this is the two panels passing through that region at different angles due to their offset.

comments.body: I looked into it a bit more. I reverted the files gadget_rotovox.h and gadget_vortex.h and compiled the project without my changes. I thought, if I do not need to change my pin assignment for https://github.com/hzeller/rpi-rgb-led-matrix then I probably need to use the pins as they are assigned in this project. And when I make changes then I get a lot of warnings when compiling. If I run vortex then it is showing output on the commandline as expected. But the screens stay black. Then I also run tesseract but the screens stay black. I had some times when there were some stripes on the screen, but after disabling a sound chip which the other project complained about I did not have the stripes anymore.

The documentation you have there is showing a mapping based on the numbering of the pins on the Pi's header, but the multivox code is using the internal GPIO numbers. If you look at https://pinout.xyz, you'll see how the pin numbers map to GPIO numbers.

Translating that document to show the gpio numbers, and renaming the signals to match the way they're named in the code, you end up with this:


```
-              |    -
(RGB_2_G1)  2  |     -
(RGB_2_B1)  3  |     GND
RGB_STROBE  4  |  14 (RGB_2_R1)
-              |  15 ROW_E
RGB_CLOCK  17  |  18 RGB_BLANK
RGB_0_G1   27  |     -
ROW_A      22  |  23 ROW_B
-              |  24 ROW_C
RGB_0_B2   10  |     -
RGB_0_G2    9  |  25 ROW_D
RGB_0_R1   11  |   8 RGB_0_R2
-              |   7 RGB_0_B1
-              |     -
RGB_1_G1    5  |     -
RGB_1_B1    6  |  12 RGB_1_R1
RGB_1_G2   13  |     -
RGB_1_R2   19  |  16 (RGB_2_G2)
(RGB_2_R2) 26  |  20 RGB_1_B2
-              |  21 (RGB_2_B2)
```

`BLANK` is `OE`, `STROBE` is `LAT`, and `CLOCK` is `CLK`.

`ROW_A`, `ROW_B`,  `ROW_C`, `ROW_D`,  `ROW_E` are the `A`, `B`, `C`, `D`, `E` pins on the HUB75E connector. In the original HUB75 interface these were simply the bits specifying the row currently being addressed, with `A` the LSB and `E` MSB. The rotovox gadget uses them this way because that's the style of panel it uses. As LED panels have moved to higher densities, the manufacturers have started to use different schemes for addressing each row. They still use the ABCDE naming on the connector, but those pins now carry a different signal, generally poorly documented and up to the user to decipher.

The panels used in the vortex gadget use A, B and C to carry signals shifting in the address a bit at a time. In the code I've named them `ADDR_CLK`, `ADDR_DAT`, and `ADDR__EN` - it was trial and error to discover which line took which signal.

If you have an original style panel, you define the `ROW_?` pins and leave the `ADDR_*` pins undefined. The driver code chooses what to compile based on which set is defined. (`ADDR__EN_MASK` appears in both code paths, so it needs to be defined as 0 if it's not used).

Putting all that together, the gadget mapping for ABCDE panels connected to your interface board would be:

```
#define RGB_0_R1 11
#define RGB_0_G1 27
#define RGB_0_B1 7
#define RGB_0_R2 8
#define RGB_0_G2 9
#define RGB_0_B2 10

#define RGB_1_R1 12
#define RGB_1_G1 5
#define RGB_1_B1 6
#define RGB_1_R2 19
#define RGB_1_G2 13
#define RGB_1_B2 20

#define ROW_A 22
#define ROW_B 23
#define ROW_C 24
#define ROW_D 25
#define ROW_E 15
#define ADDR__EN_MASK (0)

#define RGB_BLANK 18
#define RGB_CLOCK 17
#define RGB_STROBE 4
#define RGB_BLANK_MASK (1<<RGB_BLANK)
#define RGB_CLOCK_MASK (1<<RGB_CLOCK)

I notice a lot of distortion on the second screens on both strings. I don't know what could cause this. I'm currently using a Mean Well 5V 10A power supply to power the Pi an the 4 panels. Could that be the cause? If the power supply would be the cause then I would expect the distortion to be equal on all 4 panels, so I don't expect this to be it. I also lifted the panels up a bit to separate the data lines from the power lines but this boes not seem to make a difference eighter.

I also tried running it with only one string. But the distortion was still there on the second screen.

I have solved the distortion on the second screen. I found someone that had the same issue (https://github.com/hzeller/rpi-rgb-led-matrix/issues/1349). Turns out I had to increase the output voltage of my power supply a bit. I needed to set it to 5.4 volt. Around 5.2 vold the distortion comes back.

title: Question: SSL probe attachment failure for Node.js binary
body:
The logs show repeated warnings indicating a failure to attach SSL probes to /usr/bin/node, along with event drops due to a full channel.

```
time="2025-10-09T11:16:44Z" level=warning msg="Failed to process library event" error="failed to attach SSL probes to /usr/bin/node (inode 35280): failed to attach SSL_read entry uprobe: symbol SSL_read: not found" path=/usr/bin/node
time="2025-10-09T11:16:44Z" level=warning msg="Event channel full, dropping event"
```

## Steps to Reproduce

1.	Run the binary with Node.js processes present on the system.
2.	Observe logs around startup or library load events.


## Environment
	•	Binary: /usr/bin/node
	•	OS: kernel(6.14.0-1013-aws) ubuntu (24.04) arch (x86_64)
	•	Architecture: amd64/arm64


Should we attempt to attach SSL probes to Node.js binaries by default, or skip them when the relevant OpenSSL symbols (like SSL_read) are not found? 

Just want to clarify the design intent here. Thanks!
author: abhisheksoam

comments.body:
@abhisheksoam, thank you for providing the information.

To properly debug this, can you provide the following:
- Node version through `node --version`
- How did you install Node in your system? Were it `apt install` `apk add`, `nvm`, etc.

Regarding your questions, from my understanding, Node executables should have the OpenSSL symbols statically linked, so the `node` executable should have these symbols. If you are using `node` in a way that is working differently (in some way dynamically linking `libssl`) I would love to test that, and accordingly adapt the code. That's why I'm interested in reproducing that.

Regarding `Event channel full, dropping event`, can you elaborate a bit on the environment? Were you doing heavy lifting? processes that are heavily consuming the filesystem?
We can solve that easily by increasing the channel size, but I want to check first what the scenarios are, because I didn't encounter it in my tests.

Thanks!

@alex-ilgayev

> Node version through node --version
> How did you install Node in your system? Were it apt install apk add, nvm, etc.

- Node version: v20.18.1
- Installed via apt install

> Regarding “Event channel full, dropping event,” can you elaborate a bit on the environment? Were you doing heavy lifting or running processes that heavily use the filesystem?


No heavy load, it seems the issue occurs while attaching probes.

```
main.go:107
// Process library events
// and create uprobe hooks for dynamically loaded libraries
libManager := ebpf.NewLibraryManager(loader, mountNS)
defer libManager.Close()

-> This sets `retryOnError` to true by default, which causes the second condition to fail.
-> As a result, it keeps retrying to attach the SSL probe.

library_manager.go:65
    // Check if previously failed and retryOnError is disabled
    if err, ok := lm.failedLibs[inode]; ok && !lm.retryOnError {
        logrus.WithFields(logrus.Fields{
            "inode":         inode,
            "path":          path,
            "error":         err,
            "target_mnt_ns": targetMountNS,
        }).Trace("Library previously failed to hook, skipping")
        return nil
    }
```

So, it seems that because retryOnError is set to true by default, the condition never passes, causing continuous retries while attempting to attach the SSL probe. I modified the flag value to test this, and after that, the warnings stopped appearing.

Yes, that also resolved the `Event channel full, dropping event issue.`

Code snippet:
```
main.go:120

libManager := ebpf.NewLibraryManagerWithRetry(loader, mountNS, false)
defer libManager.Close()
```

@abhisheksoam 
I implemented a partial fix here: #65 
Can you run again your setup?

You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full.

> [@abhisheksoam](https://github.com/abhisheksoam) I implemented a partial fix here: [#65](https://github.com/alex-ilgayev/MCPSpy/pull/65) Can you run again your setup?
> 
> You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full.

Yes, this resolves the issue partially. How do you plan to address it in the future? I mean, in terms of design choices.

> > [@abhisheksoam](https://github.com/abhisheksoam) I implemented a partial fix here: [#65](https://github.com/alex-ilgayev/MCPSpy/pull/65) Can you run again your setup?
> > You will still see a warning (I will eventually fix it), but it shouldn't retry it, and hopefully, the channel shouldn't be full.
> 
> Yes, this resolves the issue partially. How do you plan to address it in the future? I mean, in terms of design choices.

@abhisheksoam This warning is actually legitimate and not hurting the functionality. Esthetically speaking, we could put that under debug, because it revolves around legitimate usage. The reason it's in a warning is that there could be some behavior that could hurt the program.

A little bit of background on why that happened in the first place - some `node` distribution linking`libssl` statically, means the `SSL_read` and `SSL_write` methods are within the `node` executable, and some are linking it dynamically, means we should hook into `libssl.*`.
We are trying to seek every executable named `node` before we know how it is linking to `libssl`, so we may fail. In your case (which I managed to reproduce), even though it is failing to hook to `node`, it is successfully hooking into the linked `libssl`, thus the program functionality is unhurt.

So I'm not really concerned about this behavior, except for some warning that may mislead/deter.

Got it, that makes sense. Thanks for the detailed explanation!
 I agree, since it’s not impacting functionality and stems from how Node links `libssl` differently across builds, it’s reasonable to downgrade this to a debug log. The warning might indeed cause unnecessary concern otherwise.
Thanks for the feedback, closing as it is solved

satisfaction_conditions: Prevention of continuous retry attempts when SSL probe attachment fails due to missing symbols
Resolution of event channel overflow caused by repeated probe attachment failures
Clarification of the design intent regarding SSL probe attachment behavior for Node.js binaries
Assurance that the warning behavior does not indicate a functional problem when SSL probes successfully attach to dynamically linked libssl

Hey @loncarales and @akhiljavelin, great chat and collaboration. Thank you both!
I've been unavailable for the past week, so I couldn't participate.

So, from what I understand, we have two issues that are related to the newly introduced MCP streamable HTTP tracking.
One is **a warning** for failing to hook into the `libssl`, and another for **missing the MCP traffic** that was being made when using the HTTP MCP protocol. Both appear in the K8s environment.

So, because the streamable HTTP was introduced in `0.0.3`, it makes sense that the warning didn't exist in `0.0.2` and appeared in `0.0.3`.

I would be extremely surprised if the code I wrote for the streamable HTTP tracking would work *as is* for a K8s environment, as there are many side-effects there, because we are hooking to user-mode libraries. So it makes sense it isn't supported there out of the box, but we'll get there.

So my next steps there would be:

- I work with @loncarales on merging this without introducing any fixes / any logic changes in **this** PR.
- Create an environment and play with it to understand what fails with the HTTP there.

Hope that makes sense.

title: Problems building the linux app
body:
Hello everyone, first of all thank you very much to have made this open source.

I know linux but not flutter nor app development so maybe I made as foolish mistake, feel free to tell me.

I tried to build the flutter app with these commands:
```bash
git clone https://github.com/even-realities/EvenDemoApp
flutter pub get
cd EvenDemoApp/linux
mkdir build && cd build
cmake ..
```

Here, the cmake output fails with a required file missing:

title: 队列满的机制
body:
当向队列写入数量达到设定值，send的tick大于0，队列满的情况下，如果不queue_receive一条，则发送task会在这while(temp == schedule_PendSV)，一直等待。schedule_PendSV一直不会有变化，调度器也会停止。
是有意这么设计么？
author: hlmpost

comments.body:
并没有，你说的这种情况不应该发生，更像是调试时编译器对空循环的优化导致的卡死问题。当队列满时，如果等待发送的队列等待时间到期，它会被唤醒并跳过while(temp == schedule_PendSV)循环，然后移除状态并返回错误。schedule_PendSV的值对调度器的运行并没有影响，它仅仅只是一个记录调度发生的标志位，我在这里加入循环是为了等待PendSV中断的发生，在这里，PendSV中断是一定会发生的，因为前面的TaskDelay延时函数会默认发起一次调度。
再次感谢你的测试，考虑到目前没有详细说明这些机制，我会补充一份使用手册的。

---

你可以注释掉while(temp == schedule_PendSV)循环（其实触发了中断是会立即执行中断的，只是确保万无一失才加上），然后在xPortPendSVHandler中断（调度中断）和SysTick_Handler中断（时钟中断，负责管理延时任务和定时触发调度中断）打上断点并观察。
我使用出现的问题，应该是在中断中调用了queue_send，是否现在ipc机制还不能在中断中使用有tick等待的方式？tick=0，我测了下，还没出现问题
只有任务对象才有延时等待，但中断并不是任务，所以不能设置tick等待时间，在中断中使用时，应当把ticks设置为0，我已经在使用手册中补充了这一点。
对，使用时容易忽略。freertos也需要专门的isr调用接口

title: Wrongly assigned format when reflecting a compute shaders
author: bolducke

comments.body:
Unfortunately, I don't think this is an issue with SDL_shadercross, but really rather with SDL GPU itself - or with either `glslang` or `dxc`, depending on how you look at it. Here's the reflection result:

```json
{
  "samplers": 0,
  "readonly_storage_textures": 2,
  "readonly_storage_buffers": 0,
  "readwrite_storage_textures": 1,
  "readwrite_storage_buffers": 0,
  "uniform_buffers": 1,
  "threadcount_x": 3,
  "threadcount_y": 3,
  "threadcount_z": 1
}
```

Looks reasonable! And here are the raw descriptor sets:

```
Descriptor set 0
        Binding 0, type 3
        Binding 1, type 3
Descriptor set 1
        Binding 0, type 3
Descriptor set 2
        Binding 0, type 6
```

Type 3 corresponds to `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_STORAGE_IMAGE`, which also makes sense. Unfortunately, SDL has [different plans](https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/blob/2ce3dfdf1df248dbd3a694bfe3a4d4a869db3476/src/gpu/vulkan/SDL_gpu_vulkan.c#L8340):

```c
currentWriteDescriptorSet->descriptorType = VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLED_IMAGE; // Yes, we are declaring the readonly storage texture as a sampled image, because shaders are stupid.
```

Vulkan does not appreciate the unexpected difference and promptly complains. Sadly, I think this boils down to GLSL vs HLSL source differences, as a corresponding compute shader in HLSL will produce `VK_DESCRIPTOR_TYPE_SAMPLED_IMAGE` bindings for read-only storage textures, so I'm not really sure what would be the right thing to do here.

This was discussed here: https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/issues/12202





---

For additional context, in HLSL when you do this:

```hlsl
Texture2D<float4> MyTexture : register(t0, space2);
```

This is compiled to SPIR-V with SAMPLED=1, meaning that the corresponding Vulkan descriptor must be SAMPLED_IMAGE. Avoiding this would mean manually writing a SPIR-V annotation. According to HKA (the author of SPIRV-Cross) actual "readonly storage images" are not meaningfully different from a sampled image anyway. So we made the call to make all readonly images use SAMPLED_IMAGE. 

Unfortunately, GLSL compilers will compile a `readonly image2D` to SPIR-V with SAMPLED=2, which requires a STORAGE_IMAGE Vulkan descriptor type. However, you can avoid this by using `sampler2D` with the `texelFetch` function, which will have the same effect as using `imageLoad` with a storage image. 

We're working on setting up a wiki page for SDL_shadercross so we can document all these language requirements explicitly.
The wiki would be really helpful since SDL_GPU seems to support a subset of features. Since this is more related to SDL itself, I will closed this issue.

From testing with `sampler2D`, it looks like that produces a combined texture/sampler annotation:

```json
{
  "samplers": 2,
  "readonly_storage_textures": 0,
  "readonly_storage_buffers": 0,
  "readwrite_storage_textures": 1,
  "readwrite_storage_buffers": 0,
  "uniform_buffers": 1,
  "threadcount_x": 3,
  "threadcount_y": 3,
  "threadcount_z": 1
}
```

```
Descriptor set 0
        Binding 0, type 1
        Binding 1, type 1
Descriptor set 1
        Binding 0, type 3
Descriptor set 2
        Binding 0, type 6
```

Does that mean you should bind these with `SDL_BindGPUComputeSamplers` instead of `SDL_BindGPUComputeStorageTextures`?
Yes.

So, to summarize:

In HLSL
* Sampled texture is a `TextureX` paired with a `SamplerState` (internally `SAMPLED_IMAGE` + `SAMPLER`)
* (Read-only) storage texture is a `TextureX` not paired with a `SamplerState` (internally `SAMPLED_IMAGE`)
* Read-write storage texture is a `RWTextureX` (internally `STORAGE_IMAGE`)

In GLSL
* Sampled texture is a `samplerX` (internally `COMBINED_IMAGE_SAMPLER`)
*  (Read-only) storage texture doesn't exist under SDL GPU semantics and a sampled texture accessed via `texelFetch` should be used for the same end result; sampler configuration doesn't matter
* Read-write storage texture is an `imageX` (internally `STORAGE_IMAGE`)

Is my understanding correct?

satisfaction_conditions: Explanation of why readonly storage images in GLSL produce descriptor type mismatches with SDL GPU's expectations
A concrete workaround for achieving readonly texture access in GLSL that is compatible with SDL GPU
Clarification that the issue stems from SDL GPU's design decisions rather than a bug in SDL_shadercross
Context about the underlying HLSL/GLSL semantic differences that drive SDL GPU's behavior

title: Question about texture sampler bindings
author: jkinz3

comments.body: Shadercross expects there to be 1 sampler per sampled texture. If there isn't a corresponding sampler it assumes that the texture is a readonly storage texture.
So I would need 4 different samplers in my shader, even if they're the same thing? I can do that; it's no problem. But that seems strange

In the SDL API you always bind textures and samplers in corresponding pairs, so it doesn't make sense to expect them to be separable in the shader. We could probably make that clearer in the documentation though. 

This is a design quirk stemming from a misunderstanding I had about Vulkan descriptor types. At this point adding new SDL functions that allow you to separate textures and samplers would probably just end up more confusing than the current situation, because we would have to create a new CreateShaderInfo struct and then have a separate binding path for shaders that use it.
Yup I got it to work with multiple samplers defined in HLSL. Thanks for the clarification!

author: ThrudTheBarbarian

comments.body:
So an update on this, because I was fiddling around trying to figure out any possible way to get multiple input textures into my shader...

It looks as though the above mismatch is an optimisation thing - I'd commented out any use of 'rgnImage' in the shader body while trying to figure out what was going on. Uncommenting it gives me the following declaration of main0 (spacing for clarity):

```
kernel void main0(constant type_UBO& UBO [[buffer(0)]], 
                  texture2d<float> srcImage [[texture(0)]], 
                  texture2d<float> rgnImage [[texture(1)]], 
                  texture2d<float, access::write> dstImage [[texture(2)]], 
                  sampler srcSampler [[sampler(0)]], 
                  sampler rgnSampler [[sampler(1)]], 
                  uint3 gl_GlobalInvocationID [[thread_position_in_grid]])
```

... which looks correct to me. I wrote a [shader-toy-alike](https://discord.com/channels/405784877305298944/1346621571862630420)  app while thinking I had to wait for this to be resolved, and testing everything there gives me the results I expect - when I set a constant alpha=1 in the "regions" image, I get the noise image, when I set it to 0, I get a fully transparent image. 

So bottom line: It looks as though the optimiser is getting rid of any textures that aren't being used in the kernel body, but if those textures are still supplied (as per the definition of the shader) then there is a mismatch. Whether this is a bug or user-error is up for debate, I think. I could see it being either way, but it would be nice if commenting out stuff didn't have catastrophic effects on the shader. 

For example, there was one time where I wasn't marking some textures as writeable, and then they were being swapped because of this effect, and then the app would crash with a Metal validation error. It wasn't obvious that the commenting out was the cause because it was just saying it couldn't write to the texture (the correct texture was of course writeable..)
All shader compilers strip unused resources, I don't think there's anything we can do about that from our end.
Seems fair. Can probably close this then :)
Duplicate of https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL_shadercross/issues/127

comments.body:
> I have cloned the project and its submodules completely. I run the following cmake command:
> 
> ```
> cmake -S . -B build -DSDLSHADERCROSS_DXC=ON -DDirectXShaderCompiler_INCLUDE_PATH=external/DirectXShaderCompiler/include -DDirectXShaderCompiler_dxcompiler_LIBRARY=external/DirectXShaderCompiler/lib/libdxcompiler.so -DDirectXShaderCompiler_dxil_LIBRARY=external/DirectXShaderCompiler/lib/libdxil.so -Dspirv_cross_c_shared_DIR=~/vulkansdk/1.4.304.0/x86_64/share/spirv_cross_c_shared/cmake
> ```

It looks like you passed paths to for the dxcompiler because CMake configuration failed for you.
`*_INCLUDE_PATH` and `*_PATH` variables needs paths to **existing** directories and/or files.

Run `cmake -P build-scripts/download-prebuilt-DirectXShaderCompiler.cmake` to download prebuilt directxcompiler binaries from [microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler](https://github.com/microsoft/DirectXShaderCompiler/releases), and configure with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=external/DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries`


Alternatively, build everything yourself by configuring with `-DSDLSHADERCROSS_VENDORED=TRUE`. Then you don't need to download any pre-built binaries, don't need to configure with `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH` etc.

Thank you! DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries contained the missing library, I changed all of the path directories to reference the new binaries directory and it worked. CMake command (larger than necessary, just trying to cover every base) for anyone who's interested:

```
cmake -S . -B build -DSDLSHADERCROSS_DXC=ON -DDirectXShaderCompiler_INCLUDE_PATH=external/DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries/linux/include/ -DDirectXShaderCompiler_dxcompiler_LIBRARY=external/DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries/linux/lib/libdxcompiler.so -DDirectXShaderCompiler_dxil_LIBRARY=external/DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries/linux/lib/libdxil.so -Dspirv_cross_c_shared_DIR=~/vulkansdk/1.4.304.0/x86_64/share/spirv_cross_c_shared/cmake -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=external/DirectXShaderCompiler-binaries/
```

title: Help with CMake setup
body:
Hello!

We want to add this library to our project, but we are encountering CMake issues.

So far we have recursively cloned this repo and added it as a submodule.
SDL3 (3.2.0) is statically added as a library, like [here](https://github.com/Ravbug/sdl3-sample/blob/main/CMakeLists.txt#L65), but we are getting the same error from #89.

I noticed that SDL3_DIR has to be set to the SDL3 build directory, but this relies on building SDL3 separately.

Is there a way to add this directly without the find_package functionality? If not, are there any alternatives? 

Thanks

        add_library(SDL3_shadercross-shared SHARED ${SOURCE_FILES})

@@ -198,7 +202,7 @@ endif()
 
 if(SDLSHADERCROSS_STATIC)

+       if(NOT TARGET SDL3::Headers)
                find_package(SDL3 ${SDL_REQUIRED_VERSION} REQUIRED COMPONENTS Headers)
        endif()
 
@@ -265,6 +269,9 @@ if(SDLSHADERCROSS_CLI)
                target_link_libraries(shadercross PRIVATE SDL3_shadercross::SDL3_shadercross-static)

CMake Error at TelltaleEditor/3rdparty/SDL_shadercross/CMakeLists.txt:132 (find_package):

In this type of workflow, how do I build/add SPIRV-Cross and DXBC? I have only recursively cloned the repos.

You need to configure with `SDLSHADERCROSS_VENDORED` set to a true-ish variable.
Otherwise it will look for system packages.

Thanks! It worked. Building solution files works successfully now, but building the project has some linking problems (SDL_shadercross.lib cannot be opened). I am currently trying to figure out the problem

Make sure you link to the namespaced targets:
```cmake 
target_link_libraries(mygame PRIVATE SDL3_shadercross::SDL3_shadercross-static SDL3::SDL3-static
```

Thanks!

It was a typo, I am having errors with the target name for some reason, but I think I can handle it.

title: Shader compilation fails with SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_DXBC and shader model 5.1.
body:
I'm compiling a hlsl shader to DXBC. This is the error message:

D3D11 ERROR: ID3D11Device::CreatePixelShader: Shader must be ps_4_0, ps_4_1, or ps_5_0. Shader version provided: UNRECOGNIZED [ STATE_CREATION ERROR #193: CREATEPIXELSHADER_INVALIDSHADERTYPE]

I switched the shader model to 5.0 to fix it.

These are the functions where I changed it:
SDL_ShaderCross_INTERNAL_CompileFromSPIRV()
SDL_ShaderCross_INTERNAL_CompileDXBCFromHLSL()
author: guitarfreak

comments.body:
The SDL GPU API doesn't support D3D11, so I don't really think it's worth the effort to have this library support it. What's your use case?

---

Also to clarify, this isn't shader compilation failing. The compilation clearly succeeds but D3D11 can't accept SM 5.1 bytecode.

These are the SDL gpu shader formats:

```c++
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_INVALID  0
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_PRIVATE  (1u << 0) /**< Shaders for NDA'd platforms. */
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_SPIRV    (1u << 1) /**< SPIR-V shaders for Vulkan. */
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_DXBC     (1u << 2) /**< DXBC SM5_0 shaders for D3D11. */
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_DXIL     (1u << 3) /**< DXIL shaders for D3D12. */
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_MSL      (1u << 4) /**< MSL shaders for Metal. */
#define SDL_GPU_SHADERFORMAT_METALLIB (1u << 5) /**< Precompiled metallib shaders for Metal. */
```

I was testing the compilation of a simple hlsl shader for SPIRV, DXBC, DXIL and MSL.
When you give this library DXBC you eventually call SDL_ShaderCross_INTERNAL_CompileDXBC() which calls SDL_D3DCompile() which is loaded from d3dcompiler_47.dll. And that's where it fails for shader model 5.1.

Do you really think 5.1 is correct for DXBC?
You seem to be working with very outdated source, we removed D3D11 support and bumped DXBC to 5.1 a while ago.
I see, my bad. To be fair though, in terms of official releases this has only changed since 3.1.8 which came out 5 days ago. :)

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of whether shader model 5.1 is the correct target for DXBC compilation in the current version of the library
Explanation of why the observed behavior differs from the documented shader format specifications
Information about the current state and version compatibility of the library's DXBC shader compilation support

title: Shadercross hangs when compiling HLSL vertex shader
author: karabatov

comments.body:
Was able to repro on my machine, looking into it.

---

The hang is inside DXC, for some reason it doesn't like the `matrix` keyword. It's supposed to default to a 4x4 float matrix, but I guess it's broken. If you change the declarations to a more specific format like `float4x4` the issue goes away. author: christopherliu830

comments.body: Hit the same issue where I have 3 structured buffers and 1 uniform in the vertex shader and 2 structured buffers and 1 uniform in the fragment shader. ```

Thank you!

title: Mouse won't go past certain distance from left of terminal window.
body: The mouse won't go past the halfway point of the terminal window when using any application and the distance that the mouse will go from the left of the screen decreases when I zoom out the terminal. Please advise?
author: Pako-12317

comments.body:
I suspect this is because term.everything is using the default mouse protocol which for historical reason can only handle coordinates up to a maximum value of 223 (possibly just 94 on some terminals). To get the full coordinate range you need to request the SGR mouse encoding (mode `?1006`). See xterm's [Extended coordinates](https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html#h3-Extended-coordinates) documentation for more details.

It may also be worth looking at mode `?1016`, which returns pixel coordinates. That's not as widely supported, but you can check whether a terminal will be able to handle that mode with a [`DECRQM`](https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECRQM.html) query. If the [`DECRPM`](https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/DECRPM.html) response is 0 (not recognized) or 4 (permanently reset), then it's not going to work. Although be aware that some terminals won't respond to `DECRQM` queries at all.

I think you are right, it just enables mouse with https://github.com/mmulet/term.everything/blob/2dc413f565365ed9aae5b5f27686e6f42f124e6a/escapecodes/AsiEscapeCodes.go#L7 . I will add these changes to my todo list.

---

The todo list is to-done. The fix has been added to [version 0.7.8](https://github.com/mmulet/term.everything/releases/tag/0.7.8). I added support for SGR, but I held off on querying for ?1016 support for now (will probably come back to it later).

Thanks for the assist, @j4james ! You seem very knowledgeable about terminal emulators. If you have any other ideas for improvements (or anything else I'm doing obviously wrong), please let me know! You can open an issue, a discussion, or just send me a quick email, etc. Thanks again!

title: Container stats missing with socket-proxy?
body:
Hey, and thanks for creating this project!

I migrated to `socket-proxy` yesterday and lost all individual container stats. Everyting else is fine. In the backend, I can see that table is just empty.

No errors in the logs:

```
2025/01/05 17:09:51 Server started at http://0.0.0.0:8090

├─ REST API:  http://0.0.0.0:8090/api/

└─ Dashboard: http://0.0.0.0:8090/_/
```

And:

```
2025/01/05 17:09:51 INFO Root disk mountpoint=/ io=sda

2025/01/05 17:09:51 INFO Detected network interface name=enp6s18 sent=32976148128417 recv=1927194881807

2025/01/05 17:09:51 INFO DOCKER_HOST host=tcp://socket-proxy:2375

2025/01/05 17:09:51 INFO Starting SSH server address=:45876
```

Here is my compose file:

```
services:
  beszel:
    image: 'henrygd/beszel:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    extra_hosts:
      - 'host.docker.internal:host-gateway'
    ports:
      - '8090:8090'
    volumes:
      - '/var/mounts/beszel/beszel_data:/beszel_data'
  beszel-agent:
    image: 'henrygd/beszel-agent:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      - 'DOCKER_HOST=tcp://socket-proxy:2375'
      - PORT=45876
      - >-
        KEY=ssh-ed25519
        AAAAC3NzaC1lZDI1NTE5AAAAIKN1E5TF2lzh4Otb2sfyMY0b7jVFRD26UlZ4UhB5owN9
  socket-proxy:
    image: 'lscr.io/linuxserver/socket-proxy:latest'
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - CONTAINERS=1
    volumes:
      - '/var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro'
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /run
```

I've made a few vain attempts at making this work, mostly by increasing permissions (`POST=1`, `ALLOW_RESTARTS=1`, `ALLOW_RESTARTS=1`, `ALLOW_START=1`, `ALLOW_STOP=1`) eventually abandoning brute-force and actually reading the code of both projects.

Unfortunately, reading the pertinent parts ([ref](https://github.com/henrygd/beszel/blob/main/beszel/internal/agent/docker.go), [ref](https://github.com/Tecnativa/docker-socket-proxy/blob/master/haproxy.cfg)) doesn't really tell me why this would break. It seems like it should just work!

Does anyone else have any hints on why container stats would be missing in such a simple setup?
author: goncalossilva

comments.body:
This is a bit confusing so I'll make a note to mention this in the docs.

Because the agent uses `network_mode: host`, it cannot resolve the proxy using the hostname `socket-proxy`. They are in different networks.

The solution is to expose the the proxy on localhost (this does not allow external connections), then use localhost to connect from the agent.

```yml
services:
  beszel-agent:
    environment:
      - DOCKER_HOST=tcp://127.0.0.1:2375
  socket-proxy:
    ports:
      - 127.0.0.1:2375:2375
```

Let me know if you have any trouble with this!

Ah, what a silly oversight on my part. That makes a lot of sense! Thanks for clarifying and adding a note to the docs, I think it will help others as they adopt socket-proxy and might miss this detail.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why the hostname resolution fails when using network_mode: host with a service in a different Docker network

I followed the guide at https://anubis.techaro.lol/docs/admin/configuration/subrequest-auth to set it up. I saw that the latest version has made a change to subrequest auth, so this is either a lack of docs or a bug.

### Steps to reproduce

Set up subrequest authentication as described in https://anubis.techaro.lol/docs/admin/configuration/subrequest-auth. Anubis is not showing up

### Expected behavior

Anubis should properly block traffic

### Your operating system and its version.

Linux

### Your browser and its version.

Librewolf 144

### Additional context

_No response_
author: TuTiuTe

comments.body: This is intentional behaviour. The changes in 1.23.0 make Anubis show up less frequently due to vastly improved heuristics. If you want to make Anubis more aggressive to match the previous behaviour, remove these lines from your policy file: https://github.com/TecharoHQ/anubis/blob/02989f03d0b971188d52724ae90dc93fbf99d685/data/botPolicies.yaml#L99-L141

Damn okay good to know! Thought it was a bug or on me  
Do you have  a blog post or a doc explaining these new heuristics? I'm curious as to how they work

title: Should .sync.lock & `sync_base.jsonl` be gitignored?
body:
#918 Added a new pull-first sync strategy, and as part of that it appears that two new files are created in `.beads/` during syncs - `.sync.lock` and `sync_base.jsonl`.

Should the `.sync.lock` file be added to the `.beads/.gitignore`? 

The [SYNC doc](https://github.com/steveyegge/beads/blob/main/docs/SYNC.md#files-reference) notes that:

1. The `.sync.lock` is not tracked, which sounds then like it should be added to the ignore.
2. The `sync_base.jsonl` is git-tracked, so probably should not be ignored? But I notice that when I run syncs, it does not appear to be committed pushed to the sync-branch I am using.

cc @peterkc - as you authored #918 perhaps you have a view on this question? Not sure whether to label this as a bug yet, as I am not 100% sure if I understand the feature and the change correctly.
author: joshuaballoch

comments.body:
Thanks for catching this @joshuaballoch! As the author of PR #918 (pull-first sync), I can clarify the design intent:

## `.sync.lock`

This is a **concurrency guard** — prevents two `bd sync` processes from corrupting state by running simultaneously. It's purely local and should definitely be gitignored. The docs correctly say "not tracked" but I missed adding it to the template.

## `sync_base.jsonl`

This is where the docs have an error. The file stores **your machine's last-synced state** — the snapshot used as the "base" in 3-way merge. It should be **local-only**, not git-tracked.

Here's why: if `sync_base.jsonl` were tracked, when you pull from a teammate, their base state would overwrite yours. Your next sync would then compare against *their* last sync point instead of *yours* — leading to incorrect merge decisions.

The base state is inherently per-machine. Each machine needs its own record of "what did I see last time I synced?"

## Fix Coming

I'll submit a PR to:
1. Add both files to `GitignoreTemplate` in `doctor/gitignore.go`
2. Add them to `requiredPatterns` for `bd doctor` validation
3. Correct SYNC.md line 177 ("git-tracked" → "not tracked")

For anyone hitting this now: you can manually add these to `.beads/.gitignore` or wait for the fix and run `bd doctor --fix`.

Nice one, thanks for the quick and informative reply @peterkc!

Makes sense for the `sync_base.jsonl` file - I was not sure but was wondering if it might also have been a local-only file.

Thanks again for this work, #918 was a really helpful change 🎉 🎉
@joshuaballoch PR added

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of whether .sync.lock should be gitignored with technical justification
Resolution of the apparent contradiction about sync_base.jsonl's tracking status
Technical explanation of the purpose and behavior of the new sync-related files
Identification of a concrete path forward to address the gitignore issue

title: 在 docker 部署的环境中，因为 app 的 PID 为 1，无法回收僵尸进程
body:
root@4db22dcff618:/app# ps -eo pid,ppid,user,stat,cmd
    PID    PPID USER     STAT CMD
      1       0 root     Ssl+ ./app
     31       1 root     Z    [cat] <defunct>
     32       1 root     Z    [cat] <defunct>
     34       1 root     Z    [chrome_crashpad] <defunct>
     36       1 root     Z    [chrome_crashpad] <defunct>
     41       1 root     Z    [chrome] <defunct>
     42       1 root     Z    [chrome] <defunct>
    110       1 root     ZN   [chrome] <defunct>
    150       0 root     Ss   bash
    159     150 root     R+   ps -eo pid,ppid,user,stat,cmd


AI 的调查结果：

• 问题在容器里 PID 1 的 Go 进程没有“收尸”（reap）子进程。go-rod 的 launcher 启动 Chrome 后，在 Close() 时会 Kill()
  进程组，Chrome 的子进程被强杀后变成孤儿并被 PID 1 接管，但 PID 1 不调用 wait()，于是留下 [chrome],
  [chrome_crashpad], [cat] 的僵尸。
  证据点：headless_browser 里用 rod/lib/launcher 启 Chrome，Close() 调 launcher.Cleanup()，而 Kill() 会杀整个进程
  组。详见 /home/ruijzhan/go/pkg/mod/github.com/xpzouying/headless_browser@v0.2.0/headless_browser.go 和 /home/
  ruijzhan/go/pkg/mod/github.com/go-rod/rod@v0.116.2/lib/launcher/launcher.go。

  最直接的修复是在容器里加一个 init 进程来回收僵尸：

  - docker run: 加 --init
  - docker compose: 加 init: true

  例如在 docker/docker-compose.yml：

  services:
    xiaohongshu-mcp:
      init: true

  如果你想在应用里修：在 main 启动时加一个 SIGCHLD 回收循环（syscall.Wait4(-1, ...)），不过 Docker 的 init/tini 是
  更稳的做法。
author: ruijzhan

comments.body: “docker compose: 加 init: true” 这个方法有效

感谢 @ruijzhan 发现并报告了这个问题！

你的分析非常准确，清晰地定位到了 Docker 环境中 PID 1 无法回收僵尸进程的根本原因。而且你还验证了 `init: true` 这个解决方案的有效性，这对修复工作帮助很大。

现在这个问题已经通过 PR #355 修复了，Docker 部署时会自动使用 init 进程来回收僵尸进程。

再次感谢你的贡献！👍

satisfaction_conditions: A method to prevent zombie process accumulation in Docker containers where the application runs as PID 1
A solution that can be implemented at the Docker deployment level without requiring application code changes
An explanation of the root cause linking the PID 1 behavior, go-rod's Chrome process management, and zombie process creation
