title: Incorrect role check in getAuthorForEvent function
body:
## Issue Description

In the `getAuthorForEvent` function (agent/agent.go, line 210), there's a potential role checking logic issue:

```go
func getAuthorForEvent(ctx InvocationContext, event *session.Event) string {
    if event.LLMResponse.Content != nil && event.LLMResponse.Content.Role == genai.RoleUser {
        return genai.RoleUser
    }
    return ctx.Agent().Name()
}
```

## Problem

The function checks if the Role equals `genai.RoleUser` and returns it directly. However, the event author should typically be set to the agent's name, not the role type. This suggests one of the following:

1. The role check should be checking for a different role type (e.g., `genai.RoleAssistant` or `genai.RoleModel`)
2. The return value should be the actual author/username, not a role constant
3. There might be a logical error where the condition logic is incorrect

## Impact

This could result in incorrect event author attribution when events are created by agents with LLM responses, which could cause issues in session tracking and event logging.

## Location

File: `agent/agent.go`
Line: 210
author: MRuhan17

comments.body: Hi @MRuhan17 thank you for bring this up, please let us know if you encountered any specific issue with this. This is intentional as noted in https://google.github.io/adk-docs/streaming/dev-guide/part3/#event-authorship, for typical events created by agents with LLM response the Content's Role should not be "user" and as such the agent name will be used for the Author field.

Thanks for the clarification, @bapbtmont! That makes perfect sense. Your explanation aligns with my understanding of the intended behavior.

I've already addressed this issue in PR #371 (Fix: Resolve author attribution issues in agent.go) by removing the incorrect role check and ensuring the agent name is consistently returned for author attribution.

The PR also fixes the related issue #370 about the missing invocation ended state. Once PR #371 is merged, both issues will be resolved.

Thanks for the detailed feedback and for confirming the design intent!

As mentioned in the https://google.github.io/adk-docs/streaming/dev-guide/part3/#event-authorship, If content.role == 'user', ADK sets Event.author to "user" to handle user transcriptions. This is the intended behavior, the change you provided would break this edge case.
Closing since this is intended behavior per the streaming dev guide; thanks for the clarification.

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of the design intent behind the role checking logic
Reference to authoritative documentation explaining the behavior
Explanation of the edge case that the code handles

title: 🐛 Bug Report: Using API frequently results in 429 Too Many Requests
body:
### Reproduction steps

First, thank you so much for your great work! I love Pocket-ID.
I decided to report a bug since this is an issue for me, but I understand that it could be considered a feature request.
Currently, I'm managing about 40 OIDC clients for 12 users in a homelab. Managing this via the UI is difficult, so I try to do so via infrastructure as code. I use [Trozz/terraform-provider-pocketid](https://github.com/Trozz/terraform-provider-pocketid) (to which I also contribute) to configure PocketID via Terraform/OpenTofu.
The hard rate-limiting thresholds in pocket-id are a problem.

### Expected behavior

In my scenario, it would be ideal to be able to increase the rate-limiting threshold by an order of magnitude, or better yet, opt out of it completely, to allow for full control with an external reverse proxy. In my opinion, baking it into the software is a questionable design decision.

### Actual Behavior

Often, deploying stuff is an issue because, during deployment, the system reads the state of all individual entities via separate API calls, which effectively bursts the API. These calls are often throttled during subsequent deployments and eventually rate-limited with an HTTP response code of 429 (Too Many Requests).
I found a discussion #1118 that states the rate-limiting behavior of PocketID is currently not configurable.

### Pocket ID Version

v2.1.0

### Database

SQLite

### OS and Environment

Docker version 29.1.3 on Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS served via traefik v3.6.6

### Log Output

_No response_
author: meerumschlungen

comments.body: I've added a new environment variable `DISABLE_RATE_LIMITING` in 0d40d30d876773c06e6ff44b99fc0988c013650c. This should be available in the next release :)

Thank you so much for being this responsive!
Just as a side note for people stumbling upon this: rate-limiting can now be disabled but be aware that it is probably not a good idea to just disable it when running into issues without other security measurements in place, especially when pocket-id is facing internet. Follow security principles and establish a suitable and reasonable solution for your environment e.g. perform rate-limiting via reverse proxy, configure fail2ban, etc.

[See docs](https://pocket-id.org/docs/configuration/environment-variables):

> You can disable the built-in rate limiting if you want to set your own rate limiting policy. Do not disable this if you don't have your own rate limiting configured in your reverse proxy.

satisfaction_conditions: A mechanism to bypass or disable the built-in rate limiting functionality
Support for managing multiple OIDC clients programmatically without hitting rate limits
Configuration flexibility that allows external rate limiting control

title: 🚀 Feature: Support `?access_token` query param in `/userinfo` endpoint.
body:
### Feature description

I'm trying to configure Pocket ID with Roundcube+Dovecot combo. I'm using these [authelia](https://www.authelia.com/integration/openid-connect/clients/roundcube/) and [authentik](https://integrations.goauthentik.io/chat-communication-collaboration/roundcube/#roundcube-configuration) guides as references.

Everything works great, except one part - dovecot doesn't send `Authorization` header to the userinfo endpoint. It basically appends it to the end of the URL, thus the suggestion from authentik to do the following in the config:

```
tokeninfo_url = https://authentik.company/application/o/userinfo/?access_token=
```

Would it be possible to implement something similar in pocket id as well? Not sure about the security implications, but the patch should be as simple as:

```diff
diff --git a/backend/internal/controller/oidc_controller.go b/backend/internal/controller/oidc_controller.go
index 86d26e1..7ce3464 100644
--- a/backend/internal/controller/oidc_controller.go
+++ b/backend/internal/controller/oidc_controller.go
@@ -204,8 +204,11 @@ func (oc *OidcController) createTokensHandler(c *gin.Context) {
 func (oc *OidcController) userInfoHandler(c *gin.Context) {
        _, authToken, ok := strings.Cut(c.GetHeader("Authorization"), " ")
        if !ok || authToken == "" {
-               _ = c.Error(&common.MissingAccessToken{})
-               return
+               authToken, ok = c.GetQuery("access_token")
+               if !ok || authToken == "" {
+                       _ = c.Error(&common.MissingAccessToken{})
+                       return
+               }
        }

        token, err := oc.jwtService.VerifyOAuthAccessToken(authToken)
```

plus tests obviously :) I'm happy to create PR, but I'm not auth/oidc expect, so I'm not sure about security implications of this solution - although if authentik does it, I think it's safe?

Edit: I forgot to mention - but, yes I implemented this patch in my cluster, and with it, I can confirm everything worked smoothly and as expected, with pocket ID succesfully authenticating the email user in roundcube (and by extension - in dovecot).

### Pitch

With this simple change, it opens pocked ID for supporting webmail clients supporting oauth2 integration with dovecot (like roundcube in this example, not sure if anything else?)
author: ajgon

comments.body:
Thanks for the detailed description. I'm not really a fan of implementing this into Pocket ID, because the OIDC spec doesn't mention that access tokens over query params is a valid authentication method and I've never heard of another service before that does this. In my opinion this is something Dovecot has to fix.

I've found the following workaround on Reddit though, this probably works with Pocket ID as well:
```
tokeninfo_url = https://<pocket-id>/api/oidc/userinfo?trash=
introspection_url = https://<pocket-id>/api/oidc/introspect
introspection_mode = auth
```

[Source](https://www.reddit.com/r/selfhosted/comments/omwb2j/comment/hrtznxj/?utm_source=share&utm_medium=web3x&utm_name=web3xcss&utm_term=1&utm_content=share_button)

OMG it worked! 😆 I'd swear, I was googling for the solution for like two days, because I hated to introduce this hack as well.... apparently my google-fu needs a bit of an improvement ;)

Thank you very much, for this solution! :)

title: 🐛 Bug Report: S3 storage backend does not support some S3-compatible object storage providers (e.g. Linode)
body:
### Reproduction steps

When using an S3-compatible object storage offering such as Linode's, which however does not fully support all the integrity checks that AWS has implemented, putting objects fails.

To reproduce, set up a bucket on such a provider and try to bootstrap a new Pocket ID instance. I currently only know of Linode failing for sure and don't know if it can be easily reproduced with something like MinIO.

See aws/aws-sdk-go-v2#2960 for how to potentially mitigate this when using the AWS Go SDK. There probably should be a config option to enable this backwards compatibility.

### Expected behavior

Objects (e.g. the `background.webp` during bootstrap) should be put on the object storage without issue.

### Actual Behavior

author: sunsky89757

comments.body: ## 分析上游接口地址 接入新渠道首先要明白渠道的完整接口地址，查看官方文档进行分析。 `z.ai` [官方文档](https://docs.z.ai/scenario-example/develop-tools/claude) 接入cc里面是这样配置的，就说明完整的接口地址应该是： `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic/v1/messages`。需要能理解这个完整地址的分析逻辑才能进行后面的接入。 ## 按照接口地址配置分组测试地址 拿到了完整的接口地址 `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic/v1/messages` ，那么就可以接入。 配置分组有个原则就说 上游地址 + 测试地址 = 完整接口地址，所以上游应该配置为 `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic`，测试地址 `/v1/messages` （默认就是这个，可以不配置）。 如图： ## 客户端请求 由于分组配置的上游是 `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic` ，所以把分组代理地址接入到客户端之后，客户端的完整请求地址应该是： `http://localhost:3001/proxy/glm/v1/messages`。这样在经过GPT-Load代理之后透传替换之后的上游完整路径则为： `https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic/v1/messages` 与上面分析的上游完整接口地址相符，这样才能正常使用。 --- 以上只是个例，无论接入哪个渠道都应该按照这个思路去分析，因为文档无法覆盖所有的渠道，思路比结果更重要。 具体的可以参考一下官方的路径策略设计逻辑： https://www.gpt-load.com/docs/architecture-design/routing-strategy

During a **PostgreSQL restore** operation performed with **Databasus**, the process fails due to an authentication error, even though a `.pgpass` file is automatically generated by the tool.

The backup is created from a **PostgreSQL 14** server and restored to a **PostgreSQL 14 identical (mirror) server**.  
The backup storage is a **S3-compatible object storage**.

---

## Environment
- Tool: **Databasus 2.21.1**
- Source database: PostgreSQL 14
- Target database: PostgreSQL 14
- Backup storage: S3-compatible object storage
- Authentication method: password 

---

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Configure Databasus to back up a PostgreSQL 14 database.
2. Store the backup on an S3-compatible object storage (scality).
3. Start a restore operation to a PostgreSQL 14 mirror server.
4. The restore fails at the beginning of the restore process.

---

The restore process fails with the following error:

PostgreSQL authentication failed - no password supplied. stderr: pg_restore: connecting to database for restore
WARNING: password file "/databasus-data/temp/pgpass_8dd95546-6a40-400f-aa9c-7435c52321db992840413/.pgpass" has group or world access; permissions should be u=rw (0600) or less

title: S3 bucket mapping fails when Object Lock requires checksum headers (PutObject returns 400)
body: ## Description Mapping a new S3 bucket fails during the direct test/mapping flow because the PutObject request is rejected by S3 when Object Lock parameters are involved. The API returns an HTTP 400 and the server logs indicate that S3 requires either a `Content-MD5` header or an `x-amz-checksum-*` header for these requests. As a result, users are unable to validate or map a new bucket via S3 regardless of configuration attempts. This blocks onboarding/connecting new buckets where Object Lock is enabled or required. ## Technical Details - Error message: - `failed to upload test file to S3: Content-MD5 OR x-amz-checksum- HTTP header is required for Put Object requests with Object Lock parameters` - API endpoint observed: - `POST /api/v1/storages/direct-test` - Server log: - `[GIN] 2025/12/29 - 05:28:05 | 400 | 26.509089ms | 47.150.97.18 | POST "/api/v1/storages/direct-test"` - Symptom: - “No matter what I try, I can't connect over S3 to map in a new bucket.” - Notes / suspected cause: - Our S3 client PutObject call likely sets Object Lock headers/parameters but does not include `Content-MD5` or `x-amz-checksum-*`, which some S3 providers (and AWS S3 with Object Lock) require. ## Version v2.18.1
author: smyoss

title: Special characters in filenames broken with Traefik 3.6.4
body:
## Describe the bug

When using Traefik 3.6.4, there seem to be problems with some filenames.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Create a file called "foo#bar.txt"
2. Have OpenCloud sync it to the server
3. Try to delete or download it in the Web frontend

## Expected behavior
The file should be downloaded or deleted.

## Actual behavior
The file is "stuck" and cannot be changed or deleted on the server. Deleting on the client now yields an error message in the client, and deleting in the web frontend does also not work. Neither of the clients nor the server return any useful log output, but I assume there is some kind of problem with the encoding.

## Setup

- OpenCloud 4.0.0
- Installed via Docker Compose (custom compose file, but pretty much exactly like the opencloud-compose would work)
- Existing Traefik
- The data directory is mounted as bind volume from a standard ext4 directory

## Additional context

It seems like Traefik tries to be smarter than it should be and might be related to (or even a duplicate of) opencloud-compose#174.

Observations:

- Setting `allowEncodedHash=true` in the Traefik config did _not_ help (it might be very interesting why)
- Downgrading Traefik to 3.6.2 _did_ solve the problem

In opencloud-compose, there are some `allowEncoded` settings for Traefik, and I thought adding `allowEncodedHash` might solve the problem, but it does not.

I did not find out which other characters break OpenCloud and what is the "correct" way to use them in URLs (like in this case).
author: nicokaiser

comments.body: https://github.com/traefik/traefik/issues/12399 suggests per-entrypoint configuration of allowed encoded chacacters in Traefik (and an option to allow all encoded characters again). Things like OpenCloud (maybe WebDAV in general) could be a valid usecase for this.

> Observations:
> 
> * Setting `allowEncodedHash=true` in the Traefik config did _not_ help (it might be very interesting why)
> * Downgrading Traefik to 3.6.2 _did_ solve the problem
> 
> In opencloud-compose, there are some `allowEncoded` settings for Traefik, and I thought adding `allowEncodedHash` might solve the problem, but it does not.
> 
> I did not find out which other characters break OpenCloud and what is the "correct" way to use them in URLs (like in this case).

good catch - I'm facing the same. setting "--entryPoints.https.http.encodedCharacters.allowEncodedHash=true" fixed it for me though. maybe something just isn't getting set properly in your setup

You are right: I had a typo in my entrypoint name in my setup, I did not test it yet, but I am sure `allowEncodedHash` will indeed work.

Maybe it's enough to note this in the installation instructions, and – more importantly – in the opencloud-compose repository.

satisfaction_conditions: A configuration approach that allows special characters (specifically hash symbols) in filenames to be properly handled through the reverse proxy
Documentation or guidance on the proper configuration needed for WebDAV-based applications when using Traefik 3.6.4+
A solution that works with Traefik 3.6.4 without requiring downgrade to earlier versions

title: Opencloud tries to write xattrs in the security namespace
body:
Followup of https://github.com/opencloud-eu/opencloud/issues/1853

If we read the `security.SMACK64` we won't be able to write it back. This leads to errors in environments where selinux is enabled.

We should filter the attributes and only withe attributes from the user namespace.

title: RayClusterReplicaSetStatus.Replicas value inconsistent with definition
body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

**Description**

The value of RayClusterReplicaSetStatus.Replicas does not match its intended definition under certain conditions.

According to the definition in [rayclusterreplicaset_types.go#L61](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/main/api/orchestration/v1alpha1/rayclusterreplicaset_types.go#L61)

```
Replicas is the most recently observed number of replicas.
```
However, in the current implementation — see
[rayclusterreplicaset_utils.go#L183](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/main/pkg/controller/rayclusterreplicaset/rayclusterreplicaset_utils.go#L183)

the value of Replicas is computed after filtering out inactive RayClusters, as shown in the logic around
[rayclusterreplicaset_controller.go#L134](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/main/pkg/controller/rayclusterreplicaset/rayclusterreplicaset_controller.go#L134)

This behavior makes the observed Replicas value inconsistent with its definition.

Expected behavior is that the Replicas field should reflect the most recently observed total number of replicas, regardless of whether some clusters are inactive.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a RayClusterFleet whose pods cannot start and remain in CrashLoopBackOff state
2. kubectl get rayclusterreplicasets <name> -o yaml and observe that the status.replicas field is incorrect

### Expected behavior

RayClusterReplicaSetStatus.Replicas should be aligned with its definition and represent the last observed number of replicas (including inactive ones).

### Environment

- Aibrix version: 0.4.1 & 0.5
author: zhixian82

comments.body:
Thanks for raising this issue, @zhixian82 .

IIUC, in the context of RayClusterReplicaSet, we intentionally define "replicas" as active/managed RayClusters that are still considered part of the current desired state — not including those that have been marked for deletion, are terminating, or are otherwise no longer under active control of the controller.

This aligns with patterns used in core Kubernetes workloads (e.g., Deployment, ReplicaSet), where:

.status.replicas reflects the number of non-terminated pods (i.e., pods that haven’t been deleted and are still running or starting),
Terminated or failed pods are excluded from .status.replicas but may be counted in other fields like .status.unavailableReplicas or visible via owner references.

---

But, I think we can modify the API comment to make it more accurate. 🤔
@zhixian82 would you like to make this change? 😄

> [@zhixian82](https://github.com/zhixian82) would you like to make this change? 😄

ok， https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/pull/1754， PTAL

satisfaction_conditions: Acknowledgment that the API documentation should be updated to accurately reflect the actual behavior of the Replicas field
Clarification of the intended semantic meaning of the Replicas field in the context of the RayClusterReplicaSet
A resolution path that aligns the API definition with the actual implementation behavior

title: Forks and spawns (VS Code on httptap yields nothing)
body:
Built from src, ran the sysctl commands:

$ ./httptap -- /usr/bin/code
$

That's it. VS Code actually starts, but ps auxf tells me that the command I issued to cli calls a launcher or wrapper, the actual instance is initiated there. Can I make httptap follow the process invocation?

Notably, this instance of VSC won't see the net at all, the Extension browser will tell me that it is offline. U24.04, I ran the sysctl mods before.
author: jvenge

comments.body:
Hey - it looks like the issues is that httptap exits when the top-level process exits, leaving the "real" vscode stranded in an isolated network namespace with nobody to proxy traffic to the outside world. A simple workaround is this:

```bash
httptap -- bash -c "code; sleep infinity" 
```

What's happening here is that vscode forks and detaches itself as is standard for GUI apps. Luckily, that still doesn't let it escape from the network namespace that httptap creates. All that is needed is to force httptap's proxy code to keep running even when the direct subprocess returns, which can be done with "sleep infinity". You will have to hit ctrl+c manually to exit manually when you close down vscode.

Separately, for vscode you may want to add --ignore-certificate-errors because electron does not seem to pick up httptap's CA file. So the full invocation becomes

```bash
httptap -- bash -c "code --ignore-certificate-errors; sleep infinity" 
```

Amazingly, when I do this at my end, the vscode instance that starts does not accept any keyboard input! That's really crazy. Do you see that too? I have no idea why that would be.

But going back to the original issue, for your interest and for the benefit of others who come across this issue, you can reproduce the fork-to-background phenomenon in a more minimal way by running two levels of setsid like this:

```bash
$ httptap -- setsid setsid curl http://httpbin.org/get
curl: (6) Could not resolve host: httpbin.org
```

This only applies to programs that explicitly daemonize themselves (typically by forking, then putting themselves into a new process group, then forking again), not to programs that simply start normal subprocesses. httptap has no trouble with normal subprocess creation. For example:

```bash
$ httptap -- python -c 'import subprocess; subprocess.run(["curl", "http://httpbin.org/get"])'                 
---> GET http://httpbin.org/get
<--- 200 http://httpbin.org/get (285 bytes)
...
```

Interested to hear if this resolves your issue.

---

Just adding some further notes here from my own research. The fork-detach-fork thing that GUI apps do can be reproduced via python like this:

```bash
$ httptap -- python -c 'import os; import sys; import subprocess
if os.fork(): sys.exit()
os.setsid()
if os.fork(): sys.exit()
subprocess.run(["curl", "http://httpbin.org/get"])'
```

Output:
```
curl: (6) Could not resolve host: httpbin.org
```

In contrast, if the top-level process just sleeps long enough for the job to be done then it all works out perfectly:

```bash
$ httptap -- python -c 'import os; import sys; import subprocess; import time       
if os.fork(): time.sleep(1)
os.setsid()
if os.fork(): sys.exit()
subprocess.run(["curl", "http://httpbin.org/get"])'
---> GET http://httpbin.org/get
<--- 200 http://httpbin.org/get (285 bytes)
```

I think I should add a `--no-exit` argument to httptap that causes it to keep proxying until the user kills it with ctrl+c.

Appreciate your efforts. I cannot reproduce the keyboard issue, but on the other hand, while browsing and installing extensions the amount of reported sites amounts to zilch. This either means VSC does not relay http calls to the system or they get lost somehere else. I'll have to talk to the VSC poeple on this (or dissect the src). Or see if wireshark sees something that I don't here.

When I search extensions with vscode running under httptap, I do see the HTTP calls. For example searching "axolotl" in vscode under httptap gives me this output:

```
---> POST https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/_apis/public/gallery/extensionquery
<--- 200 https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/_apis/public/gallery/extensionquery (4332 bytes)
---> POST https://mobile.events.data.microsoft.com/OneCollector/1.0?cors=true&content-type=application/x-json-stream
<--- 200 https://mobile.events.data.microsoft.com/OneCollector/1.0?cors=true&content-type=application/x-json-stream (9 bytes)
---> GET https://kappadoo.gallerycdn.vsassets.io/extensions/kappadoo/axolotl-vsnote/0.1.1/1646479180048/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.Icons.Default
<--- 200 https://kappadoo.gallerycdn.vsassets.io/extensions/kappadoo/axolotl-vsnote/0.1.1/1646479180048/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Services.Icons.Default (7350 bytes)
---> POST https://mobile.events.data.microsoft.com/OneCollector/1.0?cors=true&content-type=application/x-json-stream
<--- 200 https://mobile.events.data.microsoft.com/OneCollector/1.0?cors=true&content-type=application/x-json-stream (9 bytes)
```

The invocation that I eventually came to, making use of the --no-exit flag that I just very recently merged to main, and using --no-new-user-namespace to work around the keyboard issue I had, is this:

```
sudo $(which httptap) --no-exit --no-new-user-namespace -- sudo -u $USER code --ignore-certificate-errors .
```

If you don't have the same keyboard issue, then you should be able to do (again, with the latest from main):

```
httptap --no-exit -- code --ignore-certificate-errors .
```

If it's working then right away when vscode starts you'll see some HTTP calls such as:
```
---> OPTIONS https://default.exp-tas.com/vscode/ab
<--- 204 https://default.exp-tas.com/vscode/ab (0 bytes)
---> GET https://update.code.visualstudio.com/api/update/linux-x64/stable/903b1e9d8990623e3d7da1df3d33db3e42d80eda
<--- 200 https://update.code.visualstudio.com/api/update/linux-x64/stable/903b1e9d8990623e3d7da1df3d33db3e42d80eda (430 bytes)
---> GET https://default.exp-tas.com/vscode/ab
<--- 200 https://default.exp-tas.com/vscode/ab (4184 bytes)
```

By the way, are you by any chance running vscode using snap? Might be worth installing via rpm or deb or tar.gz if you possibly can as I've had lots of issues running httptap with snap apps on account of the way that snap uses a lot of complex containerization tech that interacts quite badly with being run in an isolated network namespace.

Built lastest: the plain httptap ... call starts code but does not yield any http call tracking. 

The sudo call, however, makes it work, so yay, success. I just don't understand what makes it tick now.

This all is happening in a fresh install of ubuntu desktop 24.04LTS  in VirtualBox, so no idea if the virtual input devices add shenanigans in this particular scenario.

Good to hear!

The sudo call does it without creating a user namespace, which is a bit of containerization tech in the linux kernel that lets you create (among other things) network namespace without being root. There seems to be a lot of work happening in the kernel and elsewhere that changes where you can create user namespaces, and how they work, so I guess it's not surprising that excising that bit of tech and just going with sudo works.

The reason there are two sudo calls in there is that vscode refuses to run as root, so you have to sudo once to create the network namespace (the first sudo in the command), then sudo again to switch back to the original user to actually run vscode.

title: IPv6 support
body:
Connecting to sites which only have a AAAA record published does not work

EDIT: Looks like all that's missing is a route out, if I `./httptap bash` and then `ip r a 2000::/3 dev httptap` everything works as expected. Since it's a proxied connection the LLA fe80::/64 address on the interface is actually fine and it appears there's a working IPv6 stack in httptap
author: asdfjkluiop

comments.body: Thanks for reporting this @asdfjkluiop. Yes, httptap does have an ipv6 stack. I just merged a PR that should set up this route automatically. If you happen to have time, would you ming building from source on main and checking that this change resolves this?

Hey alex, thanks for the update. It works however there's a bug that occurs with it. If the domain in question lacks an A record(the only time this update is needed) httptap will work as expected now but erroneously prints
> error performing DNS query: the default resolver said: lookup example.com. on nameserver:53: no such host, sending response with empty answer

and then proceed to correctly trace the connection.

EDIT: interestingly enough this does not happen with v0.0.8 if I manually add the route, it's something introduced between then and now
@asdfjkluiop hey, thanks so much for testing this out. Good to hear that it works. Yep that's output is indeed erroneous - will fix that up shortly.

satisfaction_conditions: Automatic configuration of IPv6 routing for proxied connections
Successful connection to IPv6-only domains (AAAA records without A records)

title: `error creating network namespace: operation not permitted`
body:
Hey there,

Thanks for putting together this tool!

I tried it out and it didn't work for me, any ideas what could be wrong? I'm on Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS.

```
(base) vadi@framework:~$ echo $GOPATH 
/home/vadi/.go
(base) vadi@framework:~$ go install github.com/monasticacademy/httptap@latest
go: downloading github.com/monasticacademy/httptap v0.0.8
[...]

error creating network namespace: operation not permitted
(base) vadi@framework:~$ 
```
author: vadi2

comments.body: i think vadi user don't have enough capabilities to create network namespace. this tool needs to create TUN to capture packages.
Interesting! For context, I'm the administrator user on my laptop - and the only user.
So can u try run it with `sudo`?

Related issue: when running in Docker, `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` is required. Without it, you'll see this error:
```shell
$ docker run --rm -it alpine:latest ash -c 'apk add -q curl && curl -sL https://github.com/monasticacademy/httptap/releases/latest/download/httptap_linux_$(uname -m | sed -e "s/^aarch64$/arm64/" -e "s/^i.86$/i386/").tar.gz | tar xzf - && ./httptap'
error re-executing ourselves in a new user namespace: fork/exec /proc/self/exe: operation not permitted
```

>

> (base) vadi@framework:~$ 
> ```

Same here, Ubuntu 24 LTS. Running as non-root user. With sudo it works though.
My guess it has something to do with Ubuntu's AppArmor, but I cannot reboot right now to disable it completely. Both `aa-disable` and `aa-complain` on httptap binary give an error.

Wow, this is very interesting.

Just for background: httptap first moves itself to a new user namespace, then within that user namespace (and as the root user within that user namespace) it creates a network namespace.

In general you have to be root to create a network namespace, but you can create a user namespace without being root.

Within docker, a user actually has fewer capabilities than a typical "non-root user" on a typical distro. To run httptap within docker then unfortunately requires --cap-add SYS_ADMIN. It also requires mounting /dev/net/tun into the docker container (again, unfortunate, would love to find a workaround):

```
	mkdir -p .build
	go build -o .build/httptap
	docker run \
		--interactive \
		--tty \
		--rm \
		--volume .:/src \
		--workdir /src \
		--cap-add SYS_ADMIN \
		--device /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun \
		mcr.microsoft.com/vscode/devcontainers/base:ubuntu \
		.build/httptap --no-overlay -- curl -so /dev/null https://www.monasticacademy.org
---> GET https://www.monasticacademy.org/
<--- 200 https://www.monasticacademy.org/ (34135 bytes)
```

The same thing works with alpine:

```
mkdir -p .build
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o .build/httptap
docker run \
	--interactive \
	--tty \
	--rm \
	--volume .:/src \
	--workdir /src \
	--cap-add SYS_ADMIN \
	--device /dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun \
	alpine/curl \
	.build/httptap --no-overlay -- curl -so /dev/null https://www.monasticacademy.org
---> GET https://www.monasticacademy.org/
<--- 200 https://www.monasticacademy.org/ (34135 bytes)
```

However none of this addresses @vadi2's original question. It's very strange that this doesn't work. @vadi2, just for testing, would you try this?

```bash
sudo httptap --no-new-user-namespace -- curl https://mudlet.org
```

Here it is:

```
sudo /home/vadi/.go/bin/httptap --no-new-user-namespace -- curl https://mudlet.org
---> GET https://mudlet.org/
<--- 301 https://mudlet.org/ (0 bytes)
```

> Related issue: when running in Docker, `--security-opt seccomp=unconfined` is required.

Extremely interesting. This may be the cause of several mysterious issues. Perhaps @vadi2 you have seccomp enabled system-wide and that's what's causing this?

Might be the cause of #18 also

---

OK seems like it at least correctly intercepts the request when running as root. @vadi2 could you try running again as non-root, without `--no-new-user-namespace`, and running `sudo dmesg -W` in a separate terminal while doing so? > i think vadi user don't have enough capabilities to create network namespace. this tool needs to create TUN to capture packages.

If this refers to the "You need access to /dev/net/tun" part at the bottom of the README, perhaps it is better to put this right after "To run httptap you do not need to be the root user"?

I tried to chown /dev/net/tun to the current regular user, but the error persisted

> My guess it has something to do with Ubuntu's AppArmor

This is from the output of dmesg:

    [24346.654781] audit: type=1400 audit(1738854203.795:431): apparmor="AUDIT" operation="userns_create" class="namespace" info="Userns create - transitioning profile" profile="unconfined" pid=99139 comm="httptap" requested="userns_create" target="unprivileged_userns"


> In general you have to be root to create a network namespace, but you can create a user namespace without being root.

Is this related? https://askubuntu.com/questions/1511854/how-to-permanently-disable-ubuntus-new-apparmor-user-namespace-creation-restric

Wow, looks like unpriveleged user namespaces (which httptap uses) were [turned off by default in Ubuntu 23.10](https://ubuntu.com/blog/ubuntu-23-10-restricted-unprivileged-user-namespaces). It seems that if I ship an apparmor profile with httptap, then it can still work by default. However you can turn off this feature with the following:

```shell
    sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=0
    sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
```

@vadi2 would you mind trying the above commands and seeing if httptap then works out of the box on ubuntu 24.04? If you want, you can re-enable this feature with 

```shell
    sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=1
    sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=1
```

More info on what this is doing at the link above

$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=0
$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
$ ./httptap -- curl http://1.1.1.1
error setting up overlay: error mounting overlay filesystem at /etc
("lowerdir=/etc,upperdir=/tmp/overlay-3520647796/layer,workdir=/tmp/overlay-3520647796/work"):
invalid argument
$ sudo ./httptap -- curl http://1.1.1.1
error setting up overlay: error mounting overlay filesystem at /etc
("lowerdir=/etc,upperdir=/tmp/overlay-3520647796/layer,workdir=/tmp/overlay-3520647796/work"):
invalid argument
$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined = 1
$ sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 1

Ubuntu 24.04.1 x86_64

Yes, I can confirm that it works:

```
$     sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined=0
    sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0
kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_unconfined = 0
kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns = 0
(base) vadi@framework:~$ httptap -- curl https://mudlet.org
---> GET https://mudlet.org/
<--- 301 https://mudlet.org/ (0 bytes)
```
setting the app armor params made it work. Though i must say i have done a lot of AI assisted fiddling around this so it may be a combination of those params with something else. `Ubuntu 24.04.1 LTS`

satisfaction_conditions: A method to enable httptap to create network namespaces on Ubuntu 24.04 without requiring root privileges for every execution
Identification of the root cause as Ubuntu's AppArmor restrictions on unprivileged user namespaces
A concrete configuration change that addresses the AppArmor restrictions specific to Ubuntu 24.04

title: `RequestExtra.CloseSSEStream` function field breaks JSON serialization of request types
body:
**Describe the bug**
The `CloseSSEStream` field added to the `RequestExtra` is a function type, which causes `json.Marshal` to fail on any `ServerRequest`-derived type. This breaks common use cases like logging, debugging output, or persisting protocol requests.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Use `json.Marshal` on any of the `ServerRequest` types

**Expected behavior**
I should be able to marshal any request type to JSON

**Additional context**
I'd be happy to open a fix to this issue if appropriate. I believe all is needed is to add a `json:"-"` tag.
author: Cali0707

comments.body:
I don't think it's intended that the Request types be JSON serializable. They're an encapsulation of the incoming request context, including the session and RequestExtra. If they were serializable before, it's a coincidence: certainly we made no guarantees that the Session be serializable, and it's an exported field.

Notably, the request is NOT the protocol request.

I think a better solution for your use-case would be to actually store the raw protocol request (a `jsonrpc.Request`). on the `mcp.Request` type.
Ah okay that was a misunderstanding on my end then.

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of the intended design and serialization capabilities of the Request types
Guidance on the appropriate alternative approach for persisting or logging request data
Explanation of the distinction between protocol requests and the Request wrapper types

title: [FEATURE] 能否新增agent端docker的安装方式
body: 感谢！
author: TingTing1990

comments.body: https://github.com/komari-monitor/komari-agent/pkgs/container/komari-agent

> agent

多谢，请问在agent机器上跑这个docker需要增加怎样的参数才能对应主控上的服务器，没找到文档！

---

已经先用脚本！

```
services:
  komari-agent:
    image: ghcr.io/komari-monitor/komari-agent:latest
    command: -e 你的面板地址
    container_name: komari-agent
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - /etc/os-release:/etc/os-release:ro
      - /proc:/host/proc:ro
    environment:
      AGENT_AUTO_DISCOVERY_KEY: "abc"           # 自动发现密钥
      AGENT_DISABLE_AUTO_UPDATE: true           # 禁用自动更新
      AGENT_DISABLE_WEB_SSH: true               # 禁用远程控制（web ssh 和 rce）
      AGENT_TOKEN: "abc"                        # Token
      AGENT_INTERVAL:  1                        # 数据采集间隔，单位秒
      AGENT_IGNORE_UNSAFE_CERT: true            # 忽略不安全的证书
      AGENT_MAX_RETRIES: 10                     # 最大重试次数
      AGENT_RECONNECT_INTERVAL: 1               # 重连间隔，单位秒
      AGENT_INFO_REPORT_INTERVAL: 1             # 基础信息上报间隔，单位分钟
      AGENT_INCLUDE_NICS: "ens1"                # 仅统计网卡，逗号分隔的网卡名称列表，支持通配符
      AGENT_EXCLUDE_NICS: "ens2"                # 统计时排除的网卡，逗号分隔的网卡名称列表，支持通配符
      AGENT_INCLUDE_MOUNTPOINTS: "/home,/opt"   # 磁盘统计的包含挂载点列表，使用分号分隔
      AGENT_MONTH_ROTATE: 0                     # 流量统计的月份重置日期（0表示禁用）
      AGENT_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_ID: "id"           # Cloudflare Access Client ID
      AGENT_CF_ACCESS_CLIENT_SECRET: "secret"   # Cloudflare Access Client Secret
      AGENT_MEMORY_INCLUDE_CACHE: false         # 包括缓存/缓冲区的内存使用情况
      AGENT_MEMORY_REPORT_RAW_USED: false       # 使用原始内存使用情况报告
      AGENT_CUSTOM_DNS: "114.114.114.114"       # 使用的自定义DNS服务器
      AGENT_ENABLE_GPU: false                   # 启用详细GPU监控
      AGENT_SHOW_WARNING: false                 # Windows 上显示安全警告，作为子进程运行一次
      AGENT_CUSTOM_IPV4: ""                     # 自定义 IPv4 地址
      AGENT_CUSTOM_IPV6: ""                     # 自定义 IPv6 地址
      AGENT_GET_IP_ADDR_FROM_NIC: true          # 从网卡获取IP地址
      AGENT_CONFIG_FILE: ""                     # JSON配置文件路径
    restart: unless-stopped
```

comments.body:
下面是问的AI的 GROK
Komari Moniter  服务器在墙外   节点有在墙内的， 使用了websocket 协议传输数据， 是否有被墙的风险？






### Komari Monitor 概述
Komari Monitor 是一个轻量级的、自托管的服务器监控工具，主要用于监控服务器性能指标（如 CPU、内存、磁盘等）。它基于 Go 语言开发，支持 Docker 部署和二进制文件运行，通常通过 Web 界面访问（默认端口 25774）。从公开信息看，它本身是一个监控应用，并不内置代理或翻墙功能，但用户可能在其基础上自定义配置网络传输，例如使用 WebSocket 协议来传输监控数据。

### 场景分析：服务器在墙外、节点在墙内、使用 WebSocket 传输数据
- **墙外服务器**：指 Komari Monitor 的主服务器部署在境外（如海外云服务器），负责处理和显示监控数据。
- **墙内节点**：指监控的服务器或代理节点位于中国境内（墙内），这些节点需要向墙外服务器上报数据。
- **WebSocket 协议传输**：WebSocket 是一种全双工通信协议，通常建立在 HTTP/HTTPS 之上（默认端口 80/443），数据帧加密传输。它常用于实时数据推送（如监控指标），但在墙内-墙外场景下，可能被用作数据隧道（类似于 V2Ray 或 Trojan 的 WebSocket + TLS 配置）。

这种配置本质上是墙内节点通过 WebSocket 向墙外服务器发送加密数据流，类似于一些翻墙工具的伪装方式（流量看起来像正常 HTTPS）。

### 是否有被墙的风险？
**是的，有被墙的风险，但风险程度中等，取决于具体实现和流量模式。** 中国防火墙（GFW）不会直接针对 WebSocket 协议封锁（因为它兼容现有 HTTP 基础设施，且常用于合法 Web 应用如聊天或推送），但会通过被动流量分析和主动探测来识别异常模式。以下是详细分析：

#### 1. **GFW 的检测机制**
   - **被动流量分析**：GFW 自 2021 年起能实时检测完全加密流量（如 WebSocket over TLS）。它分析数据包长度、模式和字节分布：
     - 如果前几个字节符合 HTTP/TLS 格式，GFW 可能“豁免”连接（允许通过），因为 WebSocket 握手以 HTTP Upgrade 开始，看起来像正常 HTTPS。
     - 但如果后续数据帧显示异常（如持续小包高频传输、固定长度模式，或非标准 HTTPS 流量），GFW 会触发阻塞。研究显示，这影响 Shadowsocks、VMess 等协议，而 WebSocket + TLS 类似。
   - **主动探测**：GFW 会模拟客户端连接你的墙外服务器，检查响应。如果探测到代理行为（如返回特定错误或不匹配正常 Web 服务器），会发送 TCP RST 包中断连接，并封锁 IP/端口。
   - **SNI 检测**：在 TLS 握手中，服务器名称（SNI）明文传输。如果 SNI 指向墙外域名，且流量异常，GFW 可能拉黑 IP。

#### 2. **具体风险点**
   | 风险因素 | 描述 | 概率（低/中/高） | 为什么针对你的场景？ |
   |----------|------|------------------|---------------------|
   | **流量模式异常** | WebSocket 常产生持久连接和小包数据流，与正常 HTTPS（请求-响应）不同。 | 中 | 监控数据上报可能形成固定周期模式，易被识别为“隧道流量”。 |
   | **多客户端连接** | 如果多个墙内节点同时连接墙外服务器 >5 个，持续几小时，GFW 易封锁 IPv4。 | 高 | Komari Monitor 可能涉及多节点上报，放大风险。 |
   | **端口暴露** | 默认 WebSocket 用 80/443，但自定义端口易被 DPI（深度包检测）捕获。 | 中 | 如果非标准端口，防火墙直接阻挡。 |
   | **无 TLS 加密** | 纯 ws://（非 wss://）流量明文，易被 DPI 扫描关键词。 | 高 | 推荐始终用 wss://（WebSocket Secure）。 |
   | **IP 黑名单** | 墙外服务器 IP 如果被探测为代理，全国墙内访问全封。 | 中 | 单 IP 依赖高风险；多 IP 轮换可缓解。 |

   - **历史案例**：类似 V2Ray/Trojan 的 WebSocket 配置曾有效，但 2021-2023 年 GFW 更新后，许多服务器 IP 被批量封锁。研究显示，GFW 能 100% 检测“TLS 内 TLS”模式。

#### 3. **缓解建议**
   - **加密与伪装**：
     - 始终用 **wss:// (WebSocket + TLS)**，并用有效证书（如 Let's Encrypt）。这让流量 99% 像正常 HTTPS。
     - 集成 uTLS 库模拟浏览器 TLS 指纹，规避 SNI 检测。
   - **流量优化**：
     - 随机化数据包大小/间隔，避免固定模式（e.g., 用工具分片 Client Hello）。
     - 限制连接数/时长，轮换 IP（用 Cloudflare 等 CDN 隐藏真实服务器）。
   - **协议增强**：
     - 如果 Komari Monitor 支持，结合 VMess 或 Trojan 协议（WebSocket 作为传输层），添加额外混淆。
     - 测试工具：用 V2RayNG 等客户端模拟，检查墙内连接稳定性。
   - **备用方案**：
     - 用 HTTP/2 或 gRPC 替代 WebSocket，流量更隐蔽。
     - 部署墙内中继节点（但增加延迟）。
     - 监控 GFW 更新：定期检查 IP 是否被封（工具如 greatfire.org）。

#### 4. **总体评估**
   - **短期风险低**：如果流量少、伪装好，短期内不易被封（WebSocket 兼容性高）。
   - **长期风险中高**：GFW 持续进化，2025 年检测更智能。建议从小规模测试开始，观察丢包/连接失败率。
   - **法律提醒**：在中国，使用此类配置传输数据需遵守法规，避免敏感内容。

如果提供更多细节（如具体 WebSocket 配置或 Komari 版本），我可以给出更精确建议。
如果只是域名被墙可以额外绑定一个备用域名即可 如果是ip被阻断目前无法直连通过任何协议链接 请自行使用cdn服务
谢谢大佬， 我是先反代了HTTPS，然后套了CF ， 应该没什么问题了。

satisfaction_conditions: Guidance on mitigating domain-level blocking risks for cross-border WebSocket connections
Clarification on the distinction between domain blocking and IP blocking scenarios
Validation that HTTPS/TLS layer protection is appropriate for the use case

title: [Bug]: `cu terminal` fails when using secrets
body:
### What happened?

When I have a secret set in cu environment, I'm unable to shell into the terminal. I receive the following:

```
! failed to start service: start container: secret argon2:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: not
  found
╰─✘ exec /bin/bash --rcfile /cu/rc.sh -i 0.0s ERROR
  ! start container: secret argon2:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: not found
```

Works fine as soon as I remove the secret. I've tried both `op://` && `env://` style secrets.

### Version

```shell
0.3.1
```
author: andrewthauer

comments.body:
the "failed to start service" part of this error message is suspicious here... last i checked [services aren't restored on environment Load](https://github.com/dagger/container-use/blob/f83f6550c889eb8ef6431276d33a16b895f48167/environment/environment.go#L81) so i'm not sure what service it's failing to start...

---

ah, it must be starting a service through a service binding?

repro'd this with a service that depends on a secret. couple extra properties that are relevant:
1. we don't seem to hit the bug prior to introducing a service to the equation -- ie you can still do `cu terminal` and the secret will be in there.
2. once the bug has been repro'd with with a service involved, the error is "sticky" -- doing the service-less repro will start failing with the same "failed to start service" message, almost as though cu is bringing service bindings across environments somehow. the secret ID in the string doesn't change either.

so this works:
```sh
cu config secret set TEST_SECRET env://TEST_SECRET
export TEST_SECRET=lul1
claude 'create an environment and echo the value of TEST_SECRET, then do echo $TEST_SECRET | base64'
echo <pasted_b64> | base64 -D # gives lul1
cu terminal <env id>
```

but once you do
```sh
cu config secret set TEST_SECRET env://TEST_SECRET
export TEST_SECRET=lul1
claude 'add an nginx service to the environment that depends on the value of TEST_SECRET'
cu terminal <env id>
```

then any (new?) environment with a secret in it seems to no longer be `cu terminal`-able... suspiciously, i've also got this weird behavior going on, which looks like env infos are getting mixed up:

```
cu list
ID                 TITLE                                      CREATED       UPDATED
desired-cockatoo   Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
artistic-sculpin   Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
able-satyr         Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
hardy-jawfish      Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
fine-mosquito      Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
complete-mutt      Development environment for container-us…  1 minute ago  1 minute ago
```

(im likely describing 2 separate bugs...)

---

ok [i fixed the other bug](https://github.com/dagger/container-use/pull/240), still not entirely sure what's going on with the secrets thing...

another interesting piece of evidence, though: `docker kill`ing the dagger engine makes the "sticky" `failed to start service: start container: secret argon2:XXX: not found` unstick...

I had terminal work once or twice but couldn't figure out why. Most of the time it does not. That said. your fix does seem relevant as I'm trying to get a custom base image working and it's failing a lot. Not being able to terminal with secrets is making this even more challenging to troubleshoot issues.

---

I also realized I'll get the same errors if I re-use an existing environment. The environment will be re-used, but once it tries to run other commands the tool calls will error out with something like:

```
Error: failed to run command: failed to get exit code: input: container.from.withWorkdir.withEnvVariable.withEnvVariable.withEnvVariable.withSecretVariable.withSecretVariable.wi
     thSecretVariable.withExec.withServiceBinding.withDirectory.withExec.withExec.withExec.withExec.withExec.withExec.withExec.exitCode secret
     argon2:xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx: not found
```

I believe this is due to the service references stored in the environment -- `cu terminal` is trying to bring them back up, but the secrets no longer exist.

Attempted a fix in https://github.com/dagger/container-use/pull/244 -- rather than having services define their own secrets, they now re-use the environment secrets instead
Thanks! I built from source and was able to terminal into my environment. The env also had a PG service setup as well. So, yes seems this particular issue is resolved.

A solution that allows secrets and services to coexist without causing terminal access failures

title: Help with CEL for spec.containers.envFrom
body:
Hi, great project!

I've hit a snag with the following problem:

I want my container to have an optional envFrom with exactly one configMap and one secretRef, to give the user the option of specifying a configMap and a secret.

```yaml
apiVersion: kro.run/v1alpha1
kind: ResourceGraphDefinition
metadata:
  name: my-application
spec:
  schema:
    apiVersion: v1alpha1
    kind: MyApplication
    spec:
      additionalEnv:
        enabled: boolean | default=false
        secretName: string | default=""
        configMapName: string | default=""
```

My template:

```yaml
- id: appDeployment
      template:
        apiVersion: apps/v1
        kind: Deployment
        metadata:
          name: "${schema.spec.name}"
          labels:
            app: "${schema.spec.name}"
        spec:
          replicas: ${schema.spec.replicas}
          selector:
            matchLabels:
              app: "${schema.spec.name}"
          template:
            metadata:
              labels:
                app: "${schema.spec.name}"
            spec:
              imagePullSecrets: ${schema.spec.imagePullSecrets}
              containers:
                - name: "${schema.spec.name}"
                  image: "${schema.spec.image.repository}:${schema.spec.image.tag}"
                  imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
                  ports:
                    - containerPort: 8080
                      name: http
                  envFrom: ${schema.spec.additionalEnv.enabled ? [{"configMapRef":{"name":schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName}},{"secretRef":{"name":schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName}}]:[]}
```

I will add the ConfigMap and the Secret as an external reference.

The problem is envFrom. 

How would the CEL expression look like to get?:

```yaml
envFrom:
          - configMapRef:
              name: ${schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName}
          - secretRef:
              name: ${schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName}
```

If there is a more elegant solution for this, I would be open to it. :-)

I want to add an option for the user to specify own additional ENVs through config maps and secrets.
author: rubiktubik

comments.body:
Hi! You’re very close already 🙂

A clean way to handle this is to build envFrom by conditionally concatenating lists, instead of using a single ternary. That way, each entry is only added if its value is present, and you avoid empty refs.

For example:

envFrom: ${
  (schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName != "" ?
    [{"configMapRef": {"name": schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName}}] : [])
  +
  (schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName != "" ?
    [{"secretRef": {"name": schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName}}] : [])
}


This results in:

both entries when both are set

only one entry if only a config map or secret is provided

an empty list when neither is set

Because of this, the enabled flag isn’t strictly necessary — the presence of configMapName / secretName already expresses intent — but you can keep it if it’s useful for UX.

Hope this helps, happy to clarify further if needed 🙂

Thank you! That sounds like a better solution than mine. :-)
 I'll try it out and let you know how it went.

@rubiktubik You’re welcome! Glad it helped 🙂
Feel free to reach out if you run into any issues or have follow-up questions while trying it out.

I'am getting the following error when applying the rgd:


`failed to validate node "appDeployment": type mismatch in resource "appDeployment" at path "spec.template.spec.containers[0].envFrom": expression " (schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName != \"\" ? [{\"configMapRef\":{\"name\":schema.spec.additionalEnv.configMapName}}]:[]) + (schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName != \"\" ? [{\"secretRef\":{\"name\":schema.spec.additionalEnv.secretName}}]:[]) " returns type "list(map(string, map(string, string)  ))" but expected "list(__type_appDeployment.spec.template.spec.containers.@idx.envFrom.@idx)": list element type incompatible: map value incompatible with struct field "prefix": type kind mismatch: got "map(string, string)", expected "string"`


The types seems to be wrong but it look corrects to me.

title: Could has() macro be supported in status field expressions?
body:
### Feature Description

**Problem Statement**:

I'm working with a ResourceGraphDefinition that includes two mutually exclusive resources (`local` and `remote`), where only one is created based on input conditions. I'm trying to expose the status of whichever resource exists through the custom resource's status fields, but I'm encountering a type-checking error when using the `has()` macro in status expressions.

The error I'm seeing is:

```
failed to build resourcegraphdefinition 'k0smotrondockercluster.cluster.example.com': 
failed to build OpenAPI schema for instance status: 
failed to type-check status expression "has(local) ? local.status.infrastructureReady : remote.status.infrastructureReady" 
at path "clusterStatus.infrastructureReady": 
ERROR: <input>:1:5: invalid argument to has() macro
 | has(local) ? local.status.infrastructureReady : remote.status.infrastructureReady
 | ....^
```

Interestingly, the `has()` macro works perfectly in `includeWhen` conditions:

```yaml
includeWhen:
- ${!(has(schema.spec.baseCluster) && has(schema.spec.baseCluster.kubeconfigRef))}
```

However, when I try to use it in status field expressions, the type-checker rejects it:

```yaml
status:
  clusterStatus:
    infrastructureReady: '${has(local) ? local.status.infrastructureReady : remote.status.infrastructureReady}'
```

**Proposed Solution**:

Would it be possible to support the `has()` macro in status field expressions? This would allow conditional status field selection based on which resource exists at runtime, similar to how `includeWhen` conditions work.

The use case is: when you have mutually exclusive resources in a ResourceGraph, being able to conditionally reference their status fields would provide a consistent status interface for the custom resource, regardless of which variant was created.

**Alternatives Considered**:

I've considered a few alternatives, but none seem as clean:

1. Creating both resources and having empty status fields for the non-existent one (doesn't work due to `includeWhen`)
2. Duplicating the entire ResourceGraphDefinition for each variant (maintenance burden)
3. Using a different status structure that doesn't directly map to the underlying resource (breaks the natural abstraction)

I'm curious if there's a recommended pattern I'm missing for this scenario.

**Additional Context**:

comments.body: Is this issue currently open for contribution? If so, I’d be happy to take a look and work on supporting has() in status field expressions (or help explore an alternative pattern if that’s preferred).

This issue occurs because the `has()` macro in CEL (Common Expression Language) is designed to check for the existence of fields within an object, but it cannot be used to check for the existence of a top-level resource ID defined in your `ResourceGraphDefinition`.

The type-checker fails because it treats `local` and `remote` as variables that might not be defined in the global scope of the status expression, leading to the "invalid argument" error.

To achieve this in a way that passes the `kro` type-checker today, you should use the input schema values (which drive the `includeWhen` logic) as the source of truth for your ternary operators in the status section.

You can use the following snippet for your status expressions:

```yaml
status:
  clusterStatus:
    infrastructureReady: '${!(has(schema.spec.baseCluster) && has(schema.spec.baseCluster.kubeconfigRef)) ? local.status.infrastructureReady : remote.status.infrastructureReady}'
    # Repeat this pattern for other fields

```

### Why this works:

1. **Scope:** The `schema` object is always available in the global scope for status expressions, making `has(schema.spec.baseCluster)` valid for the type-checker.
2. **Deterministic Logic:** Since `local` and `remote` are mutually exclusive based on that exact schema condition, the status mapping remains safe. Even though one resource won't exist at runtime, the CEL evaluator handles the conditional branch without attempting to access the missing resource's status.

### Recommendation for `kro`:

Supporting `has(resource_id)` directly in status expressions would definitely be a cleaner abstraction. However, until that is supported, using the schema-based conditional is the standard pattern to avoid type-checking errors.

I’ll keep an eye on this as it would be a great quality-of-life improvement for the `ResourceGraphDefinition` API.

This is due to a CEL limitation - the has() macro only accepts field selections, not identifiers ([source](https://github.com/google/cel-go/blob/v0.23.2/parser/macro.go#L401-L406)). To support this, we'd need a new feature request to expose a `resources` map or add a custom `exists()` function to kro's CEL environment. I haven't given this much thought yet, but I'm not sure how it would impact the dependency graph. @kahirokunn can you please open a seperate github issue for to request the `exist()` function/macro feature?

satisfaction_conditions: A method to conditionally reference status fields from mutually exclusive resources in ResourceGraphDefinition status expressions
An explanation of why the has() macro fails in status field expressions when checking for resource IDs
A working pattern that passes the kro type-checker for conditional status field selection
Acknowledgment of whether native support for checking resource existence in status expressions is feasible or planned

title: Title: Static CEL evaluation fails with `no such key` for optional `schema.spec` fields (even when using `has()`)
body:
### Description

<!-- Please craft a detailed description of the documentation issue or suggestion -->
<!-- Below are some suggestions but feel free to modify or remove them -->

**Observed Behavior**:
When an optional field on `schema.spec` is accessed from a static CEL expression, the runtime fails with a `no such key` error even when using `has()` (or the optional `?` accessor).
In my case, `spec.kubeconfigRef` is defined as an optional object in the SimpleSchema, but when I omit it in the Instance, the `ResourceGraphDefinitionRuntime` fails during static variable evaluation with:

> failed evaluating expression has(schema.spec.kubeconfigRef) ? [] : [{"name": "kubeconfigRef", "value": schema.spec.kubeconfigRef}]: no such key: kubeconfigRef

As a result, the `GraphResolved` and `Ready` conditions on the Instance are set to `ResolutionFailed`, and reconciliation does not proceed.

**Expected Behavior**:
- Optional fields on `schema.spec` should be safe to access from static CEL expressions using `has(schema.spec.someField)` (and ideally `schema.spec.?someField`) without causing a `no such key` runtime error when the field is absent in the Instance.
- In the example below, if `spec.kubeconfigRef` is omitted in the Instance, I would expect:
  - `has(schema.spec.kubeconfigRef)` to evaluate to `false` without error, and
  - `topology.variables` to be set to `[]` (empty list), with `GraphResolved=True` and normal reconciliation.

**Reproduction Steps** (Please include `ResourceGraphDefinition` and `Instances` files):

1. Apply a `ResourceGraphDefinition` that defines an optional `kubeconfigRef` on `schema.spec` and uses it in a static CEL expression for `Cluster.spec.topology.variables`.

  ```yaml
   apiVersion: kro.run/v1alpha1
   kind: ResourceGraphDefinition
   metadata:
     name: k0smotrondockercluster.cluster.test.io
   spec:
     schema:
       group: cluster.test.io
       apiVersion: v1alpha1
       kind: K0smotronDockerCluster
       types:
         KubeconfigRef:
           name: string | required=true
           namespace: string | required=true
       spec:
         clusterclassName: string | required=true
         k0sVersion: string | required=true pattern="^v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\+k0s\.[0-9]+$"
         controlPlaneReplicas: integer | required=true
         machineDeploymentReplicas: integer | required=true
         podCIDR: string | default="192.168.0.0/16"
         serviceCIDR: string | default="10.128.0.0/12"

         # Optional kubeconfigRef (object)
         kubeconfigRef: KubeconfigRef

         template:
           metadata:
             labels: "map[string]string | required=true"

     resources:
       - id: cluster
         template:
           apiVersion: cluster.x-k8s.io/v1beta1
           kind: Cluster
           metadata:
             name: ${schema.metadata.name}
             namespace: ${schema.metadata.namespace}
           spec:
             topology:
               class: ${schema.spec.clusterclassName}
               version: ${schema.spec.k0sVersion}
               controlPlane:
                 replicas: ${schema.spec.controlPlaneReplicas}
               workers:
                 machineDeployments:
                   - class: default-worker
                     name: md-0
                     replicas: ${schema.spec.machineDeploymentReplicas}

               # Static CEL expression that should be safe when kubeconfigRef is absent
               variables: '${has(schema.spec.kubeconfigRef) ? [{"name": "kubeconfigRef", "value": schema.spec.kubeconfigRef}] : []}'
  ```

   2. Create an Instance **without** `spec.kubeconfigRef`:

  ```yaml
   apiVersion: cluster.test.io/v1alpha1
   kind: K0smotronDockerCluster
   metadata:
     name: pmc
     namespace: pmc
   spec:
     clusterclassName: k0smotron-docker-md
     controlPlaneReplicas: 1
     k0sVersion: v1.34.2+k0s.0
     machineDeploymentReplicas: 1
     podCIDR: 192.168.0.0/16
     serviceCIDR: 10.128.0.0/12
     template:
       metadata:
         labels:
           hello: world
  ```

   3. Wait for the `K0smotronDockerCluster` Instance to be reconciled by Kro.
4. Observe that the Instance status contains `GraphResolved=False` with a `ResolutionFailed` reason and a `no such key: kubeconfigRef` error originating from static CEL evaluation of the `variables` expression.

**Versions**:
- kro version: `v0.7.0`
- Kubernetes Version (`kubectl version`): _please fill in (e.g., v1.xx.y)_

**Involved Controllers**:
- Kro controller managing `K0smotronDockerCluster` ResourceGraphDefinition
- Cluster API `Cluster` controller (for the `Cluster.cluster.x-k8s.io` resource)

**Error Logs**:
# From Instance status.conditions (GraphResolved / Ready):
failed to create runtime resource graph definition: failed to evaluate
static variables: failed evaluating expression has(schema.spec.kubeconfigRef) ? [] : [{"name": "kubeconfigRef", "value": schema.spec.kubeconfigRef}]: no such

body:
I have the following situation:

```default
git who table -l
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│Author                          Last Edit   Commits   Files        Lines (+/-)│
├──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│Bobby Foo                       3 weeks ago     316     228   17,168 /   3,171│
│Foo, Bobby                      3 weeks ago     301     109   11,487 /   3,946│
│Tom the Horse                   3 weeks ago     103     156    7,788 /   7,633│
│the Horse, Tom                  2 weeks ago      22      74    6,806 /   3,918│
│...8 more...                                                                  │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

As you can see, we have 2 users which show up twice each. The somewhat weird reason is, that we authenticate to Gitlab using LDAP, which sometimes reports us as `prename name` and sometimes as `name, prename`.

For instance:

git who table -l -mergeuser "Bobby Foo+Foo, Bobby"

│Author                          Last Edit   Commits   Files        Lines (+/-)│

└──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

title: main() function logic not executed, but top-level invocation not allowed — trapped in execution dead zone
body:
## Summary

There's a behavior inconsistency when wrapping shell scripts for Bunster compilation:

1. If I place all logic inside a `main()` function but do **not** call it, the compiled binary executes nothing.
2. If I attempt to call `main` at the top level (i.e. outside of any function), the compiler fails with the error:


## Example

Input script:

```sh
#! /bin/sh

main() {
    echo "success replace!" 
    echo "Current directory: $(pwd)"
    echo "List hidden files:" 
    ls -al ~/.config 
    echo "Print \$PATH variable:" 
    echo "$PATH" > 1.log 
    echo "Escaped quotes: He said, \"Hello world!\""
}

main
```
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build /tmp/a_wrap.sh -o ./test   
Error:  main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.

## Expected Behavior
Either Bunster should automatically invoke main() as an entry point if present;

Or it should allow top-level function calls for execution purposes;

Alternatively, support a documented convention (e.g. __bunster_run()) that the compiler will automatically invoke.

## Environment
Bunster version: v0.13.0

Go version: go 1.23.8 linux/amd64

OS: Linux container (Debian)

## Suggestions
Add documentation on how to correctly define an entry point.

Consider relaxing global scope restrictions for main() invocation.

Or provide a flag/config to designate the function to invoke at runtime.

Thanks for the great project—this tool has tremendous potential if this blocker gets addressed!
author: maytom2016

comments.body:
## Attempts to follow documentation

After reading the official documentation [here](https://bunster.netlify.app/features/groups-and-subshells), I tried grouping the logic using curly braces as a command group:

```sh
{
    echo "success replace!"
    echo "Current directory: $(pwd)"
    echo "List hidden files:"
    ls -al ~/.config
    echo "Print \$PATH variable:"
    echo "$PATH" > 1.log
    echo "Escaped quotes: He said, \"Hello world!\""
}
```
or this
```sh
(
    echo "success replace!"
    echo "Current directory: $(pwd)"
    echo "List hidden files:"
    ls -al ~/.config
    echo "Print \$PATH variable:"
    echo "$PATH" > 1.log
    echo "Escaped quotes: He said, \"Hello world!\""
)
```
But bunster build test1.sh -o ./test still fails with the same error:
main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.


---

i got it,please look this
```
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test  
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o testsh
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o testsh
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test.sh
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test.sh
Error:  main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ bunster build test1.sh -o test.sh
Error:  main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.
user@c0401f469bb7:~$ ls
test.sh  testsh  test  test1.sh
```
Despite specifying test1.sh as the input and test.sh as output, the compiler interpreted test.sh as a second input script, causing a semantic error:
```
main.sh(0:0): semantic error: only functions can exist in global scope.
```
## Expected Behavior
Bunster should distinguish input and output files correctly.

Ideally: recognize when -o is being used to designate a binary name, regardless of its extension (e.g., .sh, .out, etc.).

Alternatively: warn or prevent .sh extensions in output names to avoid treating them as shell source inputs.

sorry for delay.

This is both a bug and a misconception.

Bunster has a concept of modules. it processes all `.sh` files in current directory. in your case, since you specify the output file with `.sh` extension. it treats it as source file.

also, we have a bug in file names, it always shows `main.sh` which is confusing.

I already fixed the issue with file names in #274 . at least partly. but still need to add more fixes.


Also, fixed your issue in #277 


thanks for reporting ❤️

Thank you for responding to my opening of this issus.  Maybe I'm not yet familiar with the documentation and the usage of the bunster module.  However, I have already alleviated the usage problem by creating a new directory, moving the required files into the directory, and then executing bunster in the directory.bunster is working well now.

A workaround or solution that allows the user to successfully compile their shell scripts without the semantic error
Acknowledgment and fix of the misleading error message that always showed 'main.sh' regardless of actual filename
Resolution of the underlying issue that prevented the original script structure from compiling

嗯，我置顶一个

也是刚遇到这个问题，这个UUID的生成规则主要是系统的MachineGUID，用同一个镜像安装的MachineGUID也相同，更改掉这个MachineGUID即可，然后重启，重新登录rustdesk的UUID就会更换，密码也得重新设置
以下是自动更换MachineGUID的脚本
@echo off
setlocal enabledelayedexpansion

:: 设置注册表路径
set "regPath=HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Cryptography"
set "regValue=MachineGuid"

:: 读取当前 MachineGUID
for /f "tokens=2*" %%A in ('reg query "%regPath%" /v "%regValue%" 2^>nul') do (
    set "currentGUID=%%B"
)

echo.
echo 当前 MachineGUID 是：
echo %currentGUID%
echo.

:: 询问是否修改
set /p choice=是否修改 MachineGUID？（y/yes = 修改，n/no = 退出）: 

:: 转换为大写统一判断
set "choice=%choice%"
set "choice=%choice:~0,1%"
set "choice=%choice:~0,1%"
if /i "%choice%"=="y" goto :modify
if /i "%choice%"=="yes" goto :modify
if /i "%choice%"=="n" goto :exit
if /i "%choice%"=="no" goto :exit

echo 输入无效，默认退出。
goto :exit

:modify
:: 生成新的 v4 UUID（小写）
for /f %%i in ('powershell -command "[guid]::NewGuid().ToString().ToLower()"') do (
    set "newGUID=%%i"
)

echo.
echo 新的 MachineGUID 为：%newGUID%
echo.

:: 写入注册表
reg add "%regPath%" /v "%regValue%" /t REG_SZ /d "%newGUID%" /f >nul

if %errorlevel% neq 0 (
    echo 写入失败，请确保以管理员身份运行。
    pause
    goto :exit
)

echo 写入成功，系统将在 5 秒后重启...
timeout /t 5 /nobreak >nul
shutdown /r /t 0
goto :eof

:exit
echo 脚本执行完成，未进行修改。
pause
exit /b 0

Then when I open Claude i get: What am i missing here?
author: kelmer44

comments.body: Ghidra logs show:

```
pip3 install mcp requests
```

I was getting ENOENT errors and had to change "python" in the claude .conf to "python3".

this is already installed as i run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. I have just installed it manually like you suggest but i get the same result :(

should i be seeing any output when running the `bridge_mcp_ghidra.py` script?

BTW im running the script coming with the cloned repo, not with the release zip, i couldnt find it there

can you post the log file in the claude logs folder? On Mac its in 
```
~/Library/Logs/Claude
```
Filename:
mcp-server-ghidra.log

satisfaction_conditions: A method to make Python dependencies available to the bridge script when executed by Claude

comments.body:
@jacoblin88 

Here is the actual error:

`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'mcp'`

So do:
`pip install fastmcp`

> i got same issue, in my case i used 2 version python 3.11.0 & 3.13 so before you setup the `claude_desktop_config.json` , make sure in the "command": "python" you need put the correct full path your python, > > you can used command `which python3.11` --> this in my case or you can check ussing this command `which python` output e.g : /Users/sohay666/.pyenv/shims/python3.11 > > then you changed the `claude_desktop_config.json` > > ``` > { > "mcpServers": { > "ghidra": { > "command": "/Users/sohay666/.pyenv/shims/python3.11", > "args": [ > "/ABSOLUTE_PATH_TO/bridge_mcp_ghidra.py" > ] > } > } > } > ``` > > before: > > after: --- Hi @sohay666 thanks a lot. It works! It only work when using venv environment of python for me.

Yeah, so this should probably be in the documentation.

You need to create a python venv with something like
` python -m venv ~/bridge-mcp-ghidra-venv`

Activate the venv with `source ~/bridge-mcp-ghidra-venv/bin/activate`

Install requests and mcp with `pip install requests mcp`

And then set the command in claude_desktop_config.json to your full venv python path, eg. `/Users/name-here/bridge-mcp-ghidra-venv/bin/python`

author: Chrisrdouglas

comments.body: Good point, I'll add a requirements.txt shortly.  But you are correct, that is the right package.

Thanks Laurie! This has been fun to test out!

For anyone else who comes across this before the requirements get uploaded I got it working after installing the following:

mcp==1.5.0
requests==2.32.3
Something like this could be neat: https://treyhunner.com/2024/12/lazy-self-installing-python-scripts-with-uv/

I suggest using this command to start the client without needing to install dependencies:  
`uv run --with 'mcp==1.5.0,requests==2.32.3' bridge_mcp_ghidra.py`

title: [Bug] 在升级FastExcel从1.2.0到1.3.0后出现的，在处理多个sheet的Excel写入时发生了数组越界异常。
author: yinzhiyu-hot

comments.body: 调试了一下，得到如图结果 --- 我将sheet名称缩短至最大31个字符，则正常写入，希望这些能提供一些参考价值 --- 继续调试，定位到是 poi 限制了31，与前面提及的最大31互相印证了，看来框架需要对此做一些注释进行阐述

Hi, @yinzhiyu-hot 
Thank you for your research on this issue. It seems that this is a limitation of the Apache POI or Excel itself?

> Yes

Thanks. For now, we might optimize those document: 

- Read: https://fesod.apache.org/docs/read/sheet/
- Write: https://fesod.apache.org/docs/write/sheet/

Are there any volunteers willing to submit a PR?

感谢您这边的邀请，目前还在着重于当下，但期冀在未来为开源贡献一份绵薄之力。 --- 补充说明：1.2.0版本之所以没有问题，是由于并没有WriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler的处理，这应该是1.3.0新增的吧！所以可能依然需要关注1.3.0版本的兼容性，我个人建议是将WriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler的48行传入的sheetName按POI的31位截取后传入，并进行尝试，我本地自定义并注册MyWriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler，且按31位截取传入后，并未报错，但由于依然执行了原来的WriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler，最终无法真正印证心中所想，希望这些信息对后续的处理带来一定的参考价值。 --- 还是心有不甘，又做了进一步尝试，我在自定义的MyWriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler 重写了afterWorkbookCreate并移除了默认的WriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler，终于可以绕过默认的WriteSheetWorkbookWriteHandler，最终验证是可行的，成功写入，结果和1.2.0是一致的，大吉大利，今晚吃鸡！！！ --- 继续补充：经验证，并非只有处理多个sheet写入会发生越界，单一sheet一样存在。

Great issue!

title: Partial Updates do not produce the expected results
body:
### Search before asking

- [x] I searched in the [issues](https://github.com/alibaba/fluss/issues) and found nothing similar.


### Fluss version

0.6.0 (latest release)

### Please describe the bug 🐞

### 1.Create two source tables table_a and table_b, and create a sink table table_w
`CREATE TABLE table_a(id int, order_split_flag int, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) NOT ENFORCED);`
`CREATE TABLE table_b(id int, a_id int, inventory_num int, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) NOT ENFORCED);`
`CREATE TABLE table_w(id int, order_split_flag int, inventory_num int, PRIMARY KEY (`id`) NOT ENFORCED);`
### 2.Submit flink-job and write the merged result of table_a and table_b into table_w
`EXECUTE STATEMENT SET
BEGIN
    INSERT INTO table_w(id,order_split_flag) SELECT id,order_split_flag FROM table_a;
    INSERT INTO table_w(id,inventory_num) SELECT a_id,inventory_num FROM table_b WHERE inventory_num > 0;
END;`
### 3.Write test data to table_a and table_b
`insert into table_a values(1, 1);`
`insert into table_b values(1, 1, 10);`
`insert into table_b values(2, 1, 20);`
`insert into table_b values(2, 1, 0);`
### 4.View the results of table_w
**expect: 1, 1, null**
**actual: 1, 1, 10**

### My question:
When executing the fourth insert statement, the record with id=2 in table_b is changed to 0, which does not meet the situation of inventory_num > 0. However, it seems that the record with id=1 in table_b is read and written to table_w.
**While I am happy with this result, as it looks like another implementation of a delta join, I am puzzled by the behavior.**

### Solution

_No response_

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [x] I'm willing to submit a PR!
author: gongzexin

comments.body:
The following is the result of executing `select * from table_b` when executing the insert statement

- +I           1           1            10
- +I           2           1            20
- -U           2           1            20
- +U           2           1             0

The following is the result of executing `select * from table_w` when executing the insert statement

- +I           1                1        NULL
- -U           1                1        NULL
- +U           1                1            10
- -U           1                1            10
- +U           1                1            20
- -U           1                1            20
- +U           1                1            10

@gongzexin I added a test in my local env and can reproduce the problem. However, it seems the `1, 1, 10` result is correct as there is an `SinkMakterailizer` operator (see the link below) before sink to generate the `+U[inventory_num=10]` message for the sink. Thus the result is `1, 1, 10`. If we add configuration `table.exec.sink.upsert-materialize=NONE` to disable `SinkMaterializer`, the result will be as expected `1, 1, null`. 

https://github.com/wuchong/fluss/commit/0368485f268f25ac84b9d2d505bb838d51200082#diff-426a3724525025196caafb1cc4a605ab963067c2626cfce7e1f01cab9944c731R408

> [@gongzexin](https://github.com/gongzexin) I added a test in my local env and can reproduce the problem. However, it seems the `1, 1, 10` result is correct as there is an `SinkMakterailizer` operator (see the link below) before sink to generate the `+U[inventory_num=10]` message for the sink. Thus the result is `1, 1, 10`. If we add configuration `table.exec.sink.upsert-materialize=NONE` to disable `SinkMaterializer`, the result will be as expected `1, 1, null`.
> 
> [wuchong@0368485#diff-426a3724525025196caafb1cc4a605ab963067c2626cfce7e1f01cab9944c731R408](https://github.com/wuchong/fluss/commit/0368485f268f25ac84b9d2d505bb838d51200082#diff-426a3724525025196caafb1cc4a605ab963067c2626cfce7e1f01cab9944c731R408)

@wuchong Thank your reply. As you said, it is the SinkMaterializer that causes the results to be inconsistent with expectations. I will close this issue.
