title: Session Restores — Memory Doesn't: LLM Forgets Context After Restart
body: ### **Description** After restarting the service, existing session data (events/history) is correctly loaded from storage and the session object is created. However, the LLM does not seem to have this restored context in its working memory. As a result, even though the session exists and the past conversation events are present in the database, the agent is unable to recall previous information when the user continues the conversation. This leads to the LLM behaving as if no prior context exists. In short: **session state persists, but LLM internal memory does not refresh from the restored session**. --- ### **To Reproduce** 1. Run the service and start a conversation with the agent. 2. Provide information to the agent that it should “remember.” 3. Restart the service. 4. Continue the conversation and ask the agent about previously shared information. 5. The agent will not recall the context, even though the session and events were reloaded from storage. --- ### **Expected behavior** After service restart, the agent should load the previous session context not only into its session store, but also into the LLM working memory. The agent should correctly recall previously shared information without requiring the user to repeat it. --- ### **Screenshots** Read lower messages first. First 2 messages are before restart. Second 2 messages are after the restart. After the restart I set the same `session` object, but agent already doesn't remember what is in session. Seems like after restart all objects `event` are needed to be added to LLM context. --- ### **Desktop** * OS: Linux * Java version: 17 * ADK version 0.3.0 --- ### **Additional context** This is especially important for long-running conversational agents where persistence and continuity across restarts are expected. Currently, only session metadata is restored, but the conversational context is not re-hydrated into the model memory, causing loss of continuity for the user. A possible solution could be automatically re-injecting the session history into the LLM context after service restart, before the first user message is processed.
author: fedorovychh

comments.body:
@fedorovychh  -  can you share the code and steps to reproduce this issue ? 

`In short: session state persists, but LLM internal memory does not refresh from the restored session.`


Well, session state is not persisted.

In adk-java,  DatabaseSessionService is not supported yet.
https://google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/session/#sessionservice-implementations

I am working on the implementation for the same. 




---

Hi, 

I’d like to work on this issue. 
Could a maintainer please assign it to me? I’ll open a draft PR soon. Thanks!

> [@fedorovychh](https://github.com/fedorovychh) - can you share the code and steps to reproduce this issue ?
> 
> `In short: session state persists, but LLM internal memory does not refresh from the restored session.`
> 
> Well, session state is not persisted.
> 
> In adk-java, DatabaseSessionService is not supported yet. https://google.github.io/adk-docs/sessions/session/#sessionservice-implementations
> 
> I am working on the implementation for the same.

Hi @prasadskarmarkar ! Here’s what actually happens.

When you start a session using a specific session ID, you can send messages and store the resulting events from the `session` object in your own storage. After restarting the application, you must load those stored events and restore them back into a new `session` object with the same session ID.

Once you run your `Runner` again with the restored session, you’ll notice that the LLM does *not* remember previous conversation details. That’s expected — the stored events don’t recreate the model’s internal long-term memory, only the session structure.

For me, code of setting an object looks like this. It is an overridden method `com.google.adk.sessions.BaseSessionService#getSession`: 
```java
JsonNode memories = getResultsOrThrowException(sessionResponse, error);
List<Event> events = mapToMutableEventsPerSession(memories);
State state = formState(userId, sessionId);
Session session = Session.builder(sessionId).state(state).events(events).userId(userId).build();
return Maybe.just(session);
```
Hi @prasadskarmarkar thank you so. We already fixed this.

author: amihewat

comments.body:
The error you're seeing is because Chunker doesn't have enough memory to convert your world, this is usually because the world is quite big, or you don't have enough available memory (RAM). Chunker by default uses 75% of your available memory, so you might find that closing other applications before converting your world allows it to use the memory it needs.

You can also tell Chunker how much memory you want it to use, you need to run it from command-line in the form of `Chunker.exe -Xmx8G` to tell Chunker to use a maximum of 8 gigabytes of memory.

You can also prune the world in the Advanced Settings of Chunker which may also help if you the problem doesn't occur prior to that.

We can look further, but in most cases a large world does require more memory (especially with compression of the files), if you'd like us to we would need:
- The world size
- How much memory your computer has
- A copy of the world

title: Accessibility: Talkback does not read the value of some elements
body:
Hello, a blind user here. :)

## Reproduction steps

1. Open the app on its main screen.
2. Turn on Talkback by long pressing the up and down volume keys.
3. use left / right swipes to move around the screen.

## Expected behavior

After the labels denoting the selected model and language, the screenreader should read the spinners with their selected values. Also, on the TextView with the result text, it should read the content of the component.

## Actual behavior

The screenreader can find the spinners as well as the TextView, but only reads their description, not their value.

## Explanation

The reason for this bug is the usage of the contentDescription attribute in the activity layout file. contentDescription is typically used on static widgets, where the screenreader has no way of determining how to meaningfully report the widget to the user. For example, the record button and the other buttons on the screen are a perfect use-case for this attribute, because they're just icon buttons, and the screenreader is unable to communicate their purpose represented by the embedded images.

However, for components carying a dynamic value, like the spinners and the result TextView, this value is what screenreaders need to report to the user, so the contentDescription is not necessary. In fact, it is actually counterproductive, since it overrides the component dynamic value, which the user needs to access. In these scenarios, VI users can determine the purpose of the component by its adjacent label, which is accessible for the screenreaders.

## Solution

Removing the contentDescription attribute from the spinners and the result TextView makes thing work really nicely on my phone. :)

I could open a PR, but it's really just 3 line change.

Thanks for the great job!

title: CTD
body:
经常性CTD 错误显示内存不足（我分了24g应该不至于吃满）




DS分析：崩溃摘要
问题发生时间: 2025年8月27日 20:28:21

问题简述: Rendering entity in world (在世界中渲染实体)

直接原因: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Mesh buffer exceeds limit. (网格缓冲区超出限制)

关键模组: acceleratedrendering (加速渲染模组)

涉及实体: 玩家 PornhubVIP (你自己)

原因深度分析
根本原因: 崩溃的直接原因是 加速渲染 (Accelerated Rendering) 模组内部的 ServerMesh$Builder.checkMeshBuffer 方法检测到其管理的网格缓冲区达到了内存上限，并主动抛出 OutOfMemoryError。这通常不是为了表示整个Java虚拟机内存耗尽，而是该模组为自己设置的一个安全上限被突破了。

触发链条:

游戏尝试渲染玩家实体（你自己）。

渲染过程涉及到渲染玩家的盔甲层 (HumanoidArmorLayer)。

盔甲层需要编译和渲染模型 (ModelPart.compile 和 render)。

在这个过程中，加速渲染 (Accelerated Rendering) 模组介入，试图优化模型的编译和渲染（通过 compileFast 和 AcceleratedBufferBuilder）。

在构建优化后的网格(Mesh)时，该模组计算发现其内部缓冲区将要超出预设的容量限制，为了防止更严重的问题（如真正的、无法控制的内存溢出或图形API错误），它主动抛出错误，导致游戏崩溃。

为什么是现在？

你安装了大量修改实体模型、渲染、盔甲外观的模组（如 immersive_armors, entity_model_features, artifacts, geckolib 等）。这些模组极大地增加了玩家模型的复杂度和数据量。

你可能穿着非常复杂或由多个上述模组添加的盔甲。

加速渲染 (Accelerated Rendering) 模组试图一次性处理所有这些复杂的模型数据，导致其缓冲区需求激增，最终超过限制。

其他因素:

你使用了非常高分辨率的材质包（“立方构想 V4028 128x”和“零雾构想 V5002”），这进一步增加了显存和内存的负担。

你安装了多个性能优化/渲染修改模组（如 sodium, iris, entityculling 等），它们之间可能存在非常复杂的交互，在某些特定情况下反而会引发冲突。

title: TLS certificates aren't being validated when making HTTPS requests to LLM APIs
body: If I understand the code right, API calls are being made using HTTP clients that automatically trust all TLS certificates ([CustomEmbeddingService.java](https://github.com/jtang613/GhidrAssist/blob/7418766c548280e97f82a814a1b06ca772bcb38b/src/main/java/ghidrassist/CustomEmbeddingService.java#L58-L86), [CustomOpenAiService.java](https://github.com/jtang613/GhidrAssist/blob/7418766c548280e97f82a814a1b06ca772bcb38b/src/main/java/ghidrassist/CustomOpenAiService.java#L23-L65)). Is there any chance that the code could be modified to enable certificate validation on all HTTPS connections by default, but have an "insecure" toggles for individual connections so the user can disable certificate validation for specific endpoints (e.g., if they have an Ollama server with a self-signed certificate)?
author: cyrozap

comments.body:
Your assessment is correct - certificate validation is disabled to facilitate use with local LLMs (which typically use self-signed certificates). While not ideal, it was a pragmatic choice given the risk and impact of this are very low in this context - ie: how worried are you of a MITM attack targeting your OpenAI API requests which only contain Ghidra disassembly?

That said, I'm not against considering minimally invasive pull requests and/or adding it as a _future enhancement_ item on my todo list.

> how worried are you of a MITM attack targeting your OpenAI API requests which only contain Ghidra disassembly?

In this case I'm less worried about snooping than I am tampering. Biggest risk IMO is someone injecting responses that exploit the HTTP client, JSON parser, Markdown parser, etc., and then using that to either exfiltrate data or get RCE. Even without exploiting any parser vulnerabilities, I wonder what would happen if a response was sent to the client that included Markdown code that loaded a malicious image from the web? Or changing the prompt to, for example, [convince the LLM to access a specific URL based on private user information](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.00199v1), leaking that information to the attacker?

Regardless, I've just submitted a PR (#4) to enable HTTPS connections to be secure by default, with a simple checkbox for each provider to disable certificate verification as needed. Feel free to make any changes to it as you see fit.
Thank you for your contribution. This will be in the next release.

satisfaction_conditions: A mechanism to enable TLS certificate validation by default for HTTPS connections to LLM APIs
A user-configurable option to selectively disable certificate validation for specific endpoints
Protection against potential security vulnerabilities from man-in-the-middle attacks that could exploit parsers or manipulate LLM responses

title: MCP server stdio mode corrupted by stdout log messages
body:
## Bug Description

The MCP server startup code in `src/cli/simple-commands/mcp.js` outputs log messages to **stdout** during stdio mode initialization, which corrupts the JSON-RPC protocol stream and causes errors in MCP clients.

## Root Cause

When running `npx claude-flow mcp start` (which defaults to stdio mode), the code outputs startup messages to stdout using `printSuccess()`:

```javascript
printSuccess('Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...');
```

This outputs to **stdout**:
```
✅ Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...
```

In MCP's stdio mode, **stdout must be reserved exclusively for JSON-RPC protocol messages**. Any other output corrupts the protocol stream.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run: `npx claude-flow mcp start`
2. Observe MCP client errors due to corrupted JSON-RPC stream
3. Check stdout output - startup messages appear on stdout instead of being silent

## Expected Behavior

- The wrapper function in `simple-commands/mcp.js` should be **completely silent**
- It only spawns the real MCP server with `stdio: 'inherit'`
- The actual MCP server (`src/mcp/mcp-server.js`) already handles proper logging to stderr
- Wrapper messages are redundant and harmful

## Actual Behavior

- Wrapper outputs unnecessary startup messages to stdout
- This corrupts the JSON-RPC protocol stream
- MCP clients cannot parse the output

## Impact

- MCP server cannot be used in stdio mode with standard MCP clients
- Affects all users trying to use claude-flow as an MCP server
- Bug has existed since July 8, 2025 (commit 29800626c, PR #167)

## Affected Code

`src/cli/simple-commands/mcp.js` lines 51-97:
- Line 53: `printSuccess('Starting Claude Flow MCP server in stdio mode...')` 
- Lines 56-61: Auto-orchestrator status messages
- Lines 88-91: Exit handler messages
- Lines 105-112: Fallback error messages

All of these should be **removed** for stdio mode.

## Solution

The wrapper function should be **completely silent** in stdio mode:

```javascript
if (stdio) {
  // Start MCP server in stdio mode (like ruv-swarm)
  // The actual MCP server will handle all logging to stderr
  try {
    // ... spawn server with stdio: 'inherit' ...
    
    serverProcess.on('exit', (code) => {
      // Silent exit - server handles its own logging
      if (code !== 0) {
        process.exit(code);
      }
    });
    
    await new Promise(() => {}); // Never resolves, keeps server running
  } catch (error) {
    // Silent fail - the spawned server will handle error logging
    process.exit(1);
  }
}
```

## Why Remove Instead of Stderr?

The wrapper just spawns the real server with `stdio: 'inherit'`, which means:
1. The real MCP server (`src/mcp/mcp-server.js`) already logs properly to stderr
2. Wrapper messages are redundant
3. Even stderr messages from the wrapper add noise
4. Clean separation: wrapper is silent, server handles all I/O

## Git History

Introduced in:
- Commit: 29800626c9a3688ab8a5c0b1364b2dbedbacd7b1
- Date: July 8, 2025
- PR: #167 "feat: implement critical hook safety system & resolve all init issues"
- Author: rUv

Persisted through:
- v2.0.0-alpha.59 (6207ea53)
- v2.0.0-alpha.62 (fd295cda)  
- v2.5.0-alpha.131 (85a8988c)

## References

- MCP Protocol Specification: stdio transport requires clean stdout
- Real MCP server implementation: `src/mcp/mcp-server.js` (properly uses stderr)

Sorry, I mixed issues but there related. 

I ran some tests and managed to export bitmap formats (PNG, JPG, Canvas…) up to a **maximum width of around 21k pixels**.
I believe the issue is not directly related to SnapDOM itself (although I could be wrong, of course).

When you export a capture to a bitmap format, SnapDOM internally relies on a `<canvas>` element — and that element has browser-level size limits. These limits aren’t very clear and can vary depending on the browser, GPU, and even the content being rendered.

For example, if you’re capturing a 10,000-px-wide element with a device pixel ratio (DPR) of 2, the internal bitmap actually becomes **20k px wide**, which may exceed the canvas limit.

In that case, you can manually set `dpr: 1` or even lower values (e.g., `0.5`) to avoid decoding or rendering errors. I’ve even tested successfully up to **50 k px** using `dpr: 0.01` — though, of course, the quality was terrible.

When downloading an image, SnapDOM already forces `dpr: 1` by default, but I can make that parameter configurable again if needed.

title: [Bug]: Props spread and trackSplit is not working correctly together
author: chandani-rathi

comments.body: This works as expected because of the way Ripple treats props to make them reactive. Spreading an object loses all property accessors, the property getters - just the way JS works. There are 3 possibilities here to make it work: 1. always pass in the boxed `count` through the component tree and read with `@count` 2. declare `CounterWrapper` with explicit count and rest, and pass in count explicitly. This will keep the count prop getter from the `App` and create another one in `CounterWrapper` that still gets its value from the `App`'s count prop getter. ```jsx component CounterWrapper({ count, ...rest }) { } ``` 3. Use `trackSplit` in `CounterWrapper`, where `trackSplit` can keep the count prop getter and unwrapping `@` still gives you the original prop getter from `App`. ```jsx component CounterWrapper(props) { const [count, rest] = trackSplit(props, ['count']); } ``` I suggest you look at the compiled code to better understand how this works. Disable source maps in chrome dev tools. And open the compiled code:

Actually, @trueadm I think we can do better.

I think we can actually treat this as a bug.

When we call `_$_.spread_props`, as in this case `<Counter {...props} />`, we know that internally it calls `proxy_tracked` and the resulting proxy can reference whatever `_$_.spread_props` produces.

Now we produce:

```js
_$_.spread_props(() => ({...props}), __block)
```

but we could produce:

```js
_$_.spread_props(() => props, __block)
```

And then the proxy call, let's take the `get` trap as an example (but all traps work this way):
```js
get(_, property) {
  const obj = get(tracked);
  return obj[property];
},
```
will now reference the original object `props` vs the spread `{...props}` which loses the accessors. 

So, this way we can keep the reference pointing to the original object vs the spread.  And since the proxy handles access to all properties, we get to keep reactivity if one existed.

But I might be missing some important contexts / use case, so just want to make sure this won't cause issues.

P.S. I already tried it out with a changed transformer and it works with this particular use case.
Feel free to put up a PR with it to compare then :)

title: [Bug]: Reactivity is lost after trying to derive the value from input prop
author: chandani-rathi

comments.body:
Well looking at the first immediate issue, and it's this:

```jsx
const { transformedMessage } = useMessage({ message });  // <-- this is causing the reactive
```

When you pass through `message`, you're passing the reactive value in to the object, but that object itself won't be reactive so it's basically static on first encounter. You need to either pass the Tracked value as a whole to the component, as in without `@` as a prefix. Or you need to understand that `message` can change as a prop, and pass the entire props and then access `.message` at the other side, or use `track(() => )` to contain the reactivity.

Personally I think you should just pass the Tracked value though:

```jsx
<Input {message} />
```

Then at the other side they can just mutate it and read it normally by using `@` prefix.

So this isn't a bug in Ripple, but rather just by the fact that `useMessage` itself is being used in a non-reactive context – i.e. inside a `track` and by the fact that `message` is a reactive primitive rather than an object, which can contain the reactivity for you. A typical JS pass by reference vs pass by value setup.

We auto make destructuted props reactive but maybe we shouldn’t do this to help reduce confusion. `trackSplit` can’t auto be used as it changes the types to be wrapped tracked objects, which is why you can pass them around from it.
Can't you just do that with `trackSplit` and an empty array?

satisfaction_conditions: Clarification of the root cause explaining why reactivity is lost when passing reactive values to functions
Guidance on correct patterns for maintaining reactivity when passing props to helper functions
Confirmation that the observed behavior is not a framework bug but expected behavior based on how reactivity works

title: why not to respect the iso-639-1 or iso-639-2 language code standards?
body: What is the interest to change standards like "a" for English etc...? for a developers it becomes not really clean to always create a layer to fit the standards... anyhow....
author: ROBERT-MCDOWELL

comments.body:
Sorry for departing from the standard. Because I only speak English, `a` and `b` are the prefixes I've used internally for a while now for models and voices that predate Kokoro. Other languages just got tacked on after the fact, and I stuck to the 1-letter convention. You know the saying… "Make it work, make it right, make it fast"

BTW, similar complaints are leveled about the dependency bloat, which I'm aware of. Both of these will hopefully improve over time.

For now, I will patch the `KPipeline` constructor to map iso language codes to the appropriate 1-letter `lang_code`.
ok thanks. for eng, en-us and en-uk can be aliases of a and b indeed.. fr-ca for french canadian, fr-fr for french france....

You can now use `en-us` and `en-gb`. I don't think `en-uk` is a legal code.

[SIWIS](https://datashare.ed.ac.uk/handle/10283/2353) is the only French voice, and that's `fr-fr`, so `fr-ca` is not supported.

Aliases listed here, as you can see they still map to the 1-letter codes internally—we're taking baby steps:

https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro/blob/43bc156514cbb976b29c17e08d4a14d35181c7df/kokoro/pipeline.py#L11-L21
yes, en-gb was the right to go.... thanks!

satisfaction_conditions: Support for ISO-standard language codes as input parameters
Elimination of the need for custom mapping layers between standard codes and internal implementation
Acknowledgment and commitment to address the standards compliance issue

title: Very large text with pronunciation helper fails
body:
For short text this works fine but for very long text (my test was 40k chars, so a chapter of a book) the pronunciation hint in the form of

`[Kokoro](/kˈOkəɹO/)
`
is ignored. It will pronounce BOTH the first and second parts. Again, this only occurs on extremely long text inputs and the workaround is manually splitting the text and running it separately for each part.
author: travisapple

comments.body:
Is your text 40k chars with no newlines? The default behavior is to split on newlines:
https://github.com/hexgrad/kokoro/blob/2f4d94bba25dc73e05ec4a9ffdee72f1d46fdd5c/kokoro/pipeline.py#L233-L240

Either way will take a look at this, but another fix in the meantime is to reach into the `G2P` class and directly override the gold lexicon like this:
```py
pipelines = {lang_code: KPipeline(lang_code=lang_code, model=False) for lang_code in 'ab'}
pipelines['a'].g2p.lexicon.golds['kokoro'] = 'kˈOkəɹO'
pipelines['b'].g2p.lexicon.golds['kokoro'] = 'kˈQkəɹQ'
```
https://huggingface.co/spaces/hexgrad/Kokoro-TTS/blob/136465fbffad342a1de9e44cc326ea75090a1828/app.py#L13-L15

Recommend you only do that for proper nouns, and still use the Markdown syntax for common words or homographs.

It's 40k WITH newlines. Never more than ~300 chars per paragraph but sometimes it will split by sentence. Splitting by sentence doesn't seem to affect this issue.

Some context, I want a book reader. The book has some wild character names and so I do a search and replace on these names with pronunciations.

I'll take a hard look at the G2P options in the morning and THANK YOU for your time

Interesting, a failure is bad either way, but 40k _with_ newlines is more concerning. To help debug, if you could supply either of the following:
```py
text = '40k chars'
longest_paragraph = max(text.split('\n'), key=len)

print(longest_paragraph)      # <= if you can share the text
print(len(longest_paragraph)) # <= if the text is copyrighted
```
If the text is copyrighted, sensitive, etc no sweat, just the length is fine in that case.

Edit: Actually on second thought, the specific paragraph (with the Markdown syntax that is double-read) causing the failure would be most helpful. It could be nontrivial to reproduce & trace the issue otherwise.

It's copyrighted for sure. I'm attaching a zip file with what you need. Run fulltext.txt and then I'm attaching a sample output that shows the effect I'm getting.

[Nynaeve](/nˈInˈiːv/) had never thought that she would want the [Aes Sedai](/ˈI sɪdˈI/) to keep Lan on a short leash at her side.'''

model = KModel().to('cuda').eval()
pipeline = KPipeline(lang_code='b', model=model)
generator = pipeline(
	fulltext,
	voice = 'bf_emma',
	speed = 1.1146358814550124
)

for i, result in enumerate(generator):
	audio = result.audio.cpu().numpy()
	audio = np.int16(audio * 2 ** 15)
	sound = pydub.AudioSegment(audio.squeeze().tobytes(), frame_rate=24000, sample_width=2, channels=1)
	sound.export('test.mp3', format='mp3', bitrate='170k')

```
This will create a file that shows the issue. The first 3 word helpers are fine and then the rest are repeated.

You have what is probably a typo here `[Cairhien](/kˈɛː hˈiːn/)in` @travisapple 

Still not functionally correct, but I suspect fixing that will resolve your issue. Also, consider overriding the dictionary instead of using the `[]()` syntax.

I'll just switch to the dictionary method but I believe I'll need both eventually. Is the problem with the above text that there needs to be a space before "in"?
If you run this code you'll find that it will fail at instances without this issue.
If you delete the trailing `in` at the back of `[Cairhien](/kˈɛː hˈiːn/)in` does it not resolve the problem?
It does fix it and now that I know you need spaces around everything it should be fine. However, it might be preferable if the spaces were not required.

title: [Bug]: Documents are not processed and RAG-Chat doesn´t work correctly.

### 🔍 Bug Summary

No Processed, Weired RAG-Chat

### 📖 Description

I have the problem that although I was able to upload many documents with paperless-ngx and assign them appropriate tags that are helpful for searching, when connected to paperless-AI, only the documents in paperless-ngx are recognized but not processed, i.e., they are displayed with the status “unprocessed.” Due to the lack of processing, I can neither select a document from the Manual menu item nor from Chat, and when I ask a question about an existing document in the RAG chat, the AI gives an answer that has nothing to do with the question. The AI takes any document sources and fantasizes about something that has nothing to do with the question.

My guess is that something is wrong with the indexing or with embeddings.

title: [Bug]: "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" severely broken, causes crash, no processing
body:
### 🔍 Bug Summary

"PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" severely broken, causes crash, no processing

### 📖 Description

When setting "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" it causes the document processing to completely stop and the webservice crashes, reboots when opneing the "Manual" and "Chat" pages.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. Set up fresh paperless-ai with paperless-ngx and ollama properly configured.
2. Set above mentiones option. Option "TAGS" can be filled or empty, same result.
3. Paperless-ui will not start processing.
4. Klick "Manual" or "Chat" in the menu and webservice crashes.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Document processing should work with above mentioned options.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Service crashes, restarts.

### 🏷️ Paperless-AI Version

3.0.7

comments.body:
First of all I beg you to fill out all mandatory informations here, like described in the Issue Template.
Also I just tried a fresh install of PP-NGX and PP-AI with the mentioned setting of you and have absolutly no problems.

Hi there!
Thanks for your quick reaction. Filled up the missing point as requested. Mobile Browser I left out, since I only use desktop.

I want to mention, that when setting "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=no", document processing works, both manual and automatic, also menu items "Manual" and "Chat" work fine then. But the mentioned option is totally necessary for me, since I have two different instances running with one 2800 documents, the other 4500 documents so far and quickly growing.

I have already re-set up both instances of paperless-ai, but the problem persists as soon as I set "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes".

---

Could it be that for some reason with "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" Paperless-ai tries to re-catch tags from "localhost" instead of my correctly configured parperless url? It's strange because my tags are actually correctly listed on the dashboard already...

>       _header: 'GET /api/tags/?page=2 HTTP/1.1\r\n' +
>         'Accept: application/json, text/plain, _/_\r\n' +
>         'Content-Type: application/json\r\n' +
>         'Authorization: Token xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx\r\n' +
>         'User-Agent: axios/1.8.2\r\n' +
>         'Accept-Encoding: gzip, compress, deflate, br\r\n' +
>         'Host: localhost:8000\r\n' +
>         'Connection: keep-alive\r\n' +
>         '\r\n',
>       _keepAliveTimeout: 0,

The error logs seem showing a much bigger problem interacting with your Paperless-ngx instance. 
Are you running paperless-ngx behind some reverse proxy or firewall or something like that?

Yes, two different hosts:
- paperless-ngx in a datacenter, behind ufw and apache2 proxy
- paperless-ai on my LAN behind my router and an nginx proxy

Why does everything work with "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=no", though? Tags and Documents show up, processing works, etc..

```
code: 'ERR_BAD_REQUEST',

      Accept: 'application/json, text/plain, _/_',
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: 'Token xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx',
      'User-Agent': 'axios/1.8.2',
      'Accept-Encoding': 'gzip, compress, deflate, br'
    },
    baseURL: 'https://xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/api',
    method: 'get',
    url: 'http://localhost:8000/api/tags/?page=2',
    allowAbsoluteUrls: true,
    data: undefined
  },
```

This part is what makes me wonder. 

```
    baseURL: 'https://xxxxxxxxxxxxxxx/api',
    method: 'get',
    url: 'http://localhost:8000/api/tags/?page=2',
    allowAbsoluteUrls: true,
    data: undefined
```

You have baseURL with https with your external instance and the url is http://localhost:8000
There is something wrong on your side. 

I can 100% say Paperless-AI is not the cause of this. You are the first one reporting this particular issue. also I can not reproduce it.

If I understand you right, 

    url: 'http://localhost:8000/api/tags/?page=2',

should be

    url: 'https://[my-domain]/api/tags/?page=2',

correct?

That is what I'm also curious about. I have not set http://localhost:8000/ anywhere. It was the default setting for the paperless-ngx url when setting up paperless-AI. I don't understand why it shows up here. I have just xx'ed out my actual domain from the logs. In the config (.env) my paperless-ngx url, API-token, username are properly set, accepted by paperless-ai, and data is already fetched through the paperless-ngx API. My certificate on that host is valid (Letsencrypt). https should not be a problem, right? 

From your hint I checked my apache proxy config, and indeed it is forwarding to 'http://localhost:8000/'. When changig the proxy forward to 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/', paperless-ai crashes with the same log as above but with 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/' in the block mentioned above. So: paperless-ai - for whatever reason - takes the url my proxy is forwarding to as the actual url an hence cannot reach my paperless-ngx anymore.

For my paperless-ngx I have set my correct external url as environment variable, so paperless-ngx is not returning fals urls.

Her's some mor weird stuff:
I have deleted my volume for paperless-ai and freshly set it up again. For some reason "PROCESS_PREDEFINED_DOCUMENTS=yes" works now. changing my apache proxy setting back and forth doesn't change that, it just keeps working. My second instance though - with exact same config - doens't work.

I'll try reproducing a second working setup and report back.

> If I understand you right,
> 
> `url: 'http://localhost:8000/api/tags/?page=2',`
> should be
> 
> `url: 'https://[my-domain]/api/tags/?page=2',`
> correct?

Correct. So we can now safely say it has something to do with your reverse proxy.
As this is an user produced issue there is no way I can help you out here.
But if you find the solution keep me updated here. Just out of curiosity.

Well, the question arising is: Why does paperless-ai build wrong urls under certain conditions, when the url is actually correctly configured?

I now have two exact same setups, with the exact same proxy config, only different ports for the paperless-ngx container behind the proxy. One paperless-ai is working, the other one not.

From what I see my proxy is correctly configured. Paperless-ai is doing some bogus stuff with urls...

I'll try testing further, but I don't see this solved yet..

It is NOT doing bogus stuff with URLs. Go and check the source code yourself. 
I had multiple users where they claimed to found bugs or issues when everytime it was their setup behind BOGUS proxy and dns setups.

For me it is solved. I am not a tech support.

I am just searching to wrap gpt-oss, which is not yet working, and I notice that your configuration also used it.
I am not sure, but possibly implies some "</think>" in responses, which may be related to your issue...

> I am just searching to wrap gpt-oss, which is not yet working, and I notice that your configuration also used it. I am not sure, but possibly implies some "" in responses, which may be related to your issue...

Thanks for the hint. I'm afraid I don't understand your remark with "". Could you explain further?

I am aware that gpt-oss does not work yet, I actually use qwen3:30b, which works pretty good.

sorry, my "" was indeed containing "think".
I tried (manually) to test gpt-oss, and it is really better than qwen3:30b, at least for my use cases...

> It is NOT doing bogus stuff with URLs. Go and check the source code yourself. I had multiple users where they claimed to found bugs or issues when everytime it was their setup behind BOGUS proxy and dns setups.
> 
> For me it is solved. I am not a tech support.

Alright man, you got me! I had not set up reverse url translation properly in my proxy, so paperless-ngx returned the local url an port on responses..

What I am wondering, though, is why it suddenly worked in one instance without changing my proxy..?

Anyways, thanks for the hint and for paperless-ai as this awesome addition to paperless!

Guidance toward examining reverse proxy and URL handling configuration
Explanation of why the application was constructing URLs with localhost instead of the configured external domain

title: [Bug]: Indexing not working - Internal Server Error 500

### 🔍 Bug Summary

Indexing not working - Internal Server Error 500

### 📖 Description

Okay, installed the latest version of paperless-ai on the same virtual machine that paperless-ngx is running. I went through all the setup and think I did everything correctly.

There is just one difference to the setup instructions: My Ollama instance is running on a different virtual machine (because of hardware resource mappings). Meaning I access it via a IP address instead of localhost. 

Please see the attached *docker-compose logs* file below.

I assume it has something to do with accessing the Ollama instance via LAN instead of localhost.. But docker logs for the Ollama instance only gives me this entry:

`[GIN] 2025/08/21 - 09:08:00 | 200 |      18.069µs |   192.168.42.61 | GET      "/api/ps"`

So we see that it the paperless-ai instance is trying to access Ollama. 


### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

As an example, go to "Paperless-AI RAG Chat".

### ✅ Expected Behavior

Doing more than just giving an error.

### ❌ Actual Behavior

Not working. With messages like:

- Error starting indexing
- Error checking status

latest( via docker-compose)

title: [Bug]: paperless-ai not editing the paperless document
body:
### 🔍 Bug Summary

paperless-ai processes document without editing the paperless document

### 📖 Description

I just installed it a couple of days ago. And i let it run trough all my documents. It processed all 400 documents but did not  edit all of them in paperless. at the beginning there were over a 100 documends that had nothing changed to them but had an entry in the history with totally different tags and name and so on. 
I let it run a couple of times after that with tags so that i only processes the unedited documents. I even deleted the history but there are allways multiple documents that do not get edited. 
Currently i brought it down to 13 documents that are not beeing eidted by paperless-ai.

### 🔄 Steps to Reproduce

1. have many documents in paperless
2. run the processing
3. look at the processed documents.

### ✅ Expected Behavior

process and edit all the documents

### ❌ Actual Behavior

This error is unrelated to your issue. How many documents do you have in your ngx instance? At a certain amount it takes some time to populate the dropdown as pp-ai has to paginate over all documents sites (ngx api does not feature an endpoint that reflects all documents in a single query).

Also, I figured out, that paperless-ai can not read all tags - seems to depend on the tag creator

我也遇到了类似的问题。但是原因不一样我是试用htpasswd命令创建的密钥文件也用大佬的脚本执行了在registry-hub.yml里添加了该文件。也在docker-compose.yml中取消注释了文件的映射注释。但是我发现管理脚本所执行的添加用户并无法添加成功到和docker-compose.yml同级的htpasswd文件目录下。当然再添加完用户后我也尝试了stop dockerhub容器在start

从issue和install脚本里看到的：
1. 把 `docker-compose.yml` 中需要部署服务里面 `volumes` 中密码文件映射放开：`- ./htpasswd:/auth/htpasswd`。 
2. 生成密码的命令，在 `docker-compose.yml` 同级目录下运行：`htpasswd -Bbc ./htpasswd 用户名 密码`
3. 在需要部署的配置文件例如：registre-hub.yml 中添加配置
```
auth:
  htpasswd:
    realm: basic-realm
    path: /auth/htpasswd
```

title: Keyboard shortcuts don't work
body:
Hey @panphora,

When using the `overtype.esm.js` file, keyboard shortcuts don't seem to be working. I traced it down to the `handleAction()` function on line 2789. I don't quite get why this function is defined twice but if I replace the logic with the way the one on line 1638 works, the keyboard shortcuts work as expected.

I'm initializing the editor like so:

```javascript
<script type="module">
  import OverType, { toolbarButtons } from 'overtype.esm.js';

  const editor = new OverType('#editor', {
    autofocus: true,
    autoResize: true,
    padding: '0px',
    placeholder: "A minimum of 100 characters is required.",
    toolbar: true,
    toolbarButtons: [
      toolbarButtons.bold,
      toolbarButtons.italic,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.bulletList,
      toolbarButtons.orderedList,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.quote,
      toolbarButtons.separator,
      toolbarButtons.viewMode
    ]
  });
</script>
```
author: travisbell

comments.body:
Fixed in v2.1.1!

## What was happening

You're right that `handleAction()` appeared twice - once in `Toolbar` and once in `ShortcutsManager`. The problem was they expected different inputs:

- **Toolbar's `handleAction()`** expected a button config object with an `.action` function
- **ShortcutsManager's `handleAction()`** was sending a string like `"toggleBold"`

So when you pressed Ctrl+B, the shortcut manager sent `"toggleBold"` to the toolbar, which tried to call `"toggleBold".action()` - and failed silently.

## How we fixed it

I created a single action dispatcher (`performAction`) that both toolbar clicks and keyboard shortcuts use:

1. Each toolbar button now has an `actionId` (e.g., `"toggleBold"`)
2. The editor maintains a map of `actionId → action function`
3. Both toolbar clicks and shortcuts call `editor.performAction(actionId)`

This also means **shortcuts now work even if you customize the toolbar** - they're no longer tied to which buttons are visible.

Thanks for the detailed bug report and for tracing it down to the right area!

satisfaction_conditions: A solution that restores keyboard shortcut functionality when using the ESM module version
Resolution of the architectural inconsistency between duplicate function implementations
A technical explanation of the root cause of the malfunction

title: Question: Alert Dialog - temporarily disable escape key behavior?
body:
Thank you, @hunvreus, for creating Basecoat! I'm really enjoying it.

I've incorporated the [Alert Dialog](https://basecoatui.com/components/alert-dialog/) component into an app. When a user clicks the 'Continue' button, a 'delete' request is sent to the app's server. The app disables the 'Continue' and 'Cancel' buttons to indicate that the request is in progress.

However, I've encountered an issue where a user might (accidentally) press the escape key, causing Basecoat to hide the dialog while the request is still ongoing. This could lead to confusion - the user may believe he has cancelled the request.

Is there a way to temporarily disable the behavior of the escape key (i.e., hiding the dialog) while some other event occurs (such as an ongoing 'delete' request)?
author: sdevalk

comments.body: Yes, let me see how I would do that. I can probably expose more methods from Alpine.

Hi @hunvreus Thank you - this works! ✅

In reply:

> Replace somethingElse() woth what you need it to do... You may want to release the lock before closing as well.

Excellent! My app uses htmx - I've attached listeners to my dialog code, setting `lock = true` before a request is issued and `lock = false` after the request has finished.

> The whole idea is the same as shadcn/ui: you should be able to modify the components and make them your own.

Perfect! For reference - I use [shadcn's Alert Dialog](https://ui.shadcn.com/docs/components/alert-dialog) in another app. The `AlertDialogContent` in that component has an [onEscapeKeyDown prop](https://www.radix-ui.com/primitives/docs/components/alert-dialog#content) that I use for enabling or disabling the escape key (e.g. when a request is in progress). I like this approach - it allows me to influence the behavior.

In other words - I hope the 'lock' functionality can be integrated into Basecoat's Dialog component (so that I do not have to modify [dialog.js](https://github.com/hunvreus/basecoat/blob/main/src/js/dialog.js)).

I'm using a native `` now. You can do: ```html

Are you absolutely sure?

This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove your data from our servers.

 ``` Obviously, you can achieve the same with vanilla JS by just adding an event listener on the ``. --- Just to be clear, I don't think it'd be reasonable for me to extend the current API as it does exactly what it needs to do and you can improve upon it with vanilla JS. BTW, the latest version is 100% vanilla JS, I just gave the example with Alpine.js as it's more compact, but you could do: ```html

Are you absolutely sure?

This action cannot be undone. This will permanently delete your account and remove your data from our servers.

 ```

#### Using Virtual Environments (Recommended for Arch/Fedora/Ubuntu 23.04+)

Modern Linux distributions enforce [PEP 668](https://peps.python.org/pep-0668/), which prevents system-wide pip installs. Use a virtual environment instead:

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/gamosoft/notediscovery.git
cd notediscovery

# Create a virtual environment
python -m venv venv

# Activate it (choose your shell):
source venv/bin/activate        # Bash/Zsh (most Linux distros)
source venv/bin/activate.fish   # Fish (CachyOS, etc.)
source venv/bin/activate.csh    # Csh/Tcsh
.\venv\Scripts\activate         # Windows PowerShell

# Install dependencies and run
pip install -r requirements.txt
python run.py
```

> 💡 **Tip:** You'll need to activate the virtual environment (`source venv/bin/activate`) each time you open a new terminal before running the app.

body:
Inside NoteDiscovery a dragged in image displays fine since they have the link created as `![logo](/api/images/_attachments/logo.jpeg)`


The major problem is loading up an established markdown site with structured linked items (ie images) relative to the md file path. All images in these md files don't work as all images are not located in `/api/images/`

I can understand the API call for uploading to be able to rename, check extension, all that, but creating a coded link url that doesn't exist and only valid for NoteDiscovery limits the usefulness of the app as a markdown editor. It looks like the issue is on the bucket creation step. project isn't passed through to the create_bucket command, which means it should default from the project set on the client. However this doesn't appear to exist when the storage client is created.

`# Try to get from client (if available in future versions) or env.
    proj = getattr(client, "project", None) or os.getenv("GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT")`

title: Bug: create-new-feature.sh creates specs in wrong directory (specs/ instead of .specify/specs/)
body:
## Description

The `create-new-feature.sh` script creates spec directories in the wrong location, inconsistent with the documented Spec Kit structure and other template paths in the same script.

## Current Behavior

Line 133 in `scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh`:
```bash
SPECS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/specs"
mkdir -p "$SPECS_DIR"
```

This creates spec directories at:
- ❌ `specs/001-feature-name/` (root level)

## Expected Behavior

Should match the documented structure and be consistent with the template path (line 247):
```bash
SPECS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.specify/specs"
mkdir -p "$SPECS_DIR"
```

This would create spec directories at:
- ✅ `.specify/specs/001-feature-name/` (within .specify directory)

## Evidence of Inconsistency

**Same script, line 247** correctly uses `.specify/`:
```bash
TEMPLATE="$REPO_ROOT/.specify/templates/spec-template.md"
```

**Documented structure** shows specs under `.specify/`:
```
.specify/
  ├── memory/
  ├── specs/              ← Should be here
  │   ├── 001-feature/
  │   └── 002-feature/
  └── templates/          ← Templates correctly use .specify/
```

## Impact

**Severity**: Medium-High

- All users running `/speckit.specify` commands create specs in wrong location
- Requires manual `mv` to relocate specs to correct directory
- Breaks project organization and tooling expectations
- Affects spec discovery and navigation

**User Impact**:
- Confusion about where specs should live
- Extra manual steps after every spec creation
- Inconsistent project structure across Spec Kit installations

## Affected Versions

- Confirmed in **v0.0.85** (latest, released 2025-11-15)
- Likely affects all recent versions (tested back to v0.0.78)
- Bug exists in upstream repo: https://github.com/github/spec-kit/blob/main/scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh

## Reproduction Steps

1. Initialize Spec Kit: `specify init my-project`
2. Create a spec: `/speckit.specify "Add user authentication"`
3. Observe created directory: `specs/001-add-user-authentication/` (wrong location)
4. Expected directory: `.specify/specs/001-add-user-authentication/`

## Proposed Fix

**File**: `scripts/bash/create-new-feature.sh`
**Line**: 133

```diff
- SPECS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/specs"
+ SPECS_DIR="$REPO_ROOT/.specify/specs"
```

This single-line change aligns the script with:
- Documented Spec Kit structure
- Template path convention in same script
- User expectations
- All other `.specify/` paths

## Additional Context

Discovered while using Spec Kit with Claude Code in MCP Monorepo project. The bug caused specs to be created at root level for multiple feature branches before we identified the issue.

**Workaround** (until fixed):
After running `/speckit.specify`, manually move specs:
```bash
mv specs/NNN-feature-name .specify/specs/
```

## Related

- This affects all Spec Kit templates (claude, copilot, gemini, etc.)
- Bug is present in all distributed release ZIPs
- Affects both shell script (sh) and PowerShell (ps) variants

---

**Environment**:
- Spec Kit CLI installed via: `uv tool install specify-cli`
- Template version: v0.0.85 (claude-sh)
- OS: macOS 15.0.1
- Shell: zsh
author: Ferneyman

title: Prompt files are empty in speckit releases after 0.0.80, causing all commands to fail
body:
### **Description**

When using **speckit**, I initialized a project using the following command:

```
specify init . --ai copilot
```

The generated prompt files were completely empty, which caused all speckit commands to behave incorrectly.

To confirm that this wasn’t an issue specific to the Copilot integration, I manually downloaded the official release ZIP packages for versions **0.0.80 and later**. After extracting them, I found that the prompt files inside the release packages were also empty.

It appears that starting from version **0.0.80**, all releases contain empty prompt files — suggesting a packaging/build regression.

---

### **Steps to Reproduce**

1. Run

   ```
   specify init . --ai copilot
   ```
2. Inspect the generated `.speckit/prompts` directory — all prompt files are empty
3. Download any release ZIP from GitHub for version **0.0.80+**
4. Extract the archive and check the prompt files — they are also empty

---

### **Expected Behavior**

* Release packages should include complete prompt definitions
* Running `specify init . --ai copilot` should generate a project with valid prompt content
* speckit commands should function normally

---

### **Actual Behavior**

title: Parallel OCR
body:
### Question
Hi, I am trying to use `tessract-cli` for OCR for my document processing pipeline, however the command get executed for each page sequentially. How to run them in parallel?
author: Sinha-Ujjawal

comments.body:
You can run Tesseract OCR on multiple pages in parallel instead of sequentially by using Python’s concurrent.futures:

import concurrent.futures
import subprocess

pages = ["page1.png", "page2.png", "page3.png"]

def run_tesseract(page):
    output_file = page.replace(".png", "")
    subprocess.run(["tesseract", page, output_file])

# Run OCR in parallel
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
    executor.map(run_tesseract, pages)


Notes:

Each page is processed concurrently.

Use ProcessPoolExecutor for CPU-intensive workloads.

Limit max_workers to avoid overloading your CPU.

Command-line alternative (Linux/macOS):

ls pages/*.png | parallel tesseract {} {.}


This runs Tesseract on all images in parallel automatically.

title: Cannot convert a document as a string
body:
### Bug
Docling converter works fine for `Path` objects but not strings. I'd like to remove YAML frontmatter from some files prior to converting them.

### Steps to reproduce
Example script:

```
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import NamedTemporaryFile

from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter

with NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False, mode="w", suffix=".txt") as tmp_file:
    tmp_file.write("# Title\n\nThis is a test document.")

# Convert the file using the filename. Works fine.
markdown_file = Path(tmp_file.name)
converter = DocumentConverter()
result = converter.convert(markdown_file, raises_on_error=False)
print(result.document)


# Convert the file using a string. Does not work.
markdown_content = Path(tmp_file.name).read_text()
result = converter.convert(str(markdown_content), raises_on_error=False)
```

Error:
```
FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '# Title\n\nThis is a test document.'
```

### Docling version
```
Docling version: 2.37.0
Docling Core version: 2.38.1
Docling IBM Models version: 3.6.0
Docling Parse version: 4.0.5
Python: cpython-312 (3.12.9)
Platform: Linux-6.14.11-300.fc42.x86_64-x86_64-with-glibc2.41
```

### Python version
```
Python 3.12.9
```
author: major

comments.body:
@major the issue you have is due to the meaning of the first argument (`source`) of function `convert` from  `DocumentConverter`:
- passing a string or a `Path` means that you provide the location of the file (but **not** its content as a string). It can also be a remote file, if the string contains, for instance ,the `http` protocol.
- you can also pass the file as a stream (an object of our class `DocumentStream`), if you have its content in memory. Following your example, that would mean:

  ```py
  from io import BytesIO
  from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter
  from docling.datamodel.base_models import DocumentStream
  
  markdown_content = "# Title\n\nThis is a test document."
  stream = DocumentStream(name="myfile.md", stream=BytesIO(markdown_content.encode()))
  converter = DocumentConverter()
  result = converter.convert(stream)
  print(result.document)
  ```
Ah, that was something I didn't consider. Thank you!
@major can we close this issue?
Sure!

satisfaction_conditions: A method to convert document content that has been loaded into memory as a string
Clarification of how the converter's input parameter is interpreted for different data types
A working approach to pass document content directly to the converter without requiring a file path

from docling.pipeline.standard_pdf_pipeline import StandardPdfPipeline
from docling.datamodel.pipeline_options import PdfPipelineOptions
from surya.recognition import RecognitionPredictor
from surya.detection import DetectionPredictor
from docling.datamodel.base_models import InputFormat
from docling_core.types.doc import ImageRefMode
from docling.document_converter import DocumentConverter, PdfFormatOption
from docling.datamodel.pipeline_options import PdfPipelineOptions, TableFormerMode, EasyOcrOptions, TesseractOcrOptions, OcrMacOptions, RapidOcrOptions, smolvlm_picture_description
from docling.datamodel.settings import settings
from PIL import Image
import os
from docling.models.base_model import BaseEnrichmentModel
from docling.pipeline.standard_pdf_pipeline import StandardPdfPipeline


class SuryaOcrModel(BaseEnrichmentModel):
    def __init__(self, enabled: bool = True):
        self.enabled = enabled
        self.recognition_predictor = RecognitionPredictor()
        self.detection_predictor = DetectionPredictor()

    def is_processable(self, doc, element) -> bool:
        return self.enabled and element.type == "page_image"

    def __call__(self, doc, element_batch: Iterable) -> Iterable:
        for element in element_batch:
            image: Image.Image = element.get_image(doc).convert("RGB")

            # Run Surya OCR
            prediction = self.recognition_predictor([image], [None], self.detection_predictor)[0][0]

            for line in prediction.text_lines:
                text = line.text.strip()
                if not text:
                    continue

                l, t, r, b = line.bbox  # Already in LTRB
                bbox = BoundingBox.from_ltrb(l, t, r, b)
                doc.add_item(TextItem(text=text, bbox=bbox, page_no=element.page_no))

            yield element

class SuryaOcrPipeline(StandardPdfPipeline):
    def __init__(self, pipeline_options):
        super().__init__(pipeline_options)
        self.enrichment_pipe = []
        self.enrichment_pipe.append(SuryaOcrModel(enabled=True))

    @classmethod
    def get_default_options(cls):
        return PdfPipelineOptions(
            generate_page_images=True,
            images_scale=2.0,
            do_ocr=True
        )

@dolfim-ibm @pusapatiakhilraju 
Okay, I figured it our myself. Below is how I made it. Just for future reference.
1. To create a plugin and use it in one's project, it needs to create an individual project for the plugin first.
In my case, I created a new project "custom_docling".
2. And then, prepare the folder structure of this new project for future install.
In my case, my project looks like this.
```
custom_docling
├───src
│   └───custom_docling
│       ├───plugins
│       │   ├───__init__.py
│       │   └───custom_ocr.py
│       └───__init__.py
└───pyproject.toml
```
3. Choose a packaging tool and edit the project packaging information.
In my case, I chose setuptools for packaging (following docling's plugin guide: https://docling-project.github.io/docling/concepts/plugins/), so I wrote pyproject.toml as below.
```toml
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools >= 65.0.0"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "custom_docling"
version = "0.0.1"
dependencies = [
  "docling>=2.30.0",
  "openai>=1.65.0",
]

[project.entry-points."docling"]
custom_ocr = "custom_docling.plugins.custom_ocr"
```
*path of entry-point should not begin from "src", it is ignored by python.
4. After all above, go on coding the plugin, but don't forget add a method "ocr_engines" to the plugin.
In my case, I added the method in custom_ocr.py.
```python
def ocr_engines():
    return {
        "ocr_engines": [
            CustomOcrModel,
        ]
    }
```
5. While coding options for the model, should configure the kind correctly.
In my case, I created the options like this.
```python
class CustomOcrOptions(OcrOptions):
    kind : ClassVar[str] = "custom_ocr"
    ...
```

Some notes on implementing an OCR plugin.
  - Options class should inherits OcrOptions (from docling.datamodel.pipeline_options).
  - Options class must declare a class variable "kind" and set its default value as the same as configured in pyproject.toml.
  - Model class should inherits BaseOcrModel (from docling.models.base_ocr_model).
  - Model class should implements following method:
    - def __init__
    - def __call__
    - def get_options_type
  - get_options_type is a classmethod and should return type of Options.

After everything is done, use `pip install -e xxx` to install this plugin in the main project.

That's all.

@Bill-XU Thanks for outlining your findings and solution. I will close this issue as resolved.
@pusapatiakhilraju Feel free to re-open if you have further questions or feedback.

class ExampleFormulaUnderstandingEnrichmentModel(BaseItemAndImageEnrichmentModel):
    images_scale = 2.6

    def __init__(self, enabled: bool):
        self.enabled = enabled

    def is_processable(self, doc: DoclingDocument, element: NodeItem) -> bool:
        return (
            self.enabled
            and isinstance(element, TextItem)
            and element.label == DocItemLabel.FORMULA
        )

    def __call__(
        self,
        doc: DoclingDocument,
        element_batch: Iterable[ItemAndImageEnrichmentElement],
    ) -> Iterable[NodeItem]:
        if not self.enabled:
            return

        for enrich_element in element_batch:
            enrich_element.image.show()

            yield enrich_element.item
# How the pipeline can be extended.
class ExampleFormulaUnderstandingPipeline(StandardPdfPipeline):

    def __init__(self, pipeline_options: ExampleFormulaUnderstandingPipelineOptions):
        super().__init__(pipeline_options)
        self.pipeline_options: ExampleFormulaUnderstandingPipelineOptions

        self.enrichment_pipe = [
            ExampleFormulaUnderstandingEnrichmentModel(
                enabled=self.pipeline_options.do_formula_understanding
            )
        ]

        if self.pipeline_options.do_formula_understanding:
            self.keep_backend = True

    @classmethod
    def get_default_options(cls) -> ExampleFormulaUnderstandingPipelineOptions:
        return ExampleFormulaUnderstandingPipelineOptions()
# Example main. In the final version, we simply have to set do_formula_understanding to true.

I force upgraded my environment locally to 2.x and docling seems to work with the limited cases I tested.

My usual strategy is to set the requirement to the lowest version I know the lowest version of Python will work with. For example, if Docling works with NumPy 1.24.4, then you could say >= 1.24.4. The last version of NumPy that supports 3.9 is 2.0.2, so there should be no need to limit it to < 2.1.0 as the dependency manager won't see that version.

If there is an incompatibility with a newer version, you could also limit it on the upper side too. Keeping the requirements as loose as possible helps limit these dependency loops.

title: Dataloader not infinite
body:
I am trying to train on a very small dataset with around 10 parquet files. The training hangs after a number of steps and seems to be stuck in an infnitite loop. It always hangs at the exact same step which I traced to what I think is the call to next(train_loader) in base_train.py in the training loop around line 312.

You can recreate this from the original dataset by putting only a few shards in base_data and running something like this:
```
train_loader = tokenizing_distributed_data_loader_with_state(
    32,
    2048,
    split="train",
    device="cuda",
)

while True:
    inputs, targets, state_dict = next(train_loader)
    print(state_dict)
```

It takes a while but eventually it will hang and not return the next. I tried this with only 2 shards and it hangs after the first file; I also tried with 3 shards and it hangs after the second file. I expect it will happen on any number of shards.

I also tried reducing training params like depth, max_seq_len, device_batch_size, and total_batch_size to run through the training steps faster and I still experience the same issue, my smaller subset of training data hangs seemingly waitng on additional training data that never comes. It seems like the original dataset with 200+ shards is so big that a small model finishes training before it encounters the end of the data.

Does this seem like an issue or am I not understaning how this is supposed to work? I expected I could just drop in a different set of data in the same format and run train as is.
author: kmcnayr

comments.body: Hi! Have you checked whether the fix from https://github.com/karpathy/nanochat/pull/361 resolves this issue for you?
Aha yes that's the exact issue. Sorry for the trouble. I clearly didn't use the right keywords when I was searching for existing related items. Thank you!
No worries, thanks for checking and happy to hear that it's fixed!

title: Is epsilon incorrectly scaled in DistAdamW?
body:
I noticed that the epsilon term might not be properly scaled with the bias correction factor. 

## Current implementation:
```python
denom = exp_avg_sq.sqrt().add_(eps)
step_size = lr * (torch.sqrt(bias2) / bias1)
```

This seems to add eps directly without accounting for the bias2 correction applied via step_size.
Expected (standard AdamW):
Epsilon should be added after bias correction of the second moment:

```python
denom = (exp_avg_sq / bias2).sqrt().add_(eps)
step_size = lr / bias1
```

Am I understanding this correctly, or is there a reason for the current implementation?
author: Hyperion-shuo

comments.body:
Hi! I think you're right that usually `exp_avg_sq` is corrected for `bias2` before taking the square root and then adding `eps` only afterwards, as in PyTorch [documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html) and [implementation](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/0c5d5c7e9a53c0b32d8193eaaab2bfaabe7d070f/torch/optim/adam.py#L545). 

The implementation here comes from https://github.com/KellerJordan/modded-nanogpt/blob/master/train_gpt.py#L732-L734 and I'm not sure why they've done it this way. In the end `eps` is just a small correction factor to avoid dividing by zero, so I'm not sure it matters much in the end 🤔 

---

ping @ClassicLarry in case you want to weigh in 🙃 

---

This has now been [fixed](https://github.com/karpathy/nanochat/commit/4ddc8037975f0c11e11038a27eaf81f070971dc8). Thanks again for the report, @Hyperion-shuo!

satisfaction_conditions: Confirmation of whether the identified mathematical discrepancy in the bias correction implementation is correct or intentional
Reference to authoritative sources or standard implementations that support the correct approach to bias correction in adaptive optimizers
Acknowledgment that the implementation will be corrected to align with the standard approach

title: What's the correct way to remove models?
body:
Where are models saved to on each machine?

What's the correct way to remove downloaded models from each machine?

Can the path where models are saved to be changed? (For example, to an external hard drive connected to the Mac over thunderbolt?)

Thanks
author: martymcfly1

comments.body:
On macOS they're in `~/.exo/models`.
On Linux it conforms to XDG Base Directory Specification, see https://github.com/exo-explore/exo/blob/main/src/exo/shared/constants.py

There's currently no way to change the model dir if using the macOS app (issue for that here: https://github.com/exo-explore/exo/issues/1009).
However, if you're running from source, then you can set the `EXO_MODELS_DIR` environment variable.

---

Would it be useful to have this in the UI so you can delete directly from the dashboard? See https://github.com/exo-explore/exo/issues/1010 and thumbs it up if that's useful.
Thanks Alex.  Both excellent suggestions.
This issue is now represented in #1008, #1009 and #1010 so I'm closing it. We could also add a section to the readme to specify ~/.exo/models or ~/.local/share/exo/models as the defaults.

下面是我的dpo训练代码：
import os
import sys
__package__ = "trainer"
sys.path.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), '..')))

import argparse
import time
import math
import warnings
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import torch.distributed as dist
from contextlib import nullcontext
from torch import optim
from torch.nn.parallel import DistributedDataParallel
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, DistributedSampler
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM
from model.model_minimind import MiniMindConfig, MiniMindForCausalLM
from dataset.lm_dataset import DPODataset

warnings.filterwarnings('ignore')


def Logger(content):
    if not ddp or dist.get_rank() == 0:
        print(content)


def get_lr(current_step, total_steps, lr):
    return lr / 10 + 0.5 * lr * (1 + math.cos(math.pi * current_step / total_steps))


def logits_to_probs(logits, labels):
    # logits shape: (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size)
    # labels shape: (batch_size, seq_len)
    # probs shape: (batch_size, seq_len)
    log_probs = F.log_softmax(logits, dim=2)
    probs = torch.gather(log_probs, dim=2, index=labels.unsqueeze(2)).squeeze(-1)
    return probs


def dpo_loss(ref_probs, probs, mask, beta):
    # ref_probs 和 probs 都是 shape: (batch_size, seq_len)
    # https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind/issues/298
    seq_lengths = mask.sum(dim=1, keepdim=True)  # (batch_size, 1)
    ref_probs = (ref_probs * mask).sum(dim=1) / seq_lengths.squeeze()
    probs = (probs * mask).sum(dim=1) / seq_lengths.squeeze()

    # 将 chosen 和 rejected 数据分开
    batch_size = ref_probs.shape[0]
    chosen_ref_probs = ref_probs[:batch_size // 2]
    reject_ref_probs = ref_probs[batch_size // 2:]
    chosen_probs = probs[:batch_size // 2]
    reject_probs = probs[batch_size // 2:]

    pi_logratios = chosen_probs - reject_probs
    ref_logratios = chosen_ref_probs - reject_ref_probs
    logits = pi_logratios - ref_logratios
    loss = -F.logsigmoid(beta * logits)
    return loss.mean()


def train_epoch(epoch, wandb):
    start_time = time.time()
    for step, batch in enumerate(train_loader):
        x_chosen = batch['x_chosen'].to(args.device)
        x_rejected = batch['x_rejected'].to(args.device)
        y_chosen = batch['y_chosen'].to(args.device)
        y_rejected = batch['y_rejected'].to(args.device)
        mask_chosen = batch['mask_chosen'].to(args.device)
        mask_rejected = batch['mask_rejected'].to(args.device)
        x = torch.cat([x_chosen, x_rejected], dim=0)
        y = torch.cat([y_chosen, y_rejected], dim=0)
        mask = torch.cat([mask_chosen, mask_rejected], dim=0)

        lr = get_lr(epoch * iter_per_epoch + step, args.epochs * iter_per_epoch, args.learning_rate)
        for param_group in optimizer.param_groups:
            param_group['lr'] = lr

        with ctx:
            with torch.no_grad():
                ref_outputs = ref_model(x)
                ref_logits = ref_outputs.logits
            ref_probs = logits_to_probs(ref_logits, y)
            ref_probs = ref_probs * mask
            outputs = model(x)
            logits = outputs.logits
            probs = logits_to_probs(logits, y)
            probs = probs * mask
            loss = dpo_loss(ref_probs, probs, mask, beta=0.1)
            loss = loss / args.accumulation_steps

        scaler.scale(loss).backward()

        if (step + 1) % args.accumulation_steps == 0:
            scaler.unscale_(optimizer)
            torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), args.grad_clip)
            scaler.step(optimizer)
            scaler.update()
            optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)

        if step % args.log_interval == 0:
            spend_time = time.time() - start_time
            Logger(
                'Epoch:[{}/{}]({}/{}) loss:{:.3f} lr:{:.12f} epoch_Time:{}min:'.format(
                    epoch + 1,
                    args.epochs,
                    step,
                    iter_per_epoch,
                    loss.item() * args.accumulation_steps,
                    optimizer.param_groups[-1]['lr'],
                    spend_time / (step + 1) * iter_per_epoch // 60 - spend_time // 60))

            if (wandb is not None) and (not ddp or dist.get_rank() == 0):
                wandb.log({"loss": loss * args.accumulation_steps,
                           "lr": optimizer.param_groups[-1]['lr'],
                           "epoch_Time": spend_time / (step + 1) * iter_per_epoch // 60 - spend_time // 60})

        if (step + 1) % args.save_interval == 0 and (not ddp or dist.get_rank() == 0):
            model.eval()
            moe_path = '_moe' if lm_config.use_moe else ''
            ckp = f'{args.save_dir}/rlhf_{lm_config.hidden_size}{moe_path}.pth'

            if isinstance(model, torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel):
                state_dict = model.module.state_dict()
            else:
                state_dict = model.state_dict()
            state_dict = {k: v.half() for k, v in state_dict.items()}  # 半精度保存
            torch.save(state_dict, ckp)
            model.train()


def init_model(lm_config):
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('../model/')
    model = MiniMindForCausalLM(lm_config)

title: 关于PretrainDataset读取训练数据的问题
body:
```python
class PretrainDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, data_path_lst, max_length=512, memmap=False):
        super().__init__()
        #
        if memmap:
            with open(data_path_lst[0], 'r') as f:
                nbytes = f.seek(0, 2)
                flen = f.tell() // np.dtype('uint16').itemsize
            self.data = np.memmap(data_path_lst[0], dtype=np.dtype('uint16'), shape=(flen // max_length, max_length))
        else:
            data_lst = []
            for data_path in data_path_lst:
                with open(data_path, 'rb') as f:
                    data = np.fromfile(f, dtype=np.uint16)
                    data_lst.append(data)
            data = np.concatenate(data_lst)
            data = data[:max_length * int(len(data) / max_length)]
            # np.random.shuffle(data)
            self.data = data.reshape(-1, max_length)
```
 

从代码逻辑上看，PretrainDataset读取bin数据的时候，按照512的长度作为一条数据了好像。
但是在数据存储的时候，各条数据并没有格式化成512的程度再存入bin文件中，如果按照512长度读取出来，训练数据可能没有严格按照训练数据集的条目进行划分吧。

```python

```

title: [Question]: Query Fails at exactly 23 Entity IDs in a list. What Setting To Increase Capacity?
body:
### Do you need to ask a question?

- [x] I have searched the existing question and discussions and this question is not already answered.
- [x] I believe this is a legitimate question, not just a bug or feature request.

### Your Question

Greetings all,
I am using a mix mode or local mode LightRAG query to look for orphans in the knowledge graph.

The following query works with any number of entities in the list up to 23:
The list of entities is generated by the http://localhost:9621/graph/label/list end point which is provided in the API tab of lightrag-server.

/mix [Only provide the name of the entity in the response. Nothing else is required.] Please examine the Entity ID for all Entities in the following python list. Then please return only the Entities with a Rank of 0. [ "2023-04-02T06:06:17Z", "2023-04-22T23:01:27Z", "Alabama", "Albury", "Biological Compartments", ... ]

Here is the response:

> Albury

This is correct, but if I add only one more entity to list of entities to be examined then I get the following failed response:

> I'm sorry, but I don't have the information regarding the Entity IDs or their ranks for the entities listed. Therefore, I cannot return the entities with a rank of 0.

So at the threshold of 24 items (where the query fails) I doubled the values of: Top K Results, Max Tokens for Text Unit, Max Tokens for Global Context, and Max Tokens for Local Context.
Unfortunately, I still get the same failed response.

I also tried increasing the following in the .env file but with no success.
```
entity_summary_to_max_tokens
max_token_size
chunk_token_size
```

If I put the same query into my python query script, then it will process many more list items than just 23.
I have not yet been able to determine what the limit is when using a python query script.

Can someone please tell me where the limit is specified for LightRAG Server, or how I can ask the question in a way which bypasses the limit?

Much thanks to all
author: johnshearing

comments.body:
You cannot use RAG as a tool to query a long list of data.

 RAG is suitable for answering focused questions. RAG is not designed for comprehensive data enumeration or extracting extensive lists. This is determined by how RAG works. RAG only filters a limited number of content snippets from the knowledge base and sends them to the LLM to answer questions, making it unsuitable for generating lengthy data compilations in a single query.

Thanks @danielaskdd! 
Understood.

Now that I am starting to get familiar with the LightRAG server API I can use a python script to find all the orphans.
I will incorporate this function into the [merge application](https://github.com/johnshearing/deep_avatar/tree/main/LightRAG) I have been working on with the help of various a.i.
Soon we will have something to clean up dirty data and collect training data so as to fine-tune an a.i. to do the same.

I really appreciate your help.

title: [Question]: Clarification on Chunk Processing Order and Logic After Failure
body:
### Do you need to ask a question?

- [ ] I have searched the existing question and discussions and this question is not already answered.
- [ ] I believe this is a legitimate question, not just a bug or feature request.

### Your Question

I’d like to request some clarification on how LightRAG handles chunk and document processing, particularly in scenarios involving multiple documents and recovery after failed executions.

While processing multiple documents, I observed that the script doesn’t fully process one document before moving to the next. Instead, it processes some chunks from the first document, then switches to the second, then back to the first, and so on. Is this expected behavior? Is chunk processing done in parallel across documents, or is parallel processing done document-wise?

Also In a previous run, the process failed midway and execution was stopped. . I restarted the execution and as per the logic implemented in the LIGHTRAG scripts it checks for the file status: if it is marked as failed, it should be reprocessed right? Also the chunks had already been created in the earlier run, and some chunks had already been processed for entity and relation extraction and stored in llm_cache_response, does LightRAG automatically skips those chunks, or does it process the entire document only again after failure occurs?

Thanks for building a great tool! Looking forward to your insights on this.

_No response_
author: martina0211

comments.body:
The document processing pipeline in LightRAG is somewhat complex and is divided into two primary stages: the Extraction stage (entity and relationship extraction) and the Merging stage (entity and relationship merging). There are two key parameters that control pipeline concurrency: the maximum number of files processed in parallel (MAX_PARALLEL_INSERT) and the maximum number of concurrent LLM requests (MAX_ASYNC). The workflow is described as follows:

1. MAX_PARALLEL_INSERT controls the number of files processed in parallel during the extraction stage.
2. MAX_ASYNC limits the total number of concurrent LLM requests in the system, including those for querying, extraction, and merging. LLM requests have different priorities: query operations have the highest priority, followed by merging, and then extraction.
3. Within a single file, entity and relationship extractions from different text blocks are processed concurrently, with the degree of concurrency set by MAX_ASYNC. Only after MAX_ASYNC text blocks are processed will the system proceed to the next batch within the same file.
4. The merging stage begins only after all text blocks in a file have completed entity and relationship extraction. When a file enters the merging stage, the pipeline allows the next file to begin extraction.
5. Since the extraction stage is generally faster than merging, the actual number of files being processed concurrently may exceed MAX_PARALLEL_INSERT, as this parameter only controls parallelism during the extraction stage.
6. To prevent race conditions, the merging stage does not support concurrent processing of multiple files; only one file can be merged at a time, while other files must wait in queue.
7. Each file is treated as an atomic processing unit in the pipeline. A file is marked as successfully processed only after all its text blocks have completed extraction and merging. If any error occurs during processing, the entire file is marked as failed and must be reprocessed.
8. When a file is reprocessed due to errors, previously processed text blocks can be quickly skipped thanks to LLM caching. Although LLM cache is also utilized during the merging stage, inconsistencies in merging order may limit its effectiveness in this stage.
9. If an error occurs during extraction, the system does not retain any intermediate results. If an error occurs during merging, already merged entities and relationships might be preserved; when the same file is reprocessed, re-extracted entities and relationships will be merged with the existing ones, without impacting the query results.
10. At the end of the merging stage, all entity and relationship data are updated in the vector database. Should an error occur at this point, some updates may be retained. However, the next processing attempt will overwrite previous results, ensuring that successfully reprocessed files do not affect the integrity of future query results.

Thanks a lot for the clarification—it really helped clear things up. I appreciate your support!
I just have one more question—
Even though you mentioned that inserting custom chunks is now deprecated in the script, is there still a way I can add my own chunks (with page numbers and some extra metadata) for processing?
You can use `insert` to add custom chunks instead of the deprecated function, which requires the `file_paths` parameter for compatibility.

satisfaction_conditions: Explanation of the parallel processing behavior across multiple documents and chunks
Clarification of how the system handles failed document processing and recovery
Description of the relationship between extraction and merging stages in the processing pipeline
Information about how intermediate results and cache are utilized during reprocessing
Explanation of concurrency control mechanisms and their impact on processing order
